topics.title: Reader V1 and the laboratory workflow
text: Laboratories need results that can be trusted, explained and delivered through a workable process. Manual observation can preserve valuable expert judgement, but it can also leave measurement context dispersed across images, worksheets and information systems. Automation is useful when it improves a defined part of that process without removing the evidence a reviewer needs.

pages.title: The laboratory problem AMReye.AI addresses
text: Laboratories need results that can be trusted, explained and delivered through a workable process. Manual observation can preserve valuable expert judgement, but it can also leave measurement context dispersed across images, worksheets and information systems. Automation is useful when it improves a defined part of that process without removing the evidence a reviewer needs.
## Three practical gaps

The first gap is repeatable acquisition: lighting, pose and scale can vary between images. The second is traceable interpretation: a measured quantity, the applicable standards rule and the reviewer’s decision may not be stored as separate objects. The third is continuity: an image or observation series may become difficult to retrieve after a correction, instrument change or research reanalysis.

AMReye.AI proposes a connected measurement workflow around those gaps. The wider AMR problem provides the public health motivation, but a reader’s contribution must be demonstrated through laboratory outcomes rather than inferred from global burden figures. WHO identifies AMR as a major global health challenge; that does not establish the impact of a particular device. [R06]

The initial product should earn its place by solving these bounded problems. More sensing or computing should be added when it addresses a documented residual limitation. This sequence makes the programme testable: partners can evaluate a useful measurement workflow while the more ambitious research tracks develop their own evidence.

pages.title: Antimicrobial susceptibility as a measurement problem
text: Susceptibility testing converts a biological response under specified conditions into an interpretable laboratory result. The measured signal may be a zone diameter, a growth endpoint or another method-defined quantity. Interpretation depends on the assay, organism, antimicrobial agent and applicable standards context. A visually convincing measurement can still be ineligible for interpretation.
## Separate the layers of the result

An image contains optical intensities. A measurement algorithm estimates a physical feature from those intensities. A standards engine applies eligible rules to the measured feature. A qualified reviewer considers the evidence and resolves exceptions. Combining these layers into a single opaque score makes it harder to identify the source of an error.

The proposed reader should retain the boundaries between them. For example, a changed breakpoint table can justify a new interpretation of an unchanged diameter. A corrected plate association may invalidate both the measurement context and the prior interpretation. Those changes have different meanings and should not be represented by the same generic “updated” status. [R01] [R02]

A measurement-centred design also makes conventional methods easier to compare with learned methods. The relevant question is whether a method produces a sufficiently reliable estimate under the declared conditions, including difficult and unreadable cases. Model complexity is secondary to that result.

pages.title: From specimen to reviewed laboratory result
text: The proposed record follows the laboratory’s workflow without pretending to control every upstream activity. A case or study identifier is associated with a plate, observations are acquired, measurements are made and a reviewer determines the disposition. Each transition has a responsible actor, a timestamp and a reason when the normal path is interrupted.
## Preserve meaningful states

“Captured,” “measured,” “interpreted” and “reviewed” should be distinct states. A capture can be technically successful but unreadable. A measurable zone can lack an eligible interpretation rule. A technically consistent analysis can still be rejected because the plate identity is unresolved. These are useful distinctions for both laboratory work and subsequent evaluation.
!FIG work/assets/figures/reviewed-workflow.png | Proposed workflow states. A failed transition remains visible and does not silently advance.
## Make interruption visible

When a capture fails, the absence of an image is itself a recorded event. When an export is not acknowledged, the record remains pending reconciliation. When a reviewer changes a measurement, the original estimate remains retrievable. None of these situations should silently advance the record to a completed state.

This workflow model supports clear performance measures. Acquisition success, readable coverage, review time and export reliability can be assessed separately. It also provides a stable foundation for later automation: additional hardware can produce observations within the same record structure without redefining what a reviewed result means.

pages.title: What an endpoint reader can contribute
text: An endpoint reader can improve the consistency and traceability of reading a plate that has already reached the appropriate method-defined endpoint. It can assist with image acquisition, disk localization, zone measurement, quality checks, overlay presentation and record export. Its value depends on the accuracy and usability of those functions in the intended laboratory setting.
## A bounded and useful contribution

The reader should first establish that it can measure the permitted plate types reliably. That requires controlled geometry, calibration, readable images and a clear response to ambiguous edges. The software can then help a reviewer compare an overlay with the original plate image and identify cases that need another observation or manual handling.

The approach fits a measurement workflow already governed by method-specific standards. It does not shorten the underlying biological endpoint merely by computing the diameter quickly. EUCAST distinguishes its routine disk diffusion method from its rapid AST pathway; the product should preserve that distinction in eligibility checks and claims. [R03] [R04]

An endpoint reader should also have a useful failure mode. It should identify when the available image cannot support the requested measurement, preserve the evidence and allow the laboratory to use its established alternative workflow. The aim is a reliable contribution to laboratory work, including reliable recognition of the limits of that contribution.

pages.title: Reader V1 intended development scope
text: Reader V1 is the near-term development priority: a controlled imaging and measurement workflow for endpoint disk diffusion plates, with mandatory human review. The reference configuration at the end of this book makes one candidate optical and computing arrangement concrete. It is a development configuration, not a declaration of a finished commercial enclosure or validated clinical performance.
## Proposed minimum functional scope

The first release should associate each image with the correct plate, verify acquisition readiness, preserve the original image and calibration context, estimate permitted zone measurements and support review. Standards interpretation should be independent of the image algorithm and should refuse unsupported combinations or incomplete context.
## Evidence needed to advance

Bench measurements should establish the optical measurement chain before biological agreement is evaluated. Representative plate studies should include difficult cases, independent review and prespecified handling of unreadable results. Workflow studies should then assess whether the interface helps users without encouraging inappropriate reliance on the automated estimate.

Rapid AST, MIC estimation, genomic inference and predictive twins remain separate research tracks. They may reuse selected infrastructure, but success in Reader V1 does not validate their biological conclusions. This separation keeps the initial product objective sufficiently narrow to verify while preserving the broader platform vision.

pages.title: AMReye.AI Product Technology and Research Compendium
text: An integrated view of the proposed hardware, software and services for plate observation, traceable measurement and antimicrobial susceptibility research.
**Prepared for technical partners, laboratories and controlled investor review.**

AMReye.AI develops from a practical measurement priority: an endpoint disk diffusion reader with controlled imaging, spatial calibration, quality assessment, versioned interpretation and mandatory human review. The broader programme investigates multimodal observation, laboratory automation and predictive models.

This compendium describes product intent, engineering choices and the evidence required to advance them. It does not represent a clinically validated or cleared diagnostic device. Literature findings belong to their original studies; proposed capabilities require their own evaluation.
14 September 2026
**Controlled external review edition**

pages.title: Purpose and scope of controlled review
text: This compendium presents a proposed product platform for laboratory observation, measurement and research. Its readers should be able to determine what a module is intended to do, what physical or computational principle supports it, what evidence is missing and what would have to be demonstrated before deployment.
## Scope of the review

The central development priority is Reader V1, an endpoint disk diffusion imaging and measurement system. The wider portfolio includes integrated instruments, research imaging, automation, software and services. These share recordkeeping and engineering principles, but their intended uses and evidence requirements differ. A research imaging result should not acquire a clinical meaning simply because it appears in the same interface as a laboratory record.
## Distribution and interpretation

This edition is intended for controlled external review. The product concepts, diagrams and interfaces describe engineering intent. They are not instructions for patient treatment, evidence of regulatory clearance or confirmation that every proposed module has been built. Clinical use would require an appropriate intended use, completed validation and applicable authorization.

Financial projections, fundraising scenarios and proposed selling prices are outside the book. A dated Reader V1 candidate bill of materials appears at the end to make one engineering configuration inspectable. Component prices are purchasing observations or explicitly identified estimates, not a validated cost of a finished medical device.

pages.title: The product proposition
text: AMReye.AI aims to make laboratory observations easier to acquire consistently, inspect critically and preserve with their context. The first useful unit of value is a trustworthy measurement record: an image associated with the correct plate, a valid calibration, a reproducible measurement and a review decision that can be reconstructed.
## A platform built around observation

A plate contains more information than a final diameter alone. Its appearance, temporal development and measurement conditions can support quality assessment and research. Multiple sensing methods may add complementary information, but each added channel also introduces calibration, maintenance and interpretation work. The platform therefore treats integration as a question of demonstrated information value.
## What success would look like

A successful endpoint reader would reduce avoidable measurement and transcription variability while preserving laboratory oversight. A successful research platform would produce observations that other investigators can interpret, compare and challenge. A successful deployment would remain usable when connectivity is interrupted and would make failed or uncertain results visible.

The common aim is better evidence at the point where a laboratory makes a decision. Speed, automation and AI are valuable when they improve that evidence or reduce a verified operational burden. They are not substitutes for method suitability, traceability or biological validation.

pages.title: Reading the maturity of a capability
text: Capability maturity is expressed by what has been demonstrated, not by the sophistication of its name. The same module can have a working software demonstration, an unqualified measurement chain and no clinical validation. Those are different states and should remain distinguishable.
## Read the scope with the result

A reported agreement percentage is incomplete without the tested population, comparator, denominator, excluded cases and uncertainty. A short assay time is incomplete without its clock origin. A simulation is incomplete without the last real observation and the horizon over which it predicts.

No clinical accuracy, sub-two-hour performance, resistance-gene identification from plate images or zero-error operation is established for AMReye.AI by this compendium. Those ambitions are translated into testable research and engineering requirements. The near-term product path prioritizes controlled endpoint measurement and human review; broader capabilities advance through separate evidence gates.

This vocabulary should help technical partners compare proposals fairly. It also protects useful exploratory ideas from being discarded merely because they are not ready for clinical use. Research potential and readiness for deployment are separate assessments.
tables: The physical, biological or computational principle is supported independently; its integration here still needs evaluation.

pages.title: How the platform fits laboratory work
text: A laboratory result emerges from a chain of activities. Specimen collection, transport, processing, organism identification, susceptibility testing, review and communication can each contribute delay or uncertainty. An instrument can improve a particular step without controlling the whole chain.
## Measure the contribution at the right boundary

Reader acquisition time, analysis latency and total laboratory turnaround should be reported separately. A fast image measurement cannot recover time already spent in specimen transport or biological growth. Similarly, an early research signal may not yet be a reportable susceptibility result.

The proposed software should make these boundaries visible through distinct timestamps. Where a timestamp is missing, elapsed time should be unavailable rather than inferred silently. Partners can then identify the stage that actually limits their service and assess whether a reader, workflow integration or a different assay would address it.

## Suggested reading paths

Laboratory reviewers can begin with Reader V1, routine disk diffusion, human review and measurement validation. Engineering partners can move directly to sensing, interfaces and the development sequence. Research collaborators should connect a candidate modality to its evidence synthesis, application boundary and validation plan.

Investors should read the product portfolio together with development gates and service requirements. The breadth of the platform is an opportunity map; it is not a promise that every proposed family will be delivered in one instrument or one development cycle.

topics.title: Instrument research families
text: An integrated instrument could bring controlled observation, environmental monitoring, incubation-related functions and material handling into a coordinated laboratory workstation. Its purpose would be to make a longer biological process observable and reproducible. The appropriate physical arrangement remains open and should follow the selected assays, service requirements and risk assessment.

pages.title: The integrated instrument research family
text: An integrated instrument could bring controlled observation, environmental monitoring, incubation-related functions and material handling into a coordinated laboratory workstation. Its purpose would be to make a longer biological process observable and reproducible. The appropriate physical arrangement remains open and should follow the selected assays, service requirements and risk assessment.
## Integration creates new responsibilities

Imaging a plate at one endpoint is different from maintaining conditions over time. A time-series instrument must control or measure relevant environmental variables, preserve time origins, detect interruptions and distinguish instrument faults from biological changes. Added motion or liquid handling introduces further requirements for identity, containment, cleaning and mechanical safety.
## Keep assay boundaries intact

A direct MIC method, a disk diffusion reader and a research growth model are distinct functions even if they share an instrument housing. Each needs its own eligibility rules, controls and evidence. A research atmosphere or specialized optical mode should not be enabled within a clinical workflow merely because the hardware can support it.

The development decision is therefore modular: select a useful combination, define the interfaces and demonstrate the integrated behaviour. A broad catalogue describes possibilities across the portfolio, not a requirement to install every module in one device.

pages.title: The imaging and microscopy family
text: The imaging family extends from whole-plate observation to selected microscopic or spectroscopic investigations. Different questions demand different fields of view, spatial resolution, contrast mechanisms and temporal sampling. A single camera arrangement is unlikely to provide the best measurement for every scale.
## Choose the scale from the question

Whole-plate imaging supports spatial context, zone measurements and colony distribution. Higher magnification can support cell-level or microcolony research, but reduces the area observed at one time and increases the burden of focusing, positioning and data handling. Spectral and phase-sensitive approaches may reveal information that ordinary colour images do not, while introducing their own calibration and interpretation requirements.
## Preserve context across scales

A high-magnification field should retain its position within the parent specimen or plate. A reviewer needs to know whether the field was selected manually, by a prespecified sampling pattern or by an algorithm attracted to an unusual feature. Otherwise, a striking image can be mistaken for a representative observation.

Published single-cell AST research illustrates that specialized imaging can support short assay windows in selected experimental settings. It does not show that whole-plate imaging automatically has the same timing or clinical scope. [R11] The proposed imaging family should therefore qualify each scale and workflow on its own terms, with shared provenance rather than interchangeable claims.

pages.title: The automation and robotics family
text: Automation should remove a demonstrated source of variation or workload. Candidate functions include plate loading, indexing, scheduled observation, barcode association and transfer between qualified modules. More advanced liquid handling and robotic workflows belong to separately assessed development tracks.
## Make every physical action accountable

A motion command should have a permitted starting state, a target state, feedback and a defined response when completion is uncertain. The software record should describe what the instrument observed about the action, not merely what it requested. A command to move a plate is not evidence that the plate arrived in the correct position.
## Separate safety from conversational control

Operator assistance may explain a sequence or collect an annotation, but a learned language model should not become the sole authority for safety-critical motion or environmental control. Interlocks, command authorization and deterministic limits should remain effective when the interface or cloud service fails.

The strongest early automation candidate is often the simplest one that makes a repeated operation more consistent. The development sequence should measure operator time, identity integrity, recovery burden and maintenance demand alongside mechanical cycle time. A faster mechanism that creates more ambiguous plate associations would not satisfy the product objective.

pages.title: The research instrumentation family
text: Research instrumentation should support investigators who need reproducible observations and transparent access to data. Its outputs may include raw images, calibrated measurements, temporal features and sensor traces. The value lies in the quality and interpretability of those observations, rather than in assigning a clinical category before the relevant assay has been validated.
## A configurable but bounded environment

Research configurations can expose additional optical modes, sampling schedules and analysis options. Those choices should be versioned and recorded. An investigator should be able to reconstruct the configuration that produced a dataset and distinguish an intentional experimental change from an unrecorded instrument drift.
## Protect comparability

Open access to settings is useful only when changes remain interpretable. For example, an exposure adjustment can alter image intensity without indicating a biological change. A different illumination mode can reveal another feature while breaking direct comparability with the prior series. The research interface should make these transitions explicit.

Partnerships should define who owns observations, who can reuse them, what de-identification is required and which results may be published. Research use is not a blanket exemption from privacy, biosafety or instrument safety responsibilities. A well-designed research product gives investigators the information needed to meet those responsibilities and to evaluate whether its measurements answer their question.

topics.title: PIMS, analysis and laboratory connectivity
text: Plate information management is a proposed software product in its own right. Laboratories and research groups may need reliable plate records even when their images come from different instruments. PIMS should provide a stable identity and provenance model across those acquisition sources.

pages.title: Plate information management software
text: Plate information management is a proposed software product in its own right. Laboratories and research groups may need reliable plate records even when their images come from different instruments. PIMS should provide a stable identity and provenance model across those acquisition sources.
## Product functions

The software should organize plate associations, observations, analysis versions, quality decisions and review states. Search should answer operational questions such as which records need review, which images used a superseded calibration and which exports remain unacknowledged. Retrieval should not depend on a staff member remembering a file naming convention.
## Product boundaries

PIMS should integrate with the laboratory’s authoritative patient and order systems rather than create unnecessary duplicate identity stores. The appropriate source of truth for each field must be agreed during integration. A research deployment may use study identifiers and require no patient details at all.

The initial product value can be evaluated through successful retrieval, identity consistency, correction completeness and reviewer usability. Predictive features can be added later without changing the meaning of the original observation record. The detailed PIMS chapter and interface appendices define the proposed record relationships and expected handling of measured, derived, imputed, simulated and unavailable values.

pages.title: Analysis and decision support software
text: Analysis software converts observations into candidate measurements and reviewable evidence. Decision support adds context that helps a qualified user understand the result. These functions should be distinguished from autonomous clinical decision-making and from the deterministic application of an eligible standards rule.
## A layered analysis product

The proposed software combines conventional image processing, task-specific learned models and explicit quality logic. A geometric method may be sufficient for one measurement, while a learned model may help with variable appearance or ambiguous segmentation. Every AI capability should be compared with a simpler baseline and judged by its effect on the intended workflow.
## Keep explanations operational

An explanation should identify what affected the result and what the user can do next. A coloured overlay may help locate a boundary, but it does not establish that the algorithm used a biologically valid feature. A confidence score should have a defined empirical meaning and should be evaluated on representative data. [R21] [R22]

The product should make uncertainty actionable through review, additional observation or abstention. It should also preserve a record of overrides so that developers can investigate recurring weaknesses. Human review is most useful when the interface exposes the evidence needed for independent judgement, rather than simply asking the user to confirm an automated answer.

pages.title: Laboratory connectivity products
text: Connectivity products should move laboratory information with its meaning intact. The challenge is not only transmitting a value; it is preserving identity, units, method, status, version and correction semantics across systems that may use different conventions.
## Define a mapping before an interface

Each integration needs a field-level agreement between the sending and receiving systems. The agreement should identify authoritative identifiers, required terminology, permitted result states and acknowledgement behaviour. Common messaging standards can support that agreement, but they do not remove the need for site-specific mapping and verification.
## Design for disagreement between systems

A successful network request does not prove that a result reached the correct record. The product should reconcile acknowledgements and expose unresolved exports. Duplicate submissions should be idempotent where the receiving interface supports that behaviour. When a destination cannot represent a required field, the limitation should be resolved through the approved workflow rather than by dropping the field silently.

Connectivity can be offered as adapters, supported integrations and partner interfaces. Each should carry a compatibility statement and a conformance test set. Changes in a laboratory information system, terminology dictionary or result schema should trigger a review of the integration evidence, even when the instrument’s measurement software has not changed.

topics.title: Laboratory and research services
text: Fleet services should help a laboratory understand the condition and configuration of its instruments. A useful fleet view reports calibration validity, software versions, storage health, outstanding faults and synchronization state. It should not require central access to every patient-linked image to provide those functions.

pages.title: Fleet and instrument management services
text: Fleet services should help a laboratory understand the condition and configuration of its instruments. A useful fleet view reports calibration validity, software versions, storage health, outstanding faults and synchronization state. It should not require central access to every patient-linked image to provide those functions.
## A proposed service model

Routine telemetry should contain the minimum information needed for instrument support. A service operator may need a fault code, configuration identifier and diagnostic trace, while the laboratory retains control of clinical records. Access to a specific image for troubleshooting should be a separate, authorized action with an audit trail.

The service can coordinate signed software packages, staged updates and rollback. Instruments in the middle of a run should retain their active qualified configuration. A fleet update should not create a mixture of rules or models within one result record.
## Contract the responsibilities

The laboratory, instrument provider and hosting provider should agree who can authorize remote actions, who responds to alerts and how incidents are escalated. Service availability targets should be negotiated against the deployment context and demonstrated operating data. This compendium does not assign a contractual uptime promise.

A fleet service becomes valuable when it reduces uncertainty about instrument readiness and recovery. A dashboard full of nominally green indicators is inadequate if it cannot reveal stale telemetry, failed checks or a disconnected instrument.

pages.title: Calibration and measurement services
text: Calibration services connect instrument output to a defined measurement basis. For an imaging reader, the central task is spatial calibration at the relevant object plane, supported by checks of field dependence, stability and configuration control. Other sensing configurations require their own reference materials, transfer functions and uncertainty budgets.
## Deliver a usable calibration record

A service report should identify the instrument and configuration, the reference used, the measured residuals, the permitted operating range and the conditions that invalidate the calibration. A coefficient file without this context is insufficient for laboratory review or later investigation.

The proposed service should also distinguish calibration from adjustment. Calibration characterizes a relationship; adjustment changes the instrument. After an adjustment, the resulting measurement performance needs to be established again. Routine checks can detect departure from an accepted state, but they should not be labelled a full calibration unless they fulfil that function. [R16]
## Make serviceability a design input

Reference targets need accessible placement, stable mounting and protection from damage. The instrument should allow a service engineer to verify the measurement plane without dismantling unrelated assemblies. Calibration effort, required expertise and replacement logistics should therefore influence the design early, rather than being treated as an after-sales detail.

pages.title: Maintenance and repair services
text: Maintenance services preserve a qualified operating state and restore it after faults. They include inspection, cleaning-compatible component care, replacement, software recovery and requalification where a change can affect measurement. The scope should be specific to the instrument configuration and the laboratory’s use conditions.
## Classify the intervention by its effect

A replacement storage device may affect data integrity and recovery. A replacement light source may affect exposure, spectral response and contrast. A camera or lens change can alter the spatial measurement chain. These interventions should not share a generic “service complete” test.
## Support recovery at the laboratory

The service offer should define how users report a fault, what information is collected, when remote diagnosis is permitted and when a physical intervention is required. Spare-part planning should consider lead time, interchangeability and the evidence needed after substitution. A replacement that fits mechanically may still change the measurement behaviour.

Maintenance records should link to instrument configuration history so that later analysis can identify observations acquired before and after a change. This also supports investigation of recurring faults. The measure of a successful service is restoration of a verified, usable function with its records intact, not simply replacement of the component that first appeared suspicious.

Stable operation under the declared load and fault monitoring.

pages.title: Training and competency services
text: Training should enable users to recognize valid operation, uncertain evidence and situations requiring an alternative workflow. It should develop the ability to challenge the software when appropriate. Familiarity with the interface alone is not evidence of measurement or review competency.
## Build training around realistic decisions

A proposed training programme should include plate identity resolution, capture readiness, calibration status, overlay inspection, correction, rejection and export reconciliation. Difficult examples should be included deliberately: glare, unclear edges, incomplete context and disagreement between the visible image and the automated estimate.

Competency evaluation should ask users to make decisions on cases they have not already memorized. The evaluation should preserve the distinction between learning the interface and demonstrating the judgement required for the laboratory’s intended role.
## Keep training current

A substantial change in overlays, quality flags, rules interpretation or export behaviour may require targeted retraining. The change should be assessed for its effect on user decisions rather than simply whether a button moved. Training records should identify the product version and the relevant tasks.

The service can include guided demonstrations, practice cases, assessed exercises and refresher material. Claims that training reduces errors or review time should be supported by evaluation, including whether users become excessively trusting of the automated output. Human review works only when the human has the information, time and competence to perform it.

pages.title: Research and data partnership services
text: Research support services can help partners turn a broad idea into a reproducible investigation. The useful deliverable is a defined question, a suitable observation plan, a provenance-preserving dataset and an analysis that distinguishes evidence from interpretation. Scientific conclusions remain the responsibility of the investigators and their review process.
## Proposed support functions

AMReye.AI could support instrument configuration, acquisition metadata, annotation workflows, data quality review, interface development and reproducible analysis packaging. Partners may also need help comparing candidate sensing approaches against a conventional baseline before committing to a larger study.
## Agree the evidence and rights in advance

Data-sharing terms should address permitted reuse, confidentiality, publication review, attribution and handling of derived models. A partner’s access to an instrument should not imply permission to reuse identifiable records for unrelated model training. Similarly, a promising preliminary result should not become a public product claim before the relevant evidence review.

Research support should be evaluated by reproducibility and usefulness: whether another analyst can understand the dataset, reconstruct the processing and identify the limits of the conclusion. A large volume of generated analysis is not a substitute for an answer to the original research question. The service should make uncertainty explicit enough to guide the next experiment or engineering decision.
tables: A bounded hypothesis and a measurable outcome.

topics.title: Partner perspectives and portfolio development
text: The operator-facing experience should make the state of the plate and the state of the analysis immediately understandable. BAHU, the proposed Bio-Automation and Human User Interface concept, brings together acquisition, review and instrument orchestration while preserving the distinct responsibilities of each function.

pages.title: The laboratory user experience
text: The operator-facing experience should make the state of the plate and the state of the analysis immediately understandable. BAHU, the proposed Bio-Automation and Human User Interface concept, brings together acquisition, review and instrument orchestration while preserving the distinct responsibilities of each function.
## Organize the interface around decisions

Before capture, the user needs identity and readiness information. During review, the user needs the original image, the measurement overlay, quality findings and the relevant interpretation context. After release, the user needs export status and a reliable way to issue or inspect a correction.

An interface should display “unavailable” differently from zero, “simulated” differently from observed and “pending review” differently from approved. These distinctions should appear in text as well as colour so that the workflow remains understandable under varied displays and accessibility needs.
## Assistance without hidden authority

Voice annotation, touchless controls, mobile monitoring and augmented overlays are proposed interaction options. Their usefulness depends on the environment and on whether they reduce or increase distraction. Voice transcription should be reviewable before becoming part of a released record. A remote screen should not imply permission to control local hardware. An augmented overlay should retain registration and visibility checks.

The design should be evaluated with representative users performing realistic tasks. A visually attractive interface can still mislead if it conceals uncertainty, gives excessive prominence to an automated category or makes rejection harder than acceptance.

pages.title: The technical partner proposition
text: Technical partners need a clear account of the component they are being asked to develop, integrate or evaluate. The partnership proposition should define the interface, the operating conditions, the evidence expected and the responsibilities on either side. Broad platform language is insufficient for an engineering agreement.
## Make the contribution inspectable

An optics partner may contribute a qualified imaging path and calibration method. An electronics partner may contribute a power and control assembly with verified fault behaviour. A software partner may contribute an adapter with a conformance suite. A laboratory partner may evaluate a defined workflow using an agreed comparator and review process.
## Share interfaces before fixing form

The physical product remains malleable. Interfaces can nevertheless specify coordinate frames, timestamps, electrical limits, data types and quality states. This allows alternative layouts to be compared without losing the ability to assess their behaviour.

Partners should also agree how design changes are reviewed and how a supplied component’s evidence transfers to the integrated product. A component test can support an argument about the system, but it does not automatically establish system performance. A productive partnership makes that integration gap visible and assigns responsibility for closing it.

pages.title: The responsible investment proposition
text: A responsible investment review should examine whether the programme is converting uncertainty into evidence in a sensible order. The breadth of the proposed platform is relevant, but it should be assessed alongside the narrower product path that can be built, evaluated and supported first.
## Review the evidence behind the opportunity

For Reader V1, the essential questions concern measurement performance, laboratory usability, integration and serviceability. For an integrated instrument, the review expands to environmental control, handling, assay boundaries and production complexity. For predictive twins or genomic inference, the central uncertainty includes whether the available observations support the intended biological conclusion.
## Avoid premature extrapolation

An attractive prototype demonstration is not a substitute for representative validation. An external paper does not supply product accuracy. A component BOM does not include every cost of a supported, authorized product. These distinctions make development milestones more meaningful and prevent a broad vision from obscuring the next decision.

The financial narrative is deliberately excluded from this compendium. The final BOM supports a concrete engineering discussion about one reference configuration. Investment decisions would additionally require separate, current commercial and financial diligence, based on verified commitments and an agreed product scope.

pages.title: Lab in a box as a system concept
text: “Lab in a box” describes the integration of several laboratory functions into a coordinated instrument or system. It does not mean that all laboratory responsibilities are physically contained in a small enclosure. Specimen handling, quality management, review, biosafety and reporting can still depend on the surrounding laboratory.
## Apply the term to functions

For AMReye.AI, the concept could include plate observation, selected environmental functions, scheduled capture, analysis, record management and later handling modules. The appropriate combination depends on the intended application. An endpoint reader and a research workstation may share software while needing very different hardware.
## Integration should simplify the useful workflow

Combining modules may reduce handling, but it can also couple failures. A thermal disturbance may affect optics; a software update may affect scheduling; a mechanical fault may obstruct a plate needed for review. The design should therefore expose functional boundaries and preserve safe failure behaviour even when modules share a housing.

The term is useful when it helps explain a coherent workflow. It becomes misleading if it suggests universal assay coverage, independence from laboratory expertise or readiness that has not been demonstrated. The product should be described through the functions it has qualified and the environment in which those functions remain reliable.
tables: Which signals must be acquired, at what scale and with what traceability?
Which conditions are controlled, monitored or supplied by the laboratory?

pages.title: Lab on a chip as an assay concept
text: “Lab on a chip” refers to miniaturized fluidic or analytical structures that perform selected laboratory operations. Such devices can position small samples near sensors, reduce reagent volumes or support parallel observations. Their suitability depends on the assay and on the complete path from sample preparation to interpretable output.
## Miniaturization changes the measurement problem

At small scales, surface interactions, fluidic resistance, bubbles, evaporation and cell positioning can become central sources of variation. A chip that produces a useful signal in a research study may still require substantial work on sample compatibility, manufacturing consistency, storage and operator handling.

Published microfluidic single-cell imaging and impedance studies provide examples of rapid phenotypic research approaches. Their timing and performance belong to their particular methods and tested samples. They do not establish that a conventional plate reader can provide the same result. [R11] [R38]
## A separate product track

A chip-based assay could become a complementary research or product family. It should have its own intended use, consumable specification, reader interface and validation programme. Shared PIMS records can preserve provenance across formats, but the software should not collapse chip results and disk diffusion measurements into an interchangeable quantity.

The near-term question is whether a particular miniaturized format solves a defined assay limitation better than a simpler alternative. The terminology should describe that mechanism, not function as a general promise of speed or precision.

pages.title: Portfolio dependencies and sequencing
text: The portfolio should advance through dependencies that can be tested. Shared infrastructure can reduce duplicated work, but evidence should transfer only where the relevant assumptions remain valid. A stable plate identity model may support several product families; an optical calibration for one camera arrangement usually does not.
## Proposed dependency sequence

First establish reliable acquisition, spatial calibration and record lineage. Then evaluate endpoint measurement and human review. Add laboratory interfaces and service processes around the qualified workflow. Investigate time-series capture and additional modalities when a specific research question requires them. Integrated handling, predictive models and custom hardware should follow their own feasibility evidence.
## Preserve optionality through interfaces

The platform should avoid making an early enclosure, processor or model version a permanent conceptual boundary. Stable interfaces allow alternative components to be evaluated against the same requirements. Optionality is useful when it enables a better verified design, rather than delaying all decisions indefinitely.

Portfolio reviews should ask which uncertainty the next stage resolves and which future choices it enables. A module that adds complexity without answering an important question should be deferred. This approach allows ambitious research to proceed while the first product remains focused enough to evaluate thoroughly.

pages.title: How a proposed capability becomes a product
text: A proposed capability becomes a product when its purpose, configuration, performance limits and support responsibilities are sufficiently defined and evidenced for the intended use. A functioning demonstration is an important step, but it is not the final criterion.
## A capability transition

Consider a proposed condensation detector. It begins as a hypothesis that image features can identify a condition that compromises reading. Development needs representative examples, a conventional baseline and a definition of the condition that should trigger action. Evaluation must then determine whether the detector catches relevant failures without unnecessarily rejecting useful observations. The interface must communicate the finding and support an appropriate recovery action.

The same logic applies to a sensor, an AI model or an integration adapter: define what failure means, measure performance in the intended context and make the resulting limitation operationally manageable.
## A disciplined claim boundary

The claim should describe the function and conditions actually evaluated. A detector that identifies one type of artifact does not establish universal image quality. An algorithm that performs well at one site does not establish transferability. A sensor that agrees with another sensor does not prove both are correct.

Product development therefore includes the ability to say when the function cannot support the requested decision. Explicit limitations, abstention and recovery are part of the product design, not merely qualifications added after the technology has been built.

topics.title: Measurement architecture and sensor selection
text: The proposed platform architecture should be described through functions and interfaces before it is expressed as an enclosure. Observation, environmental management, physical control, computation, review and data storage have different timing, failure and service requirements. Their separation can be logical, electrical or physical; no single compartment arrangement is prescribed here.

pages.title: Measurement architecture without a fixed enclosure
text: The proposed platform architecture should be described through functions and interfaces before it is expressed as an enclosure. Observation, environmental management, physical control, computation, review and data storage have different timing, failure and service requirements. Their separation can be logical, electrical or physical; no single compartment arrangement is prescribed here.
## Define what crosses a boundary

An imaging subsystem should provide observations with configuration, timing and quality metadata. A control subsystem should expose permitted commands and confirmed states. An analysis subsystem should return derived values linked to exact inputs. These contracts let designers compare alternative mechanical layouts and computing arrangements without changing the meaning of a record.
## Design for coupling that cannot be eliminated

Heat from computation can change an optical assembly. A fan can introduce vibration. An illumination change can alter both image contrast and sample heating. Treating modules as separate boxes in a diagram does not remove these interactions. Integration testing should identify and quantify the couplings that matter to the selected measurement.

A candidate layout should therefore be assessed against measurement quality, access for service, contamination management, power, thermal behaviour and recovery. The strongest arrangement is the one that meets the chosen requirements with evidence. It need not be the most compact, the most sensor-rich or the one containing the newest processor.

pages.title: Optical geometry and spatial calibration
text: An imaging instrument measures a physical object through an optical projection. A zone diameter expressed in pixels becomes a length only when the relationship between the image and the relevant plate plane is established. Resolution, repeatability and accuracy describe different properties; a dense pixel array cannot substitute for a calibrated measurement chain.
## Define the measurement plane

The proposed reader should reference the plane at which zone boundaries are interpreted. A ruler attached to a raised lid can have a different scale from the agar surface under perspective imaging. Calibration therefore needs a traceable target at the intended plane, a declared working range and a check for local distortion across the field. Telecentric optics are a candidate for reducing magnification changes with depth, but their benefits must be weighed against field size, working distance and integration cost. [R15]
## Carry geometry into uncertainty

For an ideal uniform scale, diameter d equals pixel span p multiplied by scale s in millimetres per pixel. A first order independent uncertainty approximation is u(d)² = s²u(p)² + p²u(s)². Correlated terms must be included when the same images or reference features influence both quantities. This approximation does not cover all lens distortion or ambiguous biological edges. [R16]

The acceptance decision should use a measurement uncertainty budget and independent target checks. A successful camera self-test establishes instrument readiness; biological agreement still requires a separate study against the appropriate reference workflow.

pages.title: Illumination and image formation
text: Illumination is part of the measurement chain. A plate image records the combined effects of the light source, optical path, specimen, lens, sensor and processing pipeline. Changes in any of these can alter apparent contrast even when the underlying biological object is unchanged.
## Control the useful dimensions of light

The proposed reader should qualify source geometry, intensity stability, spectral content and spatial uniformity. Reflected and transmitted light can answer different questions. Oblique illumination may reveal texture while making a boundary appear different from its appearance under a standard reading geometry. A multimode acquisition should therefore identify the mode in each observation rather than merge images without provenance.
## Preserve linearity where it matters

Automatic enhancement, tone mapping and local contrast processing can improve appearance while changing quantitative relationships. A measurement pipeline should declare which processing stages are permitted and retain enough original data to investigate their effect. Camera characterization methods can help quantify noise, response and dynamic range, but the complete illuminated object still requires application-specific evaluation. [R14]

The preferred illumination arrangement should be selected through comparisons on representative non-biological targets and appropriate plate images. Evaluate not only whether a feature becomes more visible, but whether the resulting measurement remains stable across location, exposure and the permitted range of plate appearance.

Exposure timing can interact with flicker and create variable intensities.

pages.title: Environmental and mechanical stability
text: Mechanical and environmental stability determine whether an instrument can reproduce its measurement geometry over time. A stable image requires more than a rigid camera mount: the plate support, focus mechanism, lighting fixture and surrounding thermal conditions can all affect the acquired signal.
## Identify slow and fast disturbances

Slow drift may follow temperature changes, material relaxation or repeated loading. Fast disturbances may arise from fans, motion stages, nearby equipment or contact with the bench. Their signatures differ, so the instrument should not rely on a single generic stability indicator.
## Qualify the assembled instrument

Component specifications do not fully describe the behaviour of the assembly. A low-noise camera mounted on a vibrating structure can still produce unreliable images. A stable temperature sensor at one location does not prove uniform conditions throughout a chamber.

The engineering programme should measure the relationship between disturbances and the quantities that matter to the workflow. If a disturbance has no material effect within the accepted range, it may need only monitoring. If it can invalidate measurement, the response should be explicit: prevent capture, flag affected observations or require requalification. The decision should follow measured sensitivity rather than the mere presence of a sensor.
tables: Verify pose against the permitted geometry and assess scale sensitivity.
Track image quality on a stable reference and control adjustment history.
Compare inertial or image-based evidence with blur and motion artifacts.
Characterize measurement residuals across the intended ambient range.

Separate electronics cooling requirements from the observation environment.

pages.title: Timing synchronization and acquisition control
text: Time is an essential coordinate in any repeated observation system. The instrument must distinguish the biological event used as a time origin, the start and end of an exposure, the arrival of data and the completion of analysis. These timestamps can differ substantially and should not be collapsed into one “result time.”
## Synchronize the events that need comparison

For multimodal analysis, each observation should identify the interval over which it was measured. A gas sensor may average over seconds while a camera integrates light over milliseconds. Assigning both the same timestamp can create a false impression of simultaneity. Where sensor clocks differ, the synchronization method and estimated timing uncertainty should be recorded.
## Handle clock faults explicitly

A system restart, manual clock correction or loss of synchronization can disrupt ordering. Monotonic counters can help preserve local event sequence, while UTC timestamps support comparison across systems. Both may be useful, but neither should conceal an uncertain biological start time.

Acquisition scheduling should prioritize the observations required by the selected workflow. A missed scheduled image is a missing observation, not an invitation to substitute a generated image into the measured series. Later analysis can model the gap, provided that its status and uncertainty remain explicit. Timing integrity is therefore both an engineering requirement and a condition for credible growth modelling.

pages.title: Sensor selection and information value
text: Sensor selection should begin with a question that the existing observations cannot answer adequately. The relevant comparison is the information gained after accounting for calibration, confounding, maintenance, power and integration. A sensor count is not a measure of diagnostic reliability.
## Compare incremental value

A candidate channel should be assessed against the current baseline using the same records and a prespecified outcome. If it improves a model only because it identifies the acquisition site or experimental batch, it may fail when deployed elsewhere. Its value should persist under tests that separate the intended biological signal from instrument and workflow context.
## Use staged experiments

Begin with instrument characterization and non-biological controls where possible. Then test the assay-specific relationship using suitable reference observations. Finally, evaluate whether the channel improves the complete decision process, including cases in which it is missing or disagrees with other inputs.

The outcome may be to select the sensor, restrict it to research, use it only for instrument quality checks or reject it. A channel that reliably detects a lighting fault may be highly valuable even if it contains no biological information. Conversely, an attractive biological correlation may not justify product integration if it cannot be calibrated or transferred reliably.
tables: Is the measured quantity plausibly connected to the intended question?
Can the channel resolve useful variation within the permitted operating conditions?
Does it add information or repeat the same failure mechanism?
Can its response be verified and maintained in the deployment setting?
Does it disturb the sample, optical path, atmosphere or operator workflow?

pages.title: Combining modalities without counting votes
text: Multiple sensors can improve observability, but they do not guarantee independent evidence. Two cameras can share the same glare, two temperature sensors can share the same poor placement and several learned models can inherit the same biased training labels. Agreement is useful only when the reasons for possible agreement are understood.
## Model disagreement as information

The proposed fusion system should preserve each channel’s quality state and uncertainty before combining outputs. A disagreement may indicate a sensor fault, timing mismatch, domain shift or a real difference between the quantities being observed. The correct response depends on which of these explanations remains plausible.

A channel that fails its own quality check should be excluded from eligible fusion while its failure record remains. Different quantities require an explicit relationship model, not numerical voting. Independent disagreement should trigger checks of timing, calibration and assumptions. Shared disturbances require common-cause tests and independent references. A missing required channel permits only a separately evaluated degraded mode; otherwise the system should decline the result.
!FIG work/assets/figures/common-cause.png | Shared disturbances can make multiple channels agree incorrectly.
## A simple uncertainty example

For two equally precise estimates with variance σ² and correlation ρ, the variance of their average is σ²(1 + ρ)/2. With zero correlation, averaging can reduce variance. With perfect positive correlation, it does not. This mathematical example concerns uncertainty in comparable estimates; it is not a diagnostic accuracy claim.

The zero-error ambition should therefore become measurable requirements for disagreement detection, fault containment, abstention and recovery. Evaluation should include failures that affect several channels together. The product should be able to explain why a combined result is eligible, which observations contributed and which conditions would invalidate the inference.

pages.title: Using the candidate technology catalogue
text: The following forty entries form a candidate technology catalogue across the platform. They are not an installed sensor list. Some entries describe biological observation methods, some monitor the environment and others assess instrument readiness or control. Several optical entries are related acquisition modes; the catalogue also spans distinct thermal, electrical, chemical, acoustic, mechanical and magnetic principles.
## Read each entry as a selection argument

Each entry identifies the measurable signal, useful question, calibration needs, confounders, integration burden and evidence boundary. A candidate can be well established for measuring a physical quantity while remaining unproven for an AMReye.AI biological application.
## Use the catalogue to narrow choices

Selection should start with the intended assay and the unresolved measurement problem. An environmental channel may help identify an invalid observation without contributing directly to a biological model. A sophisticated spectroscopic channel may require a different sample format and belong in a research instrument rather than Reader V1.

The catalogue deliberately avoids current sensor model names and component generations. The concluding BOM identifies exact candidates for one Reader V1 configuration. That configuration uses only the components needed for its defined endpoint measurement workflow and does not attempt to implement the complete catalogue.

All application proposals require suitable qualification. A literature demonstration is cited where it supports a relevant principle or research precedent; it should not be read as evidence that the proposed AMReye.AI integration has achieved the same result.

topics.title: Imaging and spectral sensing
text: **S01 · Biological observation candidate · Core imaging pathway**

pages.title: S01 Visible reflectance imaging
text: **S01 · Biological observation candidate · Core imaging pathway**

Visible reflectance imaging measures light returned from the plate, medium, disks and growth under a defined illumination geometry. A colour sensor samples spectral bands rather than measuring a complete reflectance spectrum. Exposure, illumination spectrum and image processing influence the recorded values alongside the object itself.
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is pixel intensity in digital counts. Calibrated spatial features can be expressed in millimetres, while colour or texture features require their own definitions. This pathway supports plate overview, disk localization, zone review and selected morphology research. Camera characterization can inform response and noise assessment. [R14]
## What the channel can support

The observation can support a reviewed geometrical measurement when the image and calibration are eligible. It cannot independently establish organism identity, a resistance mechanism or a quantitative MIC. Those outputs require a suitable assay or separately validated inference.

The proposed evaluation should compare measurements across plate positions, lighting drift and repeated loading. Preserve original images so that a reviewer can distinguish an algorithmic boundary error from a limitation in the acquired evidence. A failed reflectance image should remain a failed observation even if another mode later provides a usable view.
tables: Spatial target at the measurement plane; dark and uniform-field checks; colour reference when colour is analysed.
Glare, medium colour, condensation, automatic white balance, lid markings and uneven lawn appearance.
Stable optics and lighting, clean optical access, controlled focus and sufficient data storage.
Reliable contrast and spatial measurement across the intended plate domain, not maximum megapixel count.

pages.title: S02 Transmitted light imaging
text: **S02 · Biological observation candidate · Alternative optical geometry**

Transmitted-light imaging observes light that passes through the plate and its contents. Attenuation depends on absorption, scattering, thickness and optical path. It can provide contrast different from reflected light, particularly where the medium and vessel permit a useful transmission path.
## Signal and useful question

The camera records transmitted intensity in digital counts. A normalized transmission ratio is dimensionless when a suitable reference is available. The useful question is whether this geometry makes a relevant boundary or distribution more reproducible for the selected workflow. It should not be assumed to be interchangeable with the geometry specified by a standard reading method. [R03]
## Interpretation boundary

A darker region may reflect greater thickness or scattering rather than a proportional increase in biomass. Converting intensity into a biological quantity therefore requires an assay-specific calibration and a declared operating range.

A useful bench comparison would hold the object and camera geometry stable while examining how known optical disturbances affect the image. Subsequent plate evaluation should determine whether the transmitted view assists measurement or quality review. The software should retain mode identity so that a model cannot silently treat a transmitted image as a reflected one.
tables: Uniform backlight reference, dark response and spatial calibration through the complete vessel path.
Agar thickness, opaque media, bubbles, plate base curvature, labels and stray light.
Optical access below the plate, repeatable support and separation of direct from scattered light.
Measurable improvement in the intended feature without unacceptable position or medium dependence.

pages.title: S03 Oblique dark field imaging
text: **S03 · Biological observation candidate · Surface and scattering contrast**

Oblique and dark-field arrangements reduce direct light reaching the detector and emphasize light scattered by the object. They can make edges, texture and small surface features conspicuous. The resulting contrast is strongly dependent on illumination angle, collection geometry and the object’s scattering behaviour.
## Signal and useful question

The measured signal is spatial intensity in digital counts, often interpreted through normalized contrast or texture descriptors. Candidate questions include whether an unusual surface feature is present and whether a boundary remains visible when conventional illumination is ambiguous. Such images should be treated as complementary observations rather than automatically preferred measurements.
## Avoid a visibility trap

A bright feature in dark field is evidence of scattering, not proof of a colony or a resistant subpopulation. A scratch can be optically prominent while biologically irrelevant. The review workflow should retain the corresponding conventional image and the feature’s location.

Qualification should include objects that challenge specificity: clean vessel surfaces, known surface defects and representative permitted plates. If the mode changes the apparent zone boundary, the effect must be evaluated against the selected measurement definition. Its most appropriate initial role may be research annotation or artifact review rather than the sole source of a reported diameter.
tables: Fixed illumination geometry, repeatable reference texture and field uniformity assessment.
Scratches, dust, meniscus edges, lid defects, plate tilt and specular reflections.
Additional lighting positions, optical baffling and mode-specific acquisition control.
Incremental detectability with manageable false feature rates across vessel conditions.

pages.title: S04 Polarization resolved imaging
text: **S04 · Biological observation candidate · Polarization contrast**

Polarization-resolved imaging changes or measures the orientation state of light. Polarizers can suppress some specular reflections, while polarization-dependent signals may reveal optical structure. The benefit depends on the source, object, vessel and geometry; cross-polarization does not remove every reflection or scattering artifact.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include intensity at declared polarizer angles and dimensionless polarization contrast. More complete measurements can estimate polarization state under a calibrated instrument model. The near-term question is whether the approach improves readability or artifact discrimination for a specified plate and lid material.
## Preserve the comparison

The same region should be examined with and without the polarization arrangement so that a gain in readability can be distinguished from a change in appearance. A detector trained on one vessel material may learn its polarization artifacts and fail on another.

This candidate should begin as an optical quality improvement investigation. It is not a direct measurement of antimicrobial response. If selected, the configuration and angle state belong in the capture record, and any calibration affected by the added optics must be requalified. A nominally sharper image is insufficient evidence unless the intended measurement becomes more reliable.
tables: Polarizer orientation, extinction behaviour, illumination stability and channel registration.
Stress birefringence in plastics, depolarizing scattering, scratches, angle changes and reduced light throughput.
Additional optical elements, repeatable rotation or channel switching, exposure compensation.
Better usable-image coverage without biasing the feature being measured.

pages.title: S05 Near infrared imaging
text: **S05 · Biological observation candidate · Experimental spectral mode**

Near-infrared imaging uses wavelengths beyond the main visible band, with a compatible detector and optical path. Absorption and scattering can differ from visible-light behaviour, so a feature may gain or lose contrast. Those differences do not imply that near-infrared light will reliably see through condensation or every plate material.
## Signal and useful question

The recorded signal is wavelength-band-dependent image intensity. Spatial measurements remain in millimetres only after suitable calibration. The relevant research question is whether a defined near-infrared mode improves usable observation under particular media, lids or condensation conditions.
## Test the claim directly

The evaluation should preserve paired visible and near-infrared observations and independently assess the disturbance being addressed. Improved appearance in a few images is insufficient to establish a general “fog vision” capability. The comparison should include failure cases in which the added mode makes an edge less visible or creates misleading contrast.

Near-infrared imaging remains a proposed research pathway. It should not supply a biological ground truth or replace a missing standard observation automatically. The software should identify the spectral mode and require a separately qualified analysis route before using it for a reported measurement.
tables: Spectral response, source stability, dark response, focus and spatial calibration in the selected band.
Water absorption, vessel transmission, focus shift, detector sensitivity and differences in medium contrast.
Compatible illumination, optics and filtering; assessment of optical exposure and heating.
Verified improvement over visible controls across the declared disturbance range.

pages.title: S06 Ultraviolet excited autofluorescence
text: **S06 · Biological observation candidate · Fluorescence research**

Ultraviolet-excited autofluorescence observes light emitted after endogenous materials absorb excitation energy. The emitted signal can reflect several molecular and environmental contributions. The measured fluorescence is not a unique identifier of an organism or resistance state without an appropriately validated assay and analysis.
## Signal and useful question

The detector measures emission intensity within declared wavelength bands, usually in counts or normalized relative units unless radiometrically calibrated. Candidate questions concern whether a reproducible fluorescence contrast exists and whether it adds information beyond ordinary imaging in a defined research workflow.
## Treat the exposure as part of the experiment

Excitation can affect the specimen as well as reveal it. The research design should assess whether repeated observation changes the process being measured. The acquisition record should therefore retain exposure conditions and sequence history.

Initial use should focus on optical characterization and bounded research questions. Fluorescent reporters or added probes would constitute separate assay choices with their own validation and handling requirements. The product should not imply that a general fluorescence channel provides direct susceptibility, species identification or a clinically meaningful metabolic measurement merely because it produces a distinctive image.
tables: Excitation intensity, emission filters, detector response, background and reference fluorescence stability.
Medium fluorescence, vessel fluorescence, photobleaching, exposure history and spectral overlap.
Filtered optical paths, excitation containment, suitable materials and exposure assessment.
Reproducible signal separation with a credible control for non-biological background.

pages.title: S07 Fluorescence lifetime sensing
text: **S07 · Biological observation candidate · Time-resolved fluorescence research**

Fluorescence lifetime sensing measures the temporal decay of emission after excitation rather than relying only on brightness. A decay parameter can be influenced by the molecular environment and by mixtures of emitting species. The instrument response and analysis model are essential parts of the measurement. [R56]
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include photon arrival distributions, phase shifts or fitted decay times, commonly expressed in nanoseconds for relevant fluorophores. The proposed question is whether a stable time-resolved feature provides useful research information that intensity alone cannot supply.
## Do not overinterpret a fitted lifetime

A single fitted number can conceal a mixture of signals or an inadequate decay model. The research record should retain fitting assumptions, residuals and uncertainty. Comparisons across instruments require evidence that their timing responses and analysis methods produce comparable quantities.

This is an exploratory platform candidate, not a Reader V1 requirement. Its biological interpretation would need assay-specific studies and suitable controls. A technically successful lifetime measurement establishes that a temporal optical signal was measured; it does not establish that the signal identifies a pathogen, resistance mechanism or antimicrobial response. Selection should depend on a research question sufficiently important to justify the added optical and computational burden.
tables: Timing response, reference lifetime material, background and detector temporal behaviour.
Mixed emitters, low photon counts, scattering, photobleaching and model-dependent fitting.
Pulsed or modulated excitation, suitable detection, timing electronics and substantial analysis complexity.
Identifiable and reproducible decay parameters with an incremental benefit over simpler fluorescence measurements.

pages.title: S08 Multispectral imaging
text: **S08 · Biological observation candidate · Selected spectral bands**

Multispectral imaging records a limited set of spectral bands chosen for a particular measurement question. The bands may be acquired sequentially or through parallel optical paths. Unlike a colour photograph, the acquisition can be designed around specific spectral regions, but its usefulness still depends on the sample, illumination and detector response. [R55]
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is an image stack indexed by band, with calibrated or normalized intensity values. Ratios between bands are dimensionless but remain sensitive to how their signals were acquired. Candidate questions include whether spectral contrast improves artifact discrimination or characterizes a reproducible research phenotype.
## Select bands through evidence

Adding bands increases the number of possible correlations a model can learn. A band that appears predictive within one batch may encode lighting or medium differences. Selection should therefore be evaluated under site, batch and time separation, with a conventional baseline and an ablation analysis.

The resulting image stack is a richer observation, not a direct biological conclusion. The capture record should identify all band settings and mark incomplete stacks explicitly. If a required band fails, the system should use a separately evaluated reduced-band route or decline the inference rather than silently synthesize the missing measurement.
tables: Band transmission, source spectrum, flat-field response and spatial registration.
Motion between bands, exposure differences, spectral leakage, medium variation and detector drift.
Filters or multiple sources, synchronized switching, more data and a band-aware analysis pipeline.
Each retained band adds reproducible information on held-out observations.

pages.title: S09 Hyperspectral imaging
text: **S09 · Biological observation candidate · Spectral research**

Hyperspectral imaging samples a densely resolved spectral dimension together with spatial information. The result is a data cube whose coordinates describe position and wavelength. Acquisition may involve spatial or spectral scanning, so the cube may represent a sequence of observations rather than one instantaneous view. [R55]
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is intensity or calibrated reflectance as a function of wavelength and position. Spectral features can be described through band ratios, absorption features or learned representations. The research question is whether these features explain variation that a smaller set of selected bands cannot capture reliably.
## Control dimensionality and leakage

Many correlated spectral channels can make a small dataset appear highly separable. Model evaluation should therefore separate sites, batches and acquisition sessions, and feature selection must occur within the training process. A spectrum from one region should not be allowed to reveal the identity of the same plate in a test set.

Hyperspectral observation is an exploratory research option. A useful result could be a justified reduction to a few robust bands rather than a permanent requirement for a full spectral instrument. Biological interpretation and any susceptibility claim would need independent assay-specific evidence; a visually distinctive spectral map is not sufficient.
tables: Wavelength accuracy, spectral response, dark reference, spatial registration and illumination reference.
Spectral mixing, sample movement, stray light, medium composition and preprocessing choices.
Specialized optics, longer or more complex acquisition, large datasets and spectral quality control.
Reproducible incremental information relative to multispectral and ordinary imaging baselines.

pages.title: S10 Raman spectroscopy
text: **S10 · Biological observation candidate · Vibrational spectroscopy**

Raman spectroscopy measures inelastically scattered light whose frequency shift relates to molecular vibrational behaviour. Biological spectra can contain overlapping contributions from many constituents. The measured fingerprint depends on the optical system, sample state and background, as well as on biological composition.
## Signal and useful question

The output is intensity against Raman shift, conventionally expressed in inverse centimetres.
