Candidate research questions include whether spectra provide reproducible phenotypic information and whether an assay-specific response can be detected. Published work has investigated Raman observations with machine learning for microbial identification and susceptibility research; its results do not validate this proposed integration. [R44]
## Preserve what was actually measured

A spectrum taken from a selected microscopic region does not automatically represent the whole plate. The record should retain sampling location, selection method and any preparation required. A model should not report a measured gene merely because a spectral pattern correlates with a genotype in its training set.

This candidate belongs to a dedicated research track. The first decision is whether the intended question requires molecularly sensitive information and whether Raman provides it more usefully than a simpler method. Assay transfer, representative sampling and independent validation are likely to matter as much as spectral resolution.
tables: Wavenumber reference, spectral response, optical alignment and background characterization.
Fluorescence, substrate signal, medium residues, sample heterogeneity and laser-induced changes.
Spectrometer, stable excitation, optical containment, sensitive detection and often local sampling.
Reproducible biological information after controlling substrate and acquisition effects.

topics.title: Optical, thermal and impedance sensing
text: **S11 · Biological observation candidate · Infrared spectroscopy**

pages.title: S11 Infrared absorption spectroscopy
text: **S11 · Biological observation candidate · Infrared spectroscopy**

Infrared absorption spectroscopy measures wavelength-dependent attenuation associated with molecular vibrations. A spectrum can reveal chemical composition and changes in a sample, but the optical path and measurement format strongly influence the signal. Water and substrate contributions can dominate biologically interesting features.
## Signal and useful question

The output is absorbance or transmittance against wavenumber, commonly in inverse centimetres. Candidate questions concern whether a reproducible chemical pattern can be measured in a permitted sample format and whether it relates to a defined research phenotype. It should not be assumed that an ordinary closed culture plate offers a suitable infrared transmission path.
## Keep assay format explicit

Transmission, reflection and attenuated-total-reflection arrangements do not produce interchangeable observations. A contact measurement can require a different handling workflow from non-contact plate imaging. The product description should identify that difference before discussing automation or throughput.

Infrared spectroscopy is an exploratory candidate across the broader platform. The proposed qualification should compare repeated observations of reference materials and then assess the chosen biological question with appropriate controls. A classifier’s apparent accuracy should be challenged for dependence on medium, preparation batch or instrument background. No clinical identity or susceptibility function is established by including this modality in the catalogue.
tables: Wavenumber accuracy, background spectrum, optical path and instrument response.
Water absorption, vessel material, sample thickness, contact pressure and baseline correction.
Suitable infrared optics and detector; potentially a separate sample interface or preparation route.
Stable spectral information that survives realistic sample and instrument variation.

pages.title: S12 Optical coherence tomography
text: **S12 · Biological observation candidate · Depth-resolved optical research**

Optical coherence tomography uses interferometric information to resolve optical path differences within a sample. It can produce depth profiles and cross-sectional representations of scattering structures. The relationship between optical path length and physical depth depends on refractive properties and the reconstruction model. [R57]
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include depth-dependent backscatter and reconstructed structural coordinates, with depth expressed in micrometres or millimetres under declared assumptions. Research questions could concern surface structure, thickness or subsurface morphology that a two-dimensional plate image cannot resolve.
## Distinguish structure from biological meaning

A reconstructed surface is a model-dependent measurement, not a direct resistance result. Features may arise from the medium or vessel rather than the growth being studied. The observation should therefore remain linked to a conventional overview and to the region selected for depth imaging.

This modality is a future research option, not a requirement for endpoint Reader V1. A development study should begin with known structural references and evaluate how vessel and medium effects alter reconstruction. Only then should it assess the intended biological application and the additional value relative to simpler focus, stereo or surface-imaging methods.
tables: Axial and lateral scales, reference surfaces, sensitivity range and reconstruction settings.
Multiple scattering, refractive-index variation, vessel reflections, shadowing and motion.
Interferometric optics, scanning or specialized detection, stable alignment and substantial data processing.
Depth information that is accurate enough and relevant enough to justify the added system complexity.

pages.title: S13 Quantitative phase imaging
text: **S13 · Biological observation candidate · Quantitative optical phase**

Quantitative phase imaging estimates changes in the phase of transmitted light caused by optical path differences. For a suitable sample, the signal relates to both thickness and refractive-index variation. Separating those contributions or converting them into another biological quantity requires additional assumptions and calibration.
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is phase in radians or optical path difference in length units. Candidate research questions include cell or microcolony growth, morphology and temporal changes that produce weak intensity contrast. Dry-mass estimates, where scientifically justified, are derived quantities rather than direct balance measurements.
## Respect the sample geometry

A method suitable for thin cells in a controlled optical path may not transfer to a thick, scattering agar plate. The proposed platform should treat cell-level phase research as a separate acquisition route with its own sample and field-selection records.

The evaluation should distinguish numerical reconstruction error from uncertainty in the biological interpretation. A phase map may be repeatable while an inferred mass is biased by an incorrect refractive increment. This candidate should be selected only where its assumptions can be tested and where the resulting measurement answers a question that ordinary intensity imaging cannot address adequately.
tables: Phase or path-length reference, background correction, spatial scale and reconstruction verification.
Phase wrapping, multiple scattering, refractive-index changes, drift and overlapping structures.
Interferometric or computational phase optics, stable illumination and a suitable thin-sample geometry.
Reproducible phase information with a defensible link to the intended research quantity.

pages.title: S14 Laser speckle activity sensing
text: **S14 · Biological observation candidate · Dynamic scattering research**

Laser speckle imaging records interference patterns produced when coherent light is scattered. Temporal changes in those patterns can reflect movement or other changes in the scattering scene. They can also arise from vibration, source instability or optical-path changes unrelated to biology.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include speckle contrast, correlation decay and other dimensionless temporal descriptors. Published plate-related studies have investigated speckle observations for early antibacterial-effect research. These are method-specific precedents, not established AMReye.AI performance. [R42] [R43]
## Compare against an instrument-only explanation

An early change in a speckle statistic should be challenged with controls that can reveal non-biological motion. The analysis should also preserve the relationship between exposure duration, sampling interval and the reported temporal feature.

This is an exploratory sensing pathway. Its first product contribution might be an additional research observation rather than an early clinical category. Any future susceptibility inference would need a defined clock origin, organism and drug scope, comparator and treatment of unreadable or inconsistent cases. A shorter detection window in an external study cannot be transferred to a different optical assembly by analogy alone.
tables: Stable scattering references, exposure timing, optical alignment and instrument-motion characterization.
Vibration, evaporation, thermal drift, motion of the vessel and changes in illumination coherence.
Coherent source, optical containment, mechanically stable acquisition and time-series analysis.
A biological signal that remains distinguishable from instrument and environmental dynamics.

pages.title: S15 Elastic light scattering
text: **S15 · Biological observation candidate · Angular scattering**

Elastic light scattering measures light redirected by an object without a change in photon frequency. The angular and intensity distribution depends on size, shape, refractive properties and the measurement geometry. In a heterogeneous biological sample, several structures can contribute to the same pattern.
## Signal and useful question

The instrument may record intensity against angle or a two-dimensional scattering pattern. Normalized descriptors are generally dimensionless; absolute intensity requires a calibrated optical response. Candidate questions concern whether a stable pattern can characterize a sample or flag a change that deserves further observation.
## Avoid one-to-one biological assumptions

A scattering pattern is not uniquely determined by organism identity or susceptibility. Different combinations of shape, concentration and refractive properties can produce similar observations. A learned classifier may exploit stable laboratory artifacts rather than the desired biological variation.

The proposed evaluation should include repeated measurements after repositioning and across permitted sample containers. Where a biological inference is investigated, it should be compared with a suitable reference and tested outside the acquisition batches used for development. The initial role is research characterization; a direct clinical conclusion would require substantially more evidence than pattern separation on a small dataset.
tables: Angular geometry, source stability, detector response and reference scattering objects.
Vessel curvature, multiple scattering, sample concentration, alignment and stray reflections.
Controlled source-detector geometry, baffling and a reproducible sample presentation.
Pattern stability and useful discrimination after vessel and concentration effects are controlled.

pages.title: S16 Nephelometric turbidity sensing
text: **S16 · Preparation quality candidate · Nephelometric measurement**

Nephelometry measures light scattered by suspended material at a defined observation geometry. It can support a turbidity comparison used in inoculum preparation workflows. Its output depends on particle properties and instrument geometry, so it should not be treated as a universal cell counter.
## Signal and useful question

The output may be an instrument response, a calibrated turbidity unit or a comparison with an applicable McFarland reference. The useful question is whether the preparation falls within the method’s permitted turbidity condition. A McFarland value and a viable count in CFU per millilitre are not interchangeable measurements.
## Keep preparation QC distinct from final AST

A preparation check can reduce one source of assay variation, but it does not establish that the rest of the assay was performed correctly. The record should retain the turbidity observation, its reference basis and any action taken, rather than storing only a generic “QC passed” flag.

An integrated nephelometric pathway is a proposed module. It should be evaluated independently and then as part of the selected laboratory workflow. If an organism or sample type produces an atypical optical relationship, the system should preserve the limitation rather than convert the response into an unsupported precise viable-cell concentration. [R03]
tables: Appropriate turbidity references, vessel path, detector response and repeatability checks.
Cell size, clumping, non-cell particles, bubbles, tube scratches and settling.
Defined sample holder, optical geometry, cleanable surfaces and preparation-record linkage.
Reliable method-relevant comparison across the permitted sample and vessel range.

pages.title: S17 Absorbance and optical density
text: **S17 · Biological observation candidate · Optical attenuation**

Absorbance-related measurements compare incident and transmitted light. A common expression is A = −log10(I/I0), where I is the sample signal and I0 is an appropriate reference. In microbial suspensions, scattering can contribute strongly, so an optical-density reading is not necessarily a pure molecular absorbance measurement.
## Signal and useful question

The output is dimensionless absorbance or optical density at a declared wavelength and path length. Candidate uses include tracking a reproducible optical change in a research assay or checking a preparation against a qualified reference range. Converting the reading into cell concentration requires a separate sample-specific relationship.
## Define the valid range

At high attenuation, stray light and detector limits can distort the response. At low attenuation, reference noise can dominate. A growth curve should therefore identify observations outside the qualified range rather than treating every recorded number as equally informative.

This candidate is most naturally associated with a defined liquid or optical-path assay. Its interpretation should not be imported into whole-plate imaging without evidence. The platform should preserve wavelength, path and preprocessing metadata so that researchers can distinguish biological trends from differences in optical configuration.
tables: Blank reference, optical path, detector linearity and response across the intended range.
Multiple scattering, coloured media, sedimentation, bubbles, path-length variation and stray light.
Stable source and detector geometry, reproducible vessel positioning and reference management.
Useful dynamic range and repeatability under the actual sample format.

pages.title: S18 Thermal infrared radiometry
text: **S18 · Environmental and research candidate · Surface radiometry**

Thermal infrared radiometry estimates temperature-related information from emitted radiation. The estimate depends on emissivity, reflected background radiation, optical transmission and the detector calibration. A thermal camera observes an accessible radiating surface; it does not automatically measure the temperature of material hidden beneath a lid.
## Signal and useful question

Raw signals are detector responses, while calibrated outputs may be radiance or apparent surface temperature in degrees Celsius or kelvin. Candidate questions include whether there are spatial thermal gradients, whether an assembly is heating unevenly or whether a process has departed from its qualified conditions.
## Do not confuse thermal structure with metabolic heat

A warmer region can result from lighting, airflow or electronics. Demonstrating a biological heat signal requires a much more controlled heat-flow measurement than observing apparent surface temperature. The instrument should not label a thermal image a biomass or susceptibility map without an independently validated relationship.

The proposed initial use is engineering characterization and environmental research. A thermal observation can help locate a fault or gradient, but its relationship to the plate’s relevant internal conditions must be tested. The uncertainty and emissivity assumptions should remain available to anyone interpreting the image.
tables: Traceable temperature reference, emissivity assumptions, optical path and spatial response.
Reflections, changing emissivity, vessel transmission, viewing angle and ambient background.
Appropriate infrared optics, unobstructed view and comparison with contact references.
Surface-temperature information that cannot be obtained adequately with simpler placed sensors.

pages.title: S19 Microcalorimetry
text: **S19 · Biological observation candidate · Heat-flow research**

Microcalorimetry measures small heat flows associated with physical, chemical or biological processes. In a controlled assay, changes in heat production can provide a time-resolved signal. The measured heat is the sum of relevant processes in the measurement volume and is not inherently specific to microbial growth.
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is thermal power, typically expressed in watts at an appropriate scale, and its time integral is energy in joules. Published work has investigated isothermal microcalorimetry for antimicrobial susceptibility research in defined sample contexts. [R45]
## Preserve the distinction from temperature sensing

A temperature sensor measures a local thermal state. A calorimeter estimates heat flow through a calibrated thermal relationship. Adding several temperature sensors does not automatically create a qualified calorimeter.

This candidate belongs to a dedicated research instrument or assay track. The first evaluation should establish baseline and response behaviour before asking a biological question. Any future susceptibility result would require a method-specific interpretation and comparison with a suitable reference. The cumulative heat curve should remain linked to its raw baseline, model assumptions and actual observation intervals, particularly when a run is interrupted.
tables: Electrical or other suitable heat reference, baseline stability and thermal response time.
Environmental drift, equilibration, chemical reactions, vessel differences and changing heat transfer.
Strong thermal control, sensitive differential measurement and a carefully defined sample interface.
A reproducible assay signal with acceptable detection time and baseline uncertainty.

pages.title: S20 Electrical impedance spectroscopy
text: **S20 · Biological observation candidate · Frequency-dependent electrical response**

Electrical impedance spectroscopy measures the relationship between an applied alternating signal and the resulting electrical response across frequency. Resistance, capacitance and interfacial effects can contribute to the complex impedance. In biological systems, the measured response may involve cells, medium, electrodes and geometry simultaneously.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include impedance magnitude in ohms, phase in degrees or radians, and fitted model parameters. Published AST research has used several electrical measurement formats with different response mechanisms and timing constraints. Their results should be interpreted within those specific assays. [R38] [R40] [R41]
## Explain the fitted circuit

Equivalent-circuit parameters are model-based estimates. Different circuits may fit similar data, so a numerical fit should not be assigned a biological meaning without supporting evidence. Retain the measured spectrum, fitting range, residuals and parameter uncertainty.

This is a separate assay research pathway rather than an automatic add-on to endpoint plate reading. Evaluation should compare the electrical result with an appropriate reference and assess whether the relevant antimicrobial mechanism produces a measurable response within the proposed window. Short electrical acquisition time alone is not total time to a reportable result.
tables: Open, short and suitable reference loads; frequency response; electrode and geometry characterization.
Medium conductivity, temperature, electrode polarization, fouling, bubbles and contact variation.
Analog front end, controlled electrodes or microfluidics, shielding and electrical sample compatibility.
A stable signal linked to the intended response beyond medium and electrode changes.

topics.title: Chemical, gas and acoustic sensing
text: **S21 · Chemical observation candidate · Electrochemical measurement**

pages.title: S21 Electrochemical pH sensing
text: **S21 · Chemical observation candidate · Electrochemical measurement**

Electrochemical pH sensing estimates hydrogen-ion activity through an electrode system and a reference potential. The response depends on temperature and on the condition of the sensing and reference interfaces. pH is logarithmic and dimensionless; it is not a direct measure of acid concentration in every sample.
## Signal and useful question

The instrument records an electrical potential, typically in millivolts, and converts it to pH using a qualified calibration. Candidate uses include monitoring a defined liquid research environment or identifying a chemical change that may affect an assay. The measured location must be explicit because a local probe does not describe every region of a plate.
## Interpretation boundary

A pH change can have biological or non-biological causes. Buffer capacity, gas exchange and chemical reactions can alter the relationship between biological activity and the observed value. The system should not label a pH trend as a growth rate or susceptibility result without an independently established model.

This candidate is most suitable for a dedicated research or environmental-monitoring module. Qualification should separate electrode performance from the biological hypothesis. Original voltage, temperature, calibration and derived pH should remain linked so that an investigator can evaluate whether a trend reflects the sample or a changing electrode response.
tables: Appropriate reference buffers, temperature record, response slope and offset.
Reference-junction effects, fouling, ionic composition, temperature, drift and slow equilibration.
Sample contact, cleaning or disposable interfaces, stable reference and electrical isolation.
Reliable local chemical information that matters to the chosen assay or control question.

pages.title: S22 Optical dissolved oxygen sensing
text: **S22 · Chemical and environmental candidate · Optical oxygen measurement**

Optical dissolved-oxygen sensing commonly uses oxygen-dependent quenching of a luminescent indicator. The instrument measures intensity or temporal behaviour and converts it through a calibrated relationship. The sensing element observes its local environment and can respond differently as temperature and the surrounding matrix change.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs may include luminescence phase or lifetime and derived oxygen partial pressure, concentration or percentage saturation. These quantities should not be interchanged without the required conditions and conversion model. Candidate questions include whether a defined research environment remains within its intended oxygen state.
## Link the signal to its location

An oxygen reading near a surface may differ from conditions deeper in a sample. A declining value can reflect transfer limitations as well as consumption. The research model should therefore state the sampled volume or location and distinguish observation from inferred bulk behaviour.

This is a proposed monitoring and research channel. It does not independently establish organism identity or antimicrobial susceptibility. If used in fusion, its time constant and measurement interval should accompany the value so that it is not treated as an instantaneous observation synchronized perfectly with a camera exposure.
tables: Suitable oxygen references, temperature compensation and indicator-response characterization.
Temperature, salinity or matrix effects, indicator ageing, optical background and diffusion lag.
Compatible sensing spot or probe, optical access, sample-contact assessment and local-position records.
A useful local oxygen measurement with an understood response time and maintenance burden.

pages.title: S23 Electrochemical redox potential
text: **S23 · Chemical observation candidate · Redox environment**

Oxidation-reduction potential measures an electrical potential associated with the combined electrochemical environment at a sensing electrode relative to a reference. In complex media, the value can reflect several redox couples and surface processes. It is not generally a selective measurement of one molecule or pathway.
## Signal and useful question

The primary quantity is potential in millivolts, with the reference electrode and temperature identified. A candidate use is monitoring whether a defined research environment changes in a way that merits further investigation or affects assay comparability.
## Avoid mechanistic overreach

Two samples can have similar redox potentials while differing substantially in composition or biological state. Conversely, an electrode-surface change can produce a shift without a meaningful change in the bulk sample. A model should therefore not translate the potential directly into a metabolic identity or a resistance mechanism.

The proposed evaluation should document baseline drift, response time and effects of the permitted medium range. If the channel is used as a quality indicator, define the condition it is intended to detect and the consequence of a missed or false alarm. Its strongest initial role may be contextual monitoring rather than a primary biological inference.
tables: Suitable reference solutions, reference-electrode identity and response stability checks.
Electrode fouling, dissolved gases, medium chemistry, reference drift and slow stabilization.
Contact electrode, cleanable or disposable interface and high-input-impedance measurement circuitry.
Reproducible environmental information with a defensible relationship to the selected research question.

pages.title: S24 Capacitive dielectric sensing
text: **S24 · Physical observation candidate · Dielectric response**

Capacitive dielectric sensing measures how an electric field interacts with the materials between or near electrodes. The response depends on permittivity, geometry, frequency and losses. Water content and container position can strongly influence a biological sample measurement.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include capacitance in farads at an appropriate scale, conductance and derived dielectric descriptors. Potential uses include detecting presence, monitoring a reproducible physical change or investigating whether a sample’s electrical properties contain useful research information.
## Separate presence from biology

A reliable detector of a plate or liquid level can be useful even if it provides no biological information. That engineering function should be evaluated independently from a proposed growth or composition inference. Counting the same channel as both a presence check and a biological sensor does not create two independent measurements.

This candidate requires a carefully defined operating geometry. Qualification should determine how much signal change is caused by normal placement variation before attributing a similar change to the sample. Where a derived dielectric feature is used in AI, the original measurement settings and quality state should remain available for review and reanalysis.
tables: Reference capacitors or materials, electrode geometry, frequency response and shielding.
Humidity, temperature, vessel wall thickness, position, parasitic capacitance and sample conductivity.
Stable electrodes, guarded circuitry, mechanical repeatability and a clear contact or non-contact interface.
Signal changes that remain interpretable after geometry and environmental effects are controlled.

pages.title: S25 Metal oxide gas sensing
text: **S25 · Chemical observation candidate · Broad gas-response research**

Metal-oxide gas sensors change electrical resistance in response to interactions at a heated sensing surface. Their response can depend on several gases, humidity, temperature, exposure history and the heater programme. A broad gas-response pattern is not a species-specific chemical analysis. Manufacturer documentation supports the underlying gas-sensing capability, not a microbial diagnostic claim. [R17] [R18]
## Signal and useful question

The primary output is resistance or conductance with associated operating conditions. A derived feature may summarize a response over time. The research question is whether controlled headspace observations add reproducible information after medium, cleaning agents and environmental conditions are accounted for.
## Bound the “AI nose” concept

The informal phrase describes pattern analysis of gas responses. It should not imply a measured resistance gene, a unique pathogen identity or a validated AST result. Several sensors exposed to the same uncontrolled headspace can agree for the same wrong reason.

This is a research-only biological inference candidate. A useful development outcome might instead be detection of an instrument contamination event or a changed sampling condition. The intended function should be selected from evidence rather than inferred from the sensor’s ability to produce a complex response curve.
tables: Defined reference exposures, baseline history, environmental compensation and sensor-to-sensor comparison.
Humidity, medium volatiles, carryover, cleaning chemicals, ageing and mixed gas responses.
Controlled sampling path, exposure timing, recovery management and separation from electronics heat.
Transferable information beyond environmental or batch identity, with manageable drift.

pages.title: S26 Photoacoustic gas spectroscopy
text: **S26 · Chemical observation candidate · Photoacoustic gas measurement**

Photoacoustic spectroscopy converts absorbed, modulated optical energy into a pressure-related acoustic signal. With a suitable wavelength and measurement cell, the response can support gas analysis. Selectivity depends on the optical absorption being addressed, the gas mixture and the instrument model.
## Signal and useful question

The primary signal is an acoustic or pressure-related response, converted to a concentration or partial-pressure estimate through calibration. Candidate uses include monitoring a relevant gas in a controlled research environment where the measurement adds more specificity than a broad gas-response sensor.
## Qualify the sampling chain

A precise sensor cannot correct an unrepresentative gas sample. The record should identify where gas was sampled, the flow or diffusion arrangement and the response interval. A delayed signal should not be assigned to the current plate state without a model of that delay.

This modality is a candidate for specialized monitoring or research instruments. Even a well-qualified gas concentration does not identify the biological source of that gas by itself. A biological interpretation requires an appropriate assay and controls that distinguish sample activity from medium, background and instrument contributions.
tables: Reference gas mixtures, optical power, pressure, temperature and acoustic-cell response.
Overlapping absorption, water vapour, background acoustics, leaks and sampling-path memory.
Modulated source, optical cell, acoustic detection, gas routing and environmental correction.
Required gas selectivity and sensitivity with a qualified sampling path.

pages.title: S27 Nondispersive infrared carbon dioxide sensing
text: **S27 · Environmental and research candidate · Infrared gas absorption**

Nondispersive infrared gas sensing measures attenuation in selected infrared bands associated with a target gas, commonly using a reference channel or other compensation. Carbon dioxide monitoring can provide useful environmental context, but the concentration observed depends on sampling location, ventilation and background sources.
## Signal and useful question

The output may be gas concentration in parts per million or volume fraction, with pressure and temperature conditions relevant to the conversion. Candidate questions include whether an instrument environment remains within its declared range and whether a research headspace changes reproducibly.
## Avoid inappropriate baseline correction

Some compensation strategies assume that the sensor periodically sees a known background condition. That assumption may be invalid in a controlled chamber or specialized research setting. The selected device and software configuration should therefore be assessed together.

Carbon dioxide observations may support environmental quality checks or a bounded research model. They do not independently measure viable count or susceptibility. If a biological interpretation is investigated, the model should account for transport, volume, exchange and non-biological sources rather than treating concentration as a direct growth curve.
tables: Suitable gas references, optical baseline, pressure and temperature compensation.
Humidity, optical contamination, leaks, human breath, background drift and automatic baseline assumptions.
Representative gas access, response-time characterization and protection of the optical path.
Stable environmental measurement with a sampling arrangement appropriate to the intended function.

pages.title: S28 Surface acoustic wave mass sensing
text: **S28 · Surface observation candidate · Acoustic-wave research**

Surface acoustic wave devices propagate an acoustic disturbance along a material surface. Changes in the surface environment can alter frequency, phase, velocity or attenuation. A functional coating or sample contact can make the response sensitive to mass loading or material properties, but also introduces additional sources of variation.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include frequency shift in hertz, phase and attenuation. Candidate research questions concern whether a controlled surface interaction produces a reproducible signal that is useful for the selected assay or environmental measurement.
## Treat selectivity as an assay property

A transducer does not become biologically selective merely because it is highly sensitive. If a surface chemistry is used to create selectivity, that chemistry, its stability and its cross-reactions become part of the assay that must be evaluated.

This is a future research candidate with substantial integration uncertainty. It is not proposed as a direct replacement for whole-plate imaging. The first development task would be to establish a reproducible physical response on controlled reference materials, followed by an assessment of whether the intended biological question can be addressed without confounding the signal with surface or fluid properties.
tables: Frequency and phase reference, temperature response, baseline coating and controlled loading.
Temperature, humidity, viscosity, coating ageing, nonspecific adsorption and mechanical stress.
Specialized transducer, radio-frequency electronics, surface preparation and a qualified sample interface.
A stable response with a defensible separation between intended loading and environmental effects.

pages.title: S29 Quartz crystal microbalance sensing
text: **S29 · Surface observation candidate · Resonant mass and viscoelastic response**

A quartz crystal microbalance detects changes in a resonator’s behaviour when its surface environment changes. Under restricted thin, rigid loading assumptions, frequency shifts can be related to mass per area. In liquids or soft biological layers, viscoelastic and hydrodynamic effects can make a simple mass conversion inappropriate.
## Signal and useful question

The primary outputs are resonant frequency and, where measured, dissipation or related damping quantities. A mass-per-area estimate is derived under an explicit model. Candidate research uses concern controlled surface attachment or material changes rather than weighing an entire culture plate.
## Retain the measured response

The record should preserve frequency and damping data even when the analysis reports an inferred mass. A reviewer should be able to see which model was used and whether the data were consistent with its assumptions. An apparent mass change should not be labelled biomass without an independent basis.

The modality is an exploratory research option. Its qualification should first distinguish surface loading from changes in the surrounding fluid. Clinical susceptibility or organism identification would require a separate assay and validation programme, and neither follows from the resonator’s nominal mass sensitivity alone.
tables: Frequency reference, clean-surface baseline, temperature stability and suitable loading models.
Liquid viscosity, density, soft-film behaviour, nonspecific adsorption and surface history.
Resonator interface, stable fluid or contact conditions, surface management and specialized electronics.
A reproducible response whose model assumptions remain credible in the selected sample format.

pages.title: S30 Acoustic resonance and attenuation
text: **S30 · Physical observation candidate · Acoustic material response**

Acoustic resonance and attenuation measurements examine how sound propagates through or interacts with a material system. The observed response depends on geometry, density, compressibility, viscosity and interfaces. In a plate or fluid assembly, vessel properties can contribute strongly to the signal.
## Signal and useful question

Candidate outputs include resonant frequency in hertz, sound velocity in metres per second, attenuation and dimensionless quality factor. Potential research questions include whether a reproducible physical change can be detected and separated from the mechanical properties of the holder and vessel.
## Establish a useful baseline first

An assembly may have many resonances unrelated to the sample. Development should characterize the empty holder and permitted vessels before interpreting changes in a biological context. The analysis should retain the excitation and detection conditions so that a spectral shift can be investigated later.

This is a future research candidate, with no AMReye.AI assay evidence established here. It may prove more useful for checking fill state, mechanical coupling or instrument integrity than for biological inference. Selection should follow the demonstrated function rather than the general sensitivity of acoustic methods.
tables: Known mechanical or fluid references, geometry, coupling and frequency response.
Temperature, bubbles, contact pressure, vessel variation, mounting and background vibration.
Transducers, coupling arrangement, excitation control and stable mechanical interfaces.
A signal linked to the intended physical change with acceptable sensitivity to placement.

topics.title: Environment, motion and instrument monitoring
text: **S31 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Resistance thermometry**

pages.title: S31 Resistance temperature measurement
text: **S31 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Resistance thermometry**

Resistance temperature measurement uses a material’s predictable resistance-temperature relationship. The complete result depends on the sensor, excitation, wiring, reference and conversion model. Four-wire arrangements can reduce lead-resistance effects, but they do not remove self-heating, placement or calibration uncertainty. [R20]
## Signal and useful question

The instrument measures resistance in ohms and derives temperature in degrees Celsius or kelvin. Useful questions include whether the relevant observation environment is stable, whether electronics are overheating and whether a process experienced an excursion.
## Location defines meaning

A sensor attached to a wall measures a different thermal environment from a sensor near the plate or on a processor. The record should identify location and mounting, and any inference about the sample temperature should be supported by a transfer study.

For Reader V1, temperature monitoring can support instrument characterization and fault detection. Integrated incubation would require a broader spatial and temporal assessment. Multiple agreeing sensors do not demonstrate uniformity if they are all placed in the same unrepresentative region. Qualification should include the conditions and positions that could reveal a meaningful gradient.
tables: Traceable temperature references across the intended range and complete signal-chain verification.
Self-heating, lead mismatch, thermal contact, response lag, gradients and electrical noise.
Suitable placement, wiring, analog measurement and protection from damage or contamination.
Temperature uncertainty and response time appropriate to the monitored location.

pages.title: S32 Capacitive relative humidity sensing
text: **S32 · Environmental monitoring candidate · Capacitive humidity measurement**

A capacitive humidity sensor uses a material whose dielectric response changes with water vapour exposure. The instrument converts that response into relative humidity through calibration and compensation. Relative humidity depends on temperature and describes a local gas condition, not the total water content of a plate.
## Signal and useful question

The derived output is relative humidity in percent, accompanied by temperature and sensor quality status. Candidate uses include detecting environmental changes that may affect condensation, evaporation or instrument reliability.
## Condensation is a separate event

A high humidity reading does not establish that droplets are present on the optical path, and a local sensor may miss condensation elsewhere. Image-based obstruction checks and environmental monitoring can complement each other, but they answer different questions.

The proposed system should retain sensor saturation or recovery states rather than displaying an apparently precise value throughout a compromised interval. If humidity is used in a biological model, the analysis should account for the sensor’s location and lag. Its most defensible initial role is environmental context and instrument quality assessment, with any growth-related inference evaluated separately.
tables: Suitable humidity references, temperature dependence and response-time checks.
Condensation, chemical exposure, contamination, hysteresis, placement and slow recovery after saturation.
Representative airflow, protection that does not create excessive lag and a serviceable mounting.
Stable local measurement under the intended humidity and contamination conditions.

pages.title: S33 Pressure measurement
text: **S33 · Environmental and control candidate · Pressure measurement**

Pressure sensors convert mechanical deformation or another pressure-dependent effect into an electrical signal. Absolute, gauge and differential measurements use different reference conditions. A value without its reference type can be misleading even when its numerical units are correct.
## Signal and useful question

The output is pressure in pascals or a declared multiple. Candidate functions include monitoring a gas path, detecting an obstruction or assessing a pressure difference across a relevant assembly. The selected function determines the required range, response time and reference.
## Pressure alone does not prove containment

A pressure difference can support an engineering assessment, but it does not independently establish airflow direction everywhere, filter integrity or biological containment. Those claims require the relevant system-level evaluation.

The instrument should distinguish a measured process change from a failed sensor line. Plausibility checks, maintenance records and independent observations can help resolve that difference. If a pressure measurement is required for a control decision, the response to unavailable or implausible data should be specified before the control function is enabled. The initial catalogue role is engineering monitoring rather than a direct biological measurement.
tables: Traceable pressure reference, zero, span, temperature behaviour and line integrity.
Leaks, blocked tubing, condensate, offset drift, mounting stress and pressure-port placement.
Compatible ports, tubing, seals, protective interfaces and accessible maintenance.
Reliable detection of the intended condition with a defined fault response.

pages.title: S34 Airflow measurement
text: **S34 · Environmental and control candidate · Flow measurement**

Airflow can be measured through several physical approaches, including thermal transfer and pressure-related methods. Each responds to a defined flow path and fluid condition. A local reading should not be assumed to describe circulation throughout an enclosure.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs may be volumetric flow in litres per minute, mass flow or local velocity in metres per second. Temperature, pressure and gas composition may be needed to interpret or convert the quantity. Candidate uses include monitoring cooling, detecting a restricted path or characterizing a research gas-sampling arrangement.
## Connect flow to the consequence

The product should identify why the measurement matters. Reduced electronics cooling may require throttling or shutdown. A changed research sampling flow may invalidate the time relationship between a plate and a gas observation. Those responses have different priorities and should not share an unexplained generic alarm.

Flow measurement is a proposed engineering channel. Its presence does not establish sterile airflow or safe containment. Qualification should evaluate the complete path and the relevant failure modes, including disconnected tubing or a sensor that reports plausible flow while the intended sampling route is bypassed.
tables: Suitable flow reference, gas conditions, path geometry and response across the intended range.
Leaks, turbulence, fouling, gas composition, temperature and flow-profile changes.
Defined duct or channel, low unwanted restriction and service access.
A flow quantity relevant to the function and robust to expected path changes.

pages.title: S35 Strain gauge weighing
text: **S35 · Mechanical monitoring candidate · Gravimetric measurement**

Strain-gauge weighing measures deformation of a load-bearing element and converts it to force or mass under a calibrated model. A plate assembly includes the vessel, medium, water and any biological material. Changes in those contributions are not automatically separable.
## Signal and useful question

The primary electrical response is a bridge signal, with derived load in newtons or mass in grams. Candidate functions include plate presence, gross fill checks, evaporation research and mechanical monitoring. A whole-plate mass change should not be labelled microbial biomass without a separately established relationship.
## Compare signal size with the disturbance

Nominal converter resolution is not the same as usable mass resolution. An instrument may display many decimal places while drift and handling variation dominate the change of interest. The evaluation should report repeatability and stability over the intended observation interval.

The proposed initial role is engineering and research context. Presence detection or evaporation tracking may be useful without making any biological inference. If mass data are included in fusion, preserve taring events and mechanical configuration changes so that an apparent discontinuity is not interpreted as a sudden biological event.
tables: Traceable masses, zero, span, loading position, hysteresis and drift.
Evaporation, condensation, handling forces, thermal drift, cable forces and mechanical creep.
Stable support, isolation from motion and a reproducible load path.
Useful change resolution under actual environmental and mechanical conditions.

pages.title: S36 Optical distance and presence sensing
text: **S36 · Instrument-control candidate · Optical ranging and presence**

Optical distance sensing estimates range through time-of-flight, triangulation or another declared optical principle. A coarse multizone sensor can support presence, position or clearance checks. Its spatial sampling and ranging uncertainty should not be confused with microscopic three-dimensional imaging. Manufacturer multizone ranging documentation supports an engineering presence use, not colony topography. [R19]
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include distance in millimetres, return strength and measurement-validity indicators. Candidate functions include checking that a plate or mechanism occupies a permitted region and detecting gross deviations before capture or motion.
## Use validity information

A numerical range can be unreliable when the return signal is weak or when several surfaces contribute. The control interface should preserve validity flags and avoid converting an invalid range into a confident “plate present” state.

This candidate supports instrument readiness and motion checks. If finer shape information is needed for research, a separately qualified optical method should be considered. The proposed evaluation should challenge the sensor with empty holders, permitted vessels, misalignment and reflective or transparent surfaces, then verify that the system responds appropriately when distance is unavailable or ambiguous.
tables: Known distances, target materials, ambient-light conditions and alignment.
Transparent surfaces, multiple reflections, low return signal, contamination and object angle.
Clear optical path, mounting stability and quality-aware control logic.
Reliable detection of the intended mechanical state under permitted target conditions.

pages.title: S37 Magnetic position encoding
text: **S37 · Instrument-control candidate · Magnetic position measurement**

Magnetic position encoders infer displacement or rotation from a magnetic field and its relationship to a sensing element. They can provide feedback without an exposed optical scale. Their performance depends on magnet geometry, alignment, field conditions and the conversion model.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include angle in degrees or radians, position in length units and status information. Candidate functions include verifying mechanism position, indexing a plate holder or detecting whether a shutter has reached a permitted state.
## Measure the mechanism rather than only the motor

An encoder on a motor shaft may report commanded rotation while a coupling slips or a downstream mechanism remains displaced. The relevant feedback location should follow the physical state that the system needs to know.

This is a proposed control-sensing option, not a biological modality. Qualification should include plausible failures such as misalignment, lost feedback or mechanical play. The software should distinguish estimated, commanded and confirmed positions. A safety-relevant action should not proceed merely because the last remembered position was acceptable before a restart or service intervention.
tables: Known positions, magnet alignment, full travel behaviour and repeatability.
External magnetic fields, temperature, magnet variation, mechanical backlash and mounting shifts.
Stable magnet-sensor geometry, control interface and independent limit or interlock strategy where required.
Feedback accuracy and fault detectability appropriate to the controlled mechanism.

pages.title: S38 Inertial vibration measurement
text: **S38 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Inertial measurement**

An accelerometer measures specific force along defined axes; related inertial sensors may measure angular motion. These channels can help characterize vibration, handling shocks and movement during acquisition. Their output depends on mounting, bandwidth, orientation and the influence of gravity.
## Signal and useful question

Acceleration is expressed in metres per second squared or in a declared multiple of standard gravity. Frequency-domain descriptors can summarize vibration over an observation interval. The useful question is whether mechanical disturbance is large enough to compromise the selected image or instrument state.
## Link vibration to an optical consequence

A vibration signal should not trigger an arbitrary rejection threshold without evidence. The qualification should compare inertial observations with image blur, registration error or another relevant outcome. Some measured vibration may be harmless, while an unmonitored local motion may still affect the optics.

This channel is proposed for engineering characterization and readiness checks. It may also help investigate transport damage or recurring faults. The record should preserve the interval and bandwidth used for a summary, because a single “vibration score” can conceal whether a short shock occurred during the actual exposure or at an irrelevant time.
tables: Axis scale, offset, alignment, frequency response and timestamp accuracy.
Mounting resonance, temperature, aliasing, gravity projection and electrical noise.
Rigid representative placement, synchronized sampling and signal processing.
Demonstrated relationship between the monitored disturbance and measurement quality.

pages.title: S39 Electrical power monitoring
text: **S39 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Electrical power measurement**

Voltage and current monitoring can reveal supply instability, overload, abnormal consumption or a failing subsystem. Electrical power is derived from the appropriate voltage-current relationship, with waveform and measurement timing considered where relevant. A low reported average can conceal short disturbances that affect capture or storage.
## Signal and useful question

Outputs include volts, amperes, watts and integrated energy in joules or watt-hours. Candidate functions include detecting undervoltage, verifying a load budget and relating faults to acquisition or processing activity.
## Preserve the affected operation

A power fault during storage may threaten record completeness, while a disturbance during exposure may alter an image. The system should associate the event with the relevant operation and verify recovery rather than merely clearing an alarm after the voltage returns.

This proposed channel supports reliability and service. It does not measure biological activity. Qualification should include controlled electrical load scenarios, safe shutdown and restart behaviour, and verification that a partial record cannot appear complete. Power monitoring is especially useful when paired with data-integrity checks that reveal whether an electrical event had a lasting consequence.
tables: Reference voltage and current, sense-path resistance, offset and sampling response.
Transients, wiring drops, thermal drift, measurement bandwidth and shared ground effects.
Appropriate sensing location, protection, isolation where needed and event synchronization.
Detection of disturbances that can affect the actual instrument function.

pages.title: S40 Reference photodiode monitoring
text: **S40 · Instrument-monitoring candidate · Optical reference measurement**

A reference photodiode measures light at a defined location in the illumination path. With a suitable response calibration, it can help distinguish a changing source from a changing sample. Its observation is local and spectrally weighted by the detector response.
## Signal and useful question

The primary quantity is photocurrent or converted voltage. Derived optical power or relative intensity requires a stated responsivity and geometry. Candidate uses include monitoring source stability, detecting a failed illumination channel and verifying exposure synchronization.
## A source check is not a full-field check

The photodiode may report stable light while a diffuser shifts, a lens becomes contaminated or one part of the field darkens. It should complement, rather than replace, spatial image-quality verification. A reference channel also shares some failure mechanisms with the source it monitors, so independent checks remain useful.

This candidate is particularly relevant to a controlled imaging reader. The proposed evaluation should determine which faults the reference can detect, how quickly it detects them and which faults remain invisible. The result should be a specific quality-control function with an explicit limit, not a general assurance that every captured image is correctly illuminated.
tables: Detector responsivity, linearity, dark offset, amplifier gain and reference geometry.
Detector ageing, temperature, contamination, stray light and spectral mismatch with the imaging path.
A representative pick-off location, stable optics and synchronized acquisition.
Reliable detection of illumination changes relevant to image quality.

topics.title: Software, records, data and genomic provenance
text: The proposed software system should assign clear responsibility for acquisition, physical control, analysis, review and record management. These functions have different failure consequences. A delayed research computation is not equivalent to a failed interlock, and an unavailable cloud service should not silently invalidate a locally completed observation.

pages.title: The software system and its responsibilities
text: The proposed software system should assign clear responsibility for acquisition, physical control, analysis, review and record management. These functions have different failure consequences. A delayed research computation is not equivalent to a failed interlock, and an unavailable cloud service should not silently invalidate a locally completed observation.
## Define responsibilities independently of deployment

Physical control should enforce permitted states and limits. Acquisition should preserve original observations and their context. Analysis should produce traceable derived values. PIMS should maintain identity and lineage. The operator interface should expose evidence and permitted actions. Remote services can support fleet management, collaboration and research computation when the data purpose and connection state are explicit.
## BAHU and the shared research services

BAHU is the proposed operator-facing orchestration concept. The broader cloud or “Hive” concept describes shared services for authorized data processing, models and research collaboration. These names should not conceal the functions or imply a fixed number of software layers.

The software should be testable through these contracts even when individual components are replaced. A new model or processor should not change the meaning of a plate identifier or a reviewer correction. Stable semantics are a practical form of modularity: they allow innovation while preserving the evidence chain on which laboratory trust depends.
tables: Authorized commands, confirmed states, fault handling and safe limits.
Immutable observation, timing, configuration, calibration and quality metadata.
Exact input references, method version, output type and uncertainty.
Eligible method context and independently versioned standards rules.
Responsible actor, disposition, edits, reasons and release state.
Purpose-limited exchange, acknowledgements, update control and recovery.

pages.title: PIMS as the plate record system
text: PIMS means **Plate Information Management System** in this compendium. Its central responsibility is to maintain the relationship between a physical plate, its observations, the analyses performed on those observations and the person who reviews the result. It should make that relationship inspectable without requiring a reviewer to understand the internal software implementation.
## A plate record is more than an image folder

The proposed record begins with an immutable plate identifier and an association to the permitted laboratory case or study identifier. Each capture adds its own time, instrument configuration, calibration reference, image checksum and quality state. A repeated image is another observation of the plate, not a replacement for the original. Where the plate association is uncertain, the system should stop interpretation and request identity resolution.
## Preserve the path from observation to decision

Analysis outputs reference their exact inputs. The standards interpretation records the ruleset version separately from the measurement algorithm. The reviewer can inspect the original image, measurement overlay, uncertainty and applicable interpretation context. A correction creates a new linked version with a reason; it does not erase the result that was initially presented.
!FIG work/assets/figures/pims-lineage.png | Proposed PIMS lineage. A new analysis and review preserve the original evidence and earlier decisions.

PIMS is proposed product functionality. The field dictionaries in the appendices describe interfaces, not an assertion that a complete implementation exists. A minimum useful release should demonstrate identity integrity, reproducible retrieval and a complete correction trail before adding conversational or predictive features. Laboratory connectivity should export reviewed records through a controlled mapping rather than letting a receiving system infer missing context from file names.

pages.title: Capture and observation interfaces
text: Capture and sensor interfaces should preserve what the instrument actually observed. Each record needs identity, timing, configuration, units where applicable and a quality state. The schema should make missing information explicit rather than depend on a reader to infer meaning from a filename or a blank cell.
## Proposed capture contract

A capture record identifies the plate, the acquisition device, the observation interval and the original image. It references the calibration and optical configuration used. A checksum supports integrity checking, while a storage location identifies where authorized software can retrieve the original bytes. The checksum does not replace access control or establish biological truth.
## Proposed sensor contract

A sensor observation additionally identifies the channel, physical quantity, unit, sampling or averaging interval and calibration reference. Raw response and converted value should remain linked. A value derived through a compensation model should identify that model rather than appear to be an unprocessed measurement.

Failed acquisition should create an event with an unavailable value and a reason. It should not create a zero-valued measurement. These interfaces are specifications for development; their inclusion here does not claim that a complete instrument or data service already implements them.
tables: Unique identity of the observation, stable across retrieval and reanalysis.
Association to the physical plate or explicitly unresolved identity state.
Actual acquisition start and end, with clock basis and uncertainty when relevant.
Optical, sensor and acquisition settings needed to interpret the observation.
Usable, failed, uncertain or another controlled state with reasons.
Measured, derived, imputed, simulated or unavailable.

pages.title: Calibration and measurement interfaces
text: Calibration and measurement interfaces should make the conversion from observation to quantity reproducible. The measurement record should identify the calibration that was valid for the acquisition and the analysis method that used it. Replacing a coefficient silently would make the historical result impossible to reconstruct.
## Proposed calibration contract

A calibration record includes the instrument and configuration, reference identity, method, validity range, coefficients, residuals and uncertainty basis. It also records who authorized the calibration and which changes invalidate it. A calibration can be superseded without deleting its relationship to older observations.
## Preserve corrections as new evidence

A reviewer-adjusted boundary produces a new measurement linked to the original estimate and the decision record. The system should preserve whether the change was manual, algorithmic reprocessing or a corrected calibration. Each has a different provenance.

For a zone diameter, a rounded display value should not be the only stored quantity. Preserve sufficient precision for the qualified measurement and interpretation process, while avoiding a display that implies more accuracy than the uncertainty supports. The data model should therefore separate stored numerical representation, reported precision and the uncertainty claim. [R16]
tables: Unique identity for this derived measurement version.
Exact original observations used by the method.
Calibration and configuration relationship applied to the quantity.
Named physical or analytical quantity with an explicit unit.
Estimate and uncertainty representation, including the basis or coverage convention.
Coordinates, boundary representation and coordinate frame where relevant.
Algorithm and processing configuration that produced the estimate.

pages.title: AI and interpretation interfaces
text: AI outputs and standards interpretations should remain separate records. A learned model estimates a feature or outcome from data; a standards engine applies eligible rules from a controlled source. Combining them into one unversioned label would obscure both the statistical uncertainty and the normative basis of the result.
## Proposed AI output contract

An AI record identifies the task, model package, input observations, preprocessing, output type, confidence or uncertainty representation and domain checks. It should distinguish a segmentation, a quality flag, a research prediction and a retrieved explanation. These outputs have different meanings and different permitted uses.
## Reject invalid combinations

The standards engine should not infer a missing organism or method from a plausible image. It should also avoid choosing whichever ruleset yields a more convenient category. The selected standards policy and its version should be explicit, and changes should create a new interpretation record. [R01] [R02]

A research prediction may be displayed alongside measured evidence only when its status remains clear. It should not overwrite the measured quantity or become a standards interpretation by renaming a field. These interfaces are proposed contracts intended to make such misuse detectable during development and review.
tables: Unique version of the rule-based interpretation.
Exact measurement and context being interpreted.
Authoritative ruleset identity, including applicable corrections.
Assay, organism, antimicrobial and other required eligibility fields.
Specific applicable rule or an explicit reason why no rule applies.
Eligible result, technical uncertainty, unsupported or unavailable.

pages.title: Review correction and export interfaces
text: Reviewer decisions and exports complete the evidence chain. A decision records what a responsible user concluded after inspecting the available evidence. An export records which version was released, where it was sent and whether the destination accepted it. Neither should be inferred merely from opening a screen or downloading a file.
## Proposed reviewer decision contract

The record should identify the reviewer, role, time, input record versions, disposition and reasons for changes or rejection. It should preserve the distinction between accepting a measurement, accepting an interpretation and authorizing release under the laboratory workflow.
## Export the reviewed state

An export package should identify the released record version, schema, destination mapping and integrity information. It should carry the status and correction semantics supported by the receiving workflow. Delivery acknowledgement and clinical-system acceptance may be different events.

If a released record is corrected, the product should issue a linked correction through the agreed interface and track reconciliation. The original export remains part of the audit history. This design makes it possible to investigate what a receiving system or user saw at a particular time, rather than reconstructing history from the latest database values alone.
tables: Preserve the reviewed versions and permit the next authorized workflow step.
Create linked revised values and retain the original evidence and reason.
Prevent release of the rejected result and record the relevant limitation.
Keep the record pending with the information or action needed for resolution.
Request a new observation while preserving the failed or insufficient one.

pages.title: Edge and cloud responsibilities
text: Edge and cloud responsibilities should follow latency, reliability, privacy and operating needs. Local processing can preserve acquisition and review during a network interruption. Remote services can support authorized collaboration, larger research computations and fleet operations. Neither location automatically guarantees safety or efficiency.
## Keep essential local functions explicit

The proposed instrument should retain the functions required to complete or safely interrupt its permitted local workflow. These include physical control, acquisition records, quality checks and access to the qualified local configuration. A remote outage should produce a clear synchronization state rather than a fabricated success or a silent change in analysis behaviour.
## Synchronization is a workflow

Queued records need unique identities, retry behaviour and conflict handling. A reconnect should not replace a reviewed local result with a different remote analysis silently. The system should preserve both versions and apply the appropriate review policy.

Resource selection should be based on measured workload, power, storage and service needs. The newest processor or largest model is not automatically the best choice. A smaller qualified local model may be preferable for a time-sensitive measurement, while a larger research model can run separately without changing the clinical workflow.
tables: Local deterministic response and independent limits.
Local integrity checks and sufficient temporary storage.
Qualified local capability where offline operation is required.
Remote or scheduled computation with reproducible inputs and resource limits.
Signed packages, authorization, staged rollout and rollback.
Purpose-limited exchange under agreed access and provenance rules.

pages.title: Data collection and annotation strategy
text: Data collection should be designed around the intended evaluation, not only the convenience of acquisition. A large number of near-duplicate images from a few plates can provide less useful evidence than a smaller, well-characterized set spanning the relevant conditions. The data model should preserve the relationships needed to recognize that difference.
## Define the unit of independence

Images can be nested within observations, plates, isolates, patients, batches and sites. Training and test partitions should prevent related examples from crossing the boundary in a way that inflates apparent performance. The appropriate separation depends on the claim: robustness to a new image is different from transfer to a new laboratory.
## Collect disagreement deliberately

Annotations should allow uncertainty and disagreement rather than forcing every case into a falsely precise label. Independent review and adjudication can help establish the reference for a specific task. Original annotations should remain available so that the effect of adjudication can be assessed.

The collection programme should also record why data were acquired and what reuse is permitted. Data suitable for service troubleshooting are not automatically authorized for model training. Representative data, appropriate reference labels and a controlled evaluation design are central to medical AI development principles. [R21] The proposed implementation should make those requirements part of routine data operations.
tables: Identifies camera, optics, lighting, configuration and time.
Supports eligibility and assessment of domain coverage.
Identifies who labelled the data, under what instructions and with what uncertainty.
Enable plate, isolate, patient, batch and site separation where applicable.
Prevent evaluation from silently discarding difficult cases.

pages.title: Genomic data access and provenance
text: Genomic and scientific repositories can provide valuable evidence, but they differ in curation, scope, licensing, update practices and uncertainty. The proposed platform should use selected resources through lawful, purpose-defined access and preserve the versions used in each analysis. It should not promise to ingest every repository or treat all deposited records as equally reliable.
## Separate sequence evidence from image inference

A measured sequence can be analysed for features supported by a qualified pipeline and database. An image-based prediction of a genotype is a different research task. The interface should identify whether a molecular feature was measured, computationally detected from sequence data, inferred from another phenotype or simply retrieved from literature.

CARD and NCBI Pathogen Detection illustrate complementary curated and sequence-based resources. Their documentation should guide interpretation of their outputs; database access does not establish clinical validity for a new product workflow. [R24] [R25]

The proposed service should record query parameters, tool versions and the exact evidence used. When a database changes, a new analysis should remain distinguishable from the earlier result. A disagreement between phenotype and genotype should trigger investigation of method, context and uncertainty rather than an automatic assumption that one source must be correct.
tables: Preserve ontology, evidence model, database release and applicable use terms.
Retain accession, version, sample context and quality limitations.
Identify assembly and annotation versions and avoid treating one reference as universal.
Link to the original study and retain the supported claim and limitations.
Apply the agreed purpose, access, retention and publication conditions.

topics.title: AI for acquisition, identity and zone boundaries
text: The forty capabilities that follow are candidates for task-specific AI across the platform. They span acquisition, measurement, quality, modelling, bioinformatics, workflow and service. Some may prove useful with conventional algorithms alone. The catalogue treats that outcome as a valid engineering decision.

pages.title: Using the AI capability catalogue
text: The forty capabilities that follow are candidates for task-specific AI across the platform. They span acquisition, measurement, quality, modelling, bioinformatics, workflow and service. Some may prove useful with conventional algorithms alone. The catalogue treats that outcome as a valid engineering decision.
## Evaluate the complete task

Each entry identifies inputs, outputs, why learning might help, a conventional baseline, data needs, failure modes and validation. A capability is useful only if it improves the intended decision or process under realistic conditions. A high model score on a convenient dataset is insufficient.
## Shared evidence requirements

Inputs should be representative of the intended use, evaluation partitions should respect data relationships and performance should include failed or abstained cases. Confidence needs empirical calibration. Changes in acquisition, population or workflow can alter performance and should be monitored. [R21] [R23]

The catalogue does not prescribe model generations. Candidate families include geometric methods, convolutional or transformer-based vision models, probabilistic models, sequence methods and task-specific language systems. Custom development should be driven by evidence and efficiency requirements. A model that cannot identify when its inputs are unsuitable should not be trusted merely because it performs well on routine examples.
tables: Capture, geometry, measurement and image-quality assistance.
Temporal analysis and early-response or MIC research.
Fusion, uncertainty, missingness and dataset quality.
Bioinformatics, evidence retrieval and rule-consistency support.
Workflow, maintenance, fleet and operator assistance.

pages.title: A01 Capture readiness assessment
text: **A01 · Proposed acquisition assistance**

Capture readiness assessment asks whether the next observation is likely to be usable and correctly associated. AI may recognize combinations of visual conditions that are difficult to express as a small set of thresholds. It should complement explicit checks for identity, calibration and hardware state, not override them.
## Keep hard prerequisites explicit

An expired calibration or unresolved identifier is not a visual classification problem. Such conditions should prevent the relevant workflow step regardless of the model’s confidence. Conversely, a visual warning should explain what the operator needs to inspect rather than simply displaying a red readiness score.

The qualification should compare the complete acquisition workflow with the deterministic baseline. A useful model should reduce avoidable failed captures without creating excessive operator interruptions. Cases that remain uncertain should be retained for review and future analysis, including whether the warning was justified after a successful reacquisition.
tables: Preview image, plate association, configuration, calibration validity and instrument status.
Specific readiness findings, affected region and a recommended permitted action.
Deterministic identity, presence, calibration and exposure checks.

Learning site backgrounds, overlooking unfamiliar obstructions or treating a plausible image as proof of identity.
Cause-specific detection, false rejection, usable capture yield and recovery performance on held-out sessions and sites.

pages.title: A02 Exposure and illumination selection
text: **A02 · Proposed acquisition optimization**

Exposure and illumination selection can adapt acquisition to the appearance of a permitted plate while keeping the measurement pipeline within a qualified range. AI may predict which allowed setting will produce the most useful evidence, especially when global brightness is a poor guide to the feature of interest.
## Optimize the evidence rather than the picture

The objective should be a useful, reproducible measurement image, not maximum contrast or aesthetic enhancement. A setting that makes one boundary conspicuous may suppress another relevant feature. Evaluation should therefore assess the complete permitted image domain.

The instrument should record the selected settings and preserve limits enforced independently of the model. If the model cannot find an eligible setting, it should request review or declare acquisition unsuccessful. For time-series research, any setting change should remain explicit so that intensity differences are not mistaken for biological dynamics.
tables: Preview images, permitted lighting modes, exposure limits and the intended measurement task.
A selected qualified setting and the reason or expected quality improvement.
Fixed settings or histogram-based exposure control with saturation limits.
Task-aware selection where local glare, medium appearance and boundary contrast interact.
