Optimizing visual appeal, hiding weak growth, selecting an unqualified mode or creating inconsistent time-series appearance.
Measurement quality, saturation, repeatability and setting-selection stability against fixed-setting baselines.

pages.title: A03 Focus quality assessment
text: **A03 · Proposed image-quality assessment**

Focus assessment determines whether the acquired optical detail is sufficient for a specified task. A model may distinguish genuinely informative edges from texture, noise or printed labels that can make a simple sharpness score appear favourable. The required focus quality depends on the feature being measured.
## Evaluate the relevant plane

A sharp lid inscription does not establish that the agar surface is in focus. The assessment should therefore examine the regions and plane that support the intended measurement. A global score may hide a blurred edge at the periphery of the field.

The model should be compared with conventional metrics under the same acquisition conditions. Its output should identify the affected region and support a permitted recovery action. If focus adjustment changes the qualified optical configuration, the system should apply the relevant calibration rules rather than assume that a sharper image preserves the previous measurement scale.
tables: Image regions, optical configuration, expected feature scale and optional reference-target observations.

Separating useful biological detail from high-contrast artifacts and variable medium appearance.
Controlled focus variation, realistic plate examples and independent assessments of measurement usability.
Scoring labels instead of the measurement plane, confusing noise with detail or missing spatially uneven focus.
Task-level measurement error across focus conditions, local defect detection and false rejection.

pages.title: A04 Glare and condensation detection
text: **A04 · Proposed artifact assessment**

Glare and condensation detection identifies optical conditions that obscure or distort useful evidence. AI may recognize varied droplet patterns, reflections and local veiling that are difficult to capture with a single intensity threshold. The output should describe the observation problem, not promise that another spectral mode can always repair it.
## Assess consequence as well as presence

An artifact outside the measurement region may be harmless, while a small obstruction at a critical edge can invalidate the result. The system should connect the artifact finding to the affected task rather than rejecting every imperfect image indiscriminately.

Evaluation should include cases in which the model is uncertain and cases where a different imaging mode improves appearance without restoring a valid measurement. Original observations remain available for review. Any reacquisition creates a new record, allowing investigators to assess whether the proposed recovery action actually resolved the limitation.
tables: Original image, optional paired illumination modes and permitted vessel context.

pages.title: A05 Plate pose estimation
text: **A05 · Proposed geometric estimation**

Plate pose estimation determines the position and orientation needed to relate an image to the measurement geometry. A learned model may help locate partially obscured boundaries or variable vessel shapes. The resulting transform must still be checked against the qualified optical model.
## Geometry needs an independent reference

A visually centred plate may still be tilted or displaced in height. The model should not infer a precise three-dimensional state from an image that does not contain enough information. Where pose is not identifiable, the output should express that limitation.

Any image transform used for measurement should preserve the relationship to original coordinates. The reviewer should be able to inspect the source image and the transformation applied. Qualification should include loading and positioning variations that are independent of the images used to train the estimator, with acceptance based on their effect on the actual measurement.
tables: Plate image, permitted geometry and optional fiducial observations.
Position, rotation, tilt-related indicators, transform and uncertainty.

pages.title: A06 Plate and vessel identification
text: **A06 · Proposed vessel classification**

Plate and vessel identification determines whether the observed container belongs to a permitted format and which configuration rules apply. AI may assist with visual classification when external appearance varies, but it should not infer missing assay identity merely from the vessel’s shape or colour.
## Classification is not assay confirmation

The same container can hold different media or support different workflows. The software should therefore use visual classification as a consistency check rather than an authoritative source for all assay fields.

A useful evaluation includes unfamiliar but visually similar vessels and cases in which the declared metadata are intentionally inconsistent. The system should request resolution when the conflict matters to calibration or interpretation. It should preserve the operator’s decision and the observed evidence so that recurring supplier or workflow differences can be investigated without silently broadening the permitted domain.

Candidate vessel class, consistency findings and unsupported-format state.

pages.title: A07 Barcode and label association
text: **A07 · Proposed identity-association assistance**

Barcode and label association connects a visible identifier with the correct plate record. Conventional decoding and explicit reconciliation should remain the primary path. AI may help locate a label, distinguish overlapping text or flag a mismatch, but it should never invent a missing identifier.
## Identity errors deserve a separate metric

A correctly measured zone attached to the wrong case is not a successful result. Evaluation should therefore measure association integrity independently of image-analysis accuracy. A high barcode decoding rate is insufficient if the workflow can attach a valid code to the wrong physical object.

Uncertain associations should remain unresolved until an authorized user or qualified process supplies the missing evidence. The record should retain the original label image, decoded values and decision history. AI assistance is justified only if it improves this process without converting uncertainty into a confident but unsupported match.

pages.title: A08 Antimicrobial disk localization
text: **A08 · Proposed object localization**

Antimicrobial disk localization identifies candidate disk centres and boundaries within an eligible plate image. Learned object detectors may handle appearance variation, partial occlusion and clutter better than a purely geometric method. Their detections still need consistency checks and a relationship to the permitted assay layout.
## Evaluate the complete disk map

Per-object detection scores can conceal a plate-level error that matters to the workflow. The evaluation should therefore assess whether the complete disk map is correct and whether uncertain objects are flagged before interpretation.

The software should preserve detection geometry and link any reviewer correction to the original output. A detector should not determine antimicrobial identity from position unless the layout is independently established and validated for that workflow. Object localization supplies a geometric input; it does not by itself establish the drug, disk content or eligible interpretation rule.
tables: Original plate image, spatial calibration and permitted disk or layout context.
Candidate disk locations, extents, confidence and unresolved detections.

Treating labels, bubbles or colonies as disks, missing low-contrast disks or merging nearby objects.

pages.title: A09 Disk label recognition
text: **A09 · Proposed text recognition assistance**

Disk label recognition attempts to read visible markings and associate them with the correct antimicrobial metadata. AI may assist when characters are small, rotated or partially obscured. The consequence of a plausible but incorrect reading can be substantial, so the system should favour unresolved status over guessing.
## Use dictionaries carefully

A restricted vocabulary can reduce impossible outputs, but it can also force an incorrect valid label when the true label is absent. Unknown and unreadable states should therefore remain available. The model should not use a likely susceptibility pattern to decide which drug label it thinks it sees.

The preferred workflow combines visible evidence with independently established assay metadata and review. Corrections should preserve both the original recognition output and the final association. Qualification should examine rare but consequential confusions, rather than reporting only an average character accuracy that hides a wrong antimicrobial identity.
tables: Disk-region images, permitted terminology and independently supplied panel or layout information.

pages.title: A10 Zone boundary segmentation
text: **A10 · Proposed boundary estimation**

Zone boundary segmentation estimates the image region corresponding to a method-defined inhibition boundary. Learned segmentation can model appearance variation and ambiguous local texture, but it must be evaluated against the actual reading definition. A smooth or visually attractive contour is not necessarily the correct contour.
## Preserve the boundary definition

Different biological appearances may require different reading rules. The model should not silently standardize every edge to the same visual pattern. Method and organism context must remain available to the qualified workflow. [R03]

Evaluation should include comparison with conventional algorithms and independent human measurements. Where readers disagree, the reference process and uncertainty should be documented. The product should preserve the original image, estimated boundary and any reviewer adjustment so that an error can be traced to acquisition, segmentation, calibration or interpretation rather than attributed vaguely to “the AI.”
tables: Eligible image, disk geometry, calibration and relevant reading context.
Boundary representation, calibrated measurement inputs and local uncertainty.

Smoothing away meaningful irregularity, following glare, ignoring faint growth or importing training annotation bias.

topics.title: AI for measurement, growth and early AST research
text: **A11 · Proposed uncertainty estimation**

pages.title: A11 Spatial measurement uncertainty
text: **A11 · Proposed uncertainty estimation**

Spatial measurement uncertainty describes how precisely a physical quantity can be supported by the observation and measurement chain. AI may estimate local ambiguity or predict when an image is likely to produce a large measurement error. It should complement, not replace, a physically grounded calibration uncertainty budget.
## Combine evidence without double counting

If the model’s uncertainty estimate already reflects a calibration effect, adding the same effect again can overstate uncertainty. Omitting it can understate uncertainty. The proposed budget should therefore identify the source and dependence of each component. [R16]

A useful uncertainty output should support a decision: whether a measurement is suitable, whether more evidence is needed and how a reviewer should interpret a near-boundary result. Reporting a narrow interval is not an objective in itself. The interval must behave as claimed on independent data and remain meaningful under the declared operating conditions.
tables: Image, boundary candidates, spatial calibration, configuration and repeatability evidence.

Independent reference measurements, repeated observations and difficult cases with documented reader disagreement.
Confidently extrapolating beyond the data, omitting systematic bias or treating model confidence as physical uncertainty.
Empirical interval coverage, interval width, bias and performance across image-quality and site strata.

pages.title: A12 Lawn quality assessment
text: **A12 · Proposed plate-quality assessment**

Lawn quality assessment identifies visible patterns that may make a disk diffusion observation unsuitable or difficult to interpret. AI may recognize irregular coverage, strong spatial variation or other appearance problems. The output should be a quality finding tied to the image, not an unsupported diagnosis of the cause.
## Describe the observation before its cause

An uneven appearance may have several explanations. The interface should identify what is visible and why it affects the task. It should avoid claiming that an image proves a specific preparation error when that conclusion requires additional records.

The qualification should include the permitted organism and medium range and preserve cases on which experts disagree. A model that correctly flags obvious failures but rejects many useful plates may add workload without improving the laboratory result. Evaluate usable coverage and consequential missed defects together, with the laboratory’s established alternative workflow available for unresolved cases. [R03]
tables: Whole-plate image, local texture, assay context and optional paired observations.
Quality regions, observed pattern description and measurement-eligibility recommendation.
Spatial intensity and texture uniformity measures with explicit review rules.
Recognition of complex patterns that vary with medium and organism appearance.
Representative quality variation and independent expert labels with reasons and uncertainty.
Rejecting legitimate morphology, missing localized defects or learning one laboratory’s preparation style.
Quality-defect detection, false rejection and the effect on downstream measurement and review.

pages.title: A13 Mixed morphology detection
text: **A13 · Proposed morphology review assistance**

Mixed morphology detection flags visually distinct growth patterns that may deserve expert review. AI can assist with locating differences in colour, texture, size or spatial organization. A visual difference is not sufficient to confirm a mixed culture, contamination or species identity.
## Keep visual and biological labels separate

The dataset should distinguish “different appearance observed” from “mixed culture confirmed.” Combining those labels would teach a model to make a stronger claim than the image supports. The same caution applies to colony size variation that can arise within one population.

The initial proposed function is triage for review. It should direct attention to the relevant original evidence and preserve the reviewer’s disposition. Evaluation should ask whether the flag improves detection of important cases without creating excessive false alarms. Any later biological classification would require a separately defined task, representative reference data and an explicit intended-use boundary.
tables: Plate or colony-region images, acquisition context and optional temporal observations.
Candidate regions with differing appearance and an explicit review flag.
Colour and texture clustering, size distributions and manual comparison.

Confusing illumination or medium variation with morphology, or missing subtle differences between biological populations.
Region detection and review usefulness; biological conclusions evaluated separately against appropriate confirmation.

pages.title: A14 Within zone colony flagging
text: **A14 · Proposed within-zone observation assistance**

Within-zone colony flagging locates candidate growth-like features inside an inhibition region. AI may help detect small or visually subtle objects and preserve their location for review. The feature can have several explanations, including artifacts, mixed populations or biological phenomena that require confirmation.
## A flag is a prompt to investigate

Heteroresistance research provides reasons to take population heterogeneity seriously, but an image flag does not establish a resistant subpopulation. The dedicated application chapter develops the alternative explanations and confirmation boundary. [R07] [R08]

The proposed workflow should preserve both flagged and unflagged original images so that missed features can be investigated. If the image resolution cannot support the requested observation, the system should say so. Upscaling or generating a sharper-looking feature must not be used as evidence that a colony was actually observed.
tables: Eligible high-detail image, zone geometry and optional repeated observations.
Candidate feature locations, appearance evidence, size estimates where calibrated and uncertainty.
Local contrast detection, connected components and expert inspection.
Distinguishing variable small features from background structure across image conditions.
Region annotations, artifact examples, temporal correspondence and separately recorded confirmation results.
Missing low-contrast growth, labelling dust or droplets as colonies, or equating a visual feature with heteroresistance.

pages.title: A15 Readability and abstention
text: **A15 · Proposed task-level readability decision**

Readability assessment combines relevant quality findings to decide whether the available evidence supports a particular measurement. It is broader than detecting blur or glare alone. AI may help model interactions among defects, but the final eligibility logic should remain explicit and reviewable.
## Report the denominator

In an illustrative set of 100 observations, accepting 90 and abstaining on 10 gives 90 percent coverage. Accuracy among the accepted observations does not describe the full set by itself. This example is a reporting illustration, not AMReye.AI performance.

The proposed evaluation should prespecify how abstentions enter the analysis and what happens operationally to an unreadable case. A useful system should reduce consequential accepted errors while keeping the fallback workload manageable. It should not optimize a headline agreement rate by excluding precisely the cases that matter most to laboratory users.
tables: Image, task, calibration state, artifact findings, boundary uncertainty and required metadata.
Readable, unreadable or uncertain state with specific reasons and permitted next actions.

pages.title: A16 Temporal image registration
text: **A16 · Proposed temporal geometry alignment**

Temporal image registration aligns repeated observations so that apparent movement can be distinguished from a change in the object. AI may assist where conventional feature matching struggles with changing biological appearance. Registration must preserve the physical meaning of the measurement rather than warp every image into superficial agreement.
## Retain original coordinates

Every registered feature should remain traceable to the original observation. A researcher should be able to inspect the transform and determine whether a reported growth displacement exceeds the registration uncertainty.

Rigid or constrained transforms may be preferable when they match the physical motion of the plate. More flexible models should be justified by the acquisition geometry and evaluated for distortion of biological features. A failed registration should not be repaired by silently interpolating or generating an image. The temporal model can handle an explicit gap more honestly than a convincing but unsupported alignment.

pages.title: A17 Colony tracking
text: **A17 · Proposed object tracking research**

Colony tracking links candidate objects across time to study persistence, growth and spatial relationships. AI may combine appearance and motion information when objects change shape or become difficult to separate. The tracking identity is a computational hypothesis, not a permanent biological identity established by the image alone.
## Preserve ambiguous events

When two regions merge visually, the software may no longer be able to attribute subsequent area to the original objects. It should mark that limitation rather than fabricate two precise tracks. A missing observation should likewise remain distinguishable from a true disappearance.

The proposed initial role is research analysis. Evaluation should focus on the quantities investigators intend to derive, such as growth trajectories or spatial interaction measures. A tracker with visually smooth paths can still bias those quantities. Original segmentations, association decisions and manual corrections should therefore remain available for reproducibility and error analysis.

pages.title: A18 Growth curve estimation
text: **A18 · Proposed temporal feature estimation**

Growth-curve estimation fits a temporal representation to observed features such as area, intensity or another qualified signal. AI may model nonlinear relationships or combine observations with different quality levels. The fitted curve should identify what quantity it describes; an image-area trajectory is not automatically a viable-cell growth curve.
## Distinguish fitting from forecasting

A curve fitted through existing observations summarizes those observations. Extending it into the future is a forecast that needs additional evaluation. The software should keep the observed interval and forecast interval visually and numerically distinct.

The research record should preserve units, preprocessing and model assumptions. If a parameter such as a rate cannot be estimated reliably from the available data, it should remain uncertain or unavailable. A smooth curve should not create the impression that a sparse or interrupted observation series contains more biological evidence than was actually acquired.
tables: Time-stamped measured features, observation uncertainty, quality states and assay context.

Representative time series, independent reference measurements where biological quantities are inferred and realistic missingness.
Confusing exposure changes with growth, overfitting sparse data or reporting parameters that are not identifiable.

pages.title: A19 Early response research classification
text: **A19 · Research target for selected early-response workflows**

Early-response classification investigates whether a defined observation window can support a reliable susceptibility-related conclusion in a selected assay. AI may combine temporal and morphological evidence, but the biological response must be present and measurable. Computation cannot recover a response that has not yet become informative.
## Define the sub-two-hour target

The target should state whether the clock begins at sample loading, another assay event or a different documented origin. The specimen context, organism-drug combinations, comparator and success criteria must be fixed before evaluation. Upstream preparation time should be reported separately when it is outside the target clock.

Published single-cell and electrical studies demonstrate that short windows are scientifically investigable in particular methods. They do not establish a universal limit or AMReye.AI performance. [R11] [R38] Endpoint Reader V1 and this research track should therefore retain separate eligibility rules and claims.
tables: Qualified early observations, declared assay clock, organism and drug context, and quality records.

pages.title: A20 MIC estimation research
text: **A20 · Research target for quantitative inference**

MIC estimation research asks whether a defined set of observations can support a useful prediction of a method-specific MIC. The output is a prediction, not a direct broth microdilution measurement. A disk-zone diameter does not contain a universally invertible mapping to a precise MIC across organisms, drugs and conditions.
## Preserve the reference method

Reference MIC data should retain method, dilution structure, off-scale results and quality context. A model should not turn an interval-censored or off-scale reference into an invented exact value. Units such as milligrams per litre must remain explicit.

The proposed output should be visibly labelled predicted and should not overwrite a measured result. Any future clinical use would require a bounded intended use and its own validation. Direct MIC testing through a qualified assay remains a different product function, even when both outputs can be stored in the same PIMS environment.

topics.title: AI for multimodal learning and model quality
text: **A21 · Proposed multimodal research representation**

pages.title: A21 Multimodal representation learning
text: **A21 · Proposed multimodal research representation**

Multimodal representation learning combines information from different observation channels into features useful for a defined task. It can model relationships that are difficult to express manually. Its value depends on whether the channels add relevant information and whether their timing, calibration and missingness are understood.
## Demonstrate complementarity

A combined model should be compared with its strongest single-channel baseline. Removing each channel can reveal whether it contributes useful information or merely increases complexity. The evaluation should also challenge common-cause disturbances that can affect several channels at once.

The representation itself is not a biological result. Its downstream use must be defined and evaluated. A fused score should retain the original observations and their quality states so that a reviewer can investigate why the result changed after a sensor fault, configuration change or reprocessing. Unqualified signals should not gain credibility merely by entering a larger model.
tables: Qualified images and sensor observations with units, intervals, calibration and quality states.
Task-specific representation, contributing channels and a bounded downstream prediction.
Explicit feature concatenation, simple statistical models and single-modality comparisons.
Nonlinear relationships and interactions among complementary signals.
Synchronized representative data, controlled confounders and enough independent cases for the model complexity.
Learning site or batch identity, relying on a shortcut channel or failing when a modality is missing.
Held-out task performance, modality ablation, missing-channel tests and cross-site transfer.

pages.title: A22 Sensor disagreement detection
text: **A22 · Proposed disagreement and fault assessment**

Sensor disagreement detection identifies observations that are inconsistent with their expected relationship. AI may learn normal cross-channel patterns and highlight unusual residuals. The detected discrepancy can have several explanations, including a sensor fault, timing error, changed environment or an inadequate model.
## Disagreement does not identify the truth

If two channels disagree, the model should not automatically choose the one that resembles its training data. The investigation should consider calibration, timing, location and what each channel measures. A third channel helps only if it contributes sufficiently independent information.

The proposed output should support a defined recovery path. Some events may justify excluding a failed auxiliary sensor; others may invalidate the whole observation. These paths need separate evaluation. A system that detects a discrepancy but still releases the same unsupported conclusion has not achieved the intended error-reduction function.
tables: Sensor observations, independent quality checks, synchronization information and expected relationships.
Disagreement event, affected channels, supporting residuals and uncertainty.
Physical consistency rules, calibrated residual thresholds and independent reference checks.

Missing common-cause errors, overflagging legitimate differences or identifying the wrong channel as faulty.
Fault-specific detection, false alarms, detection delay and correct escalation or abstention.

pages.title: A23 Missing modality handling
text: **A23 · Proposed missing-data handling**

Missing-modality handling determines what analysis remains justified when one or more expected channels are unavailable. AI may support a qualified reduced-input model or a research imputation, but neither should be represented as if the missing sensor produced a real observation.
## Missingness has a cause

A channel absent because a sample is outside its range may contain different information from a channel absent because a cable disconnected. The model should not assume those events are equivalent. The original reason should remain part of the record.

For a clinical workflow, only separately qualified degraded modes should be eligible. Research imputation can be useful for model exploration or sensitivity analysis, but it should carry an imputed value type and a link to the method. It must not fill gaps in the original measured series or conceal that the biological observation was never acquired.
tables: Available channels, explicit missingness reasons, quality states and intended task.

Treating informative missingness as random, hiding a sensor failure or promoting imputation to measured evidence.

pages.title: A24 Out of distribution detection
text: **A24 · Proposed domain suitability assessment**

Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input differs materially from the domain in which a model was developed and evaluated. No detector can guarantee recognition of every unfamiliar case. Its role is to provide an additional signal for review and abstention, alongside explicit eligibility checks.
## Domain is more than appearance

A familiar-looking plate can still have an unsupported organism, drug, medium or reading time. Those conditions require explicit context checks. Conversely, an unfamiliar background may not affect the measurement if the relevant evidence remains qualified.

The proposed system should combine domain indicators with task-specific quality assessment. Evaluation should include new sites, instruments, vessel types and workflow conditions without using them to tune the detector after seeing the final test results. A novelty score should be explained through its tested operational meaning, not presented as a universal measure of biological uncertainty.
tables: Images, metadata, model representations and declared training or validation domain.
Domain-suitability indicators, relevant differences and an uncertain or unsupported state.

Shift-specific detection, accepted-case error, coverage and transfer to unseen shift types.

pages.title: A25 Confidence calibration
text: **A25 · Proposed confidence calibration**

Confidence calibration examines whether a model’s stated confidence corresponds to observed performance. A model can rank easy and difficult cases well while still assigning misleading probabilities. Calibration should be evaluated separately from discrimination and should remain specific to the task and population.
## Confidence is not a permission rule by itself

A high calibrated probability still needs to be interpreted against the consequence of error, the intended use and the availability of review. A low-confidence output may require another observation or an established alternative workflow.

Calibration should be reassessed when the model, acquisition pipeline or data distribution changes materially. The record should identify the calibration method and dataset version. A display should avoid false precision: a percentage with several decimal places does not communicate more useful certainty if the supporting evaluation is limited. The purpose is an empirically meaningful uncertainty statement that helps the user make an appropriate decision.
tables: Model outputs, independent reference outcomes and relevant population or quality strata.
Calibrated probabilities or intervals, calibration diagnostics and applicability limits.
Held-out empirical reliability analysis and simple post-processing calibration methods.
Conditional uncertainty models where error behaviour varies with image or workflow features.
Independent calibration data and a separate final evaluation set with sufficient event counts.
Reusing test data, hiding subgroup miscalibration or assuming calibration survives domain shift.
Reliability curves, suitable scoring rules, interval coverage and subgroup analysis.

pages.title: A26 Active data selection
text: **A26 · Proposed data acquisition support**

Active data selection prioritizes examples that may be useful for improving a model or resolving a known evidence gap. AI can identify uncertainty, diversity or disagreement patterns, but its selection can also bias the resulting dataset. A representative evaluation set must remain independent of that process.
## Preserve the sampling story

A dataset enriched for difficult cases is useful for development but may not estimate routine prevalence or workflow performance. Its selection policy should therefore accompany the data. Researchers should be able to reconstruct why a record entered the training set.

The proposed function should support expert-led collection decisions rather than autonomously expand data use. Privacy, consent and partner permissions still apply. A model should not request patient-linked data merely because an uncertainty score is high. The collection plan should identify the minimum information needed to answer the development question and maintain separate evaluation data for the final claim.

pages.title: A27 Annotation quality assistance
text: **A27 · Proposed annotation quality assistance**

Annotation assistance identifies potentially inconsistent, incomplete or difficult labels for human review. AI may compare annotations with image features or with related records. Its role is to surface questions, not to replace independent reference labels with the model’s preferred answer.
## Avoid circular ground truth

If a model’s prediction becomes the label used to evaluate the same model, apparent agreement can improve without any improvement in truth. The annotation process should preserve who saw which information and when. Blinded review is important where it supports the selected evaluation design.

The proposed interface should present the original evidence, competing annotations and the relevant instructions. An adjudicator should be able to retain uncertainty rather than being forced to choose a precise value. Quality assistance succeeds when it improves the reliability and transparency of the reference process, not when it makes the dataset look more consistent with the current model.

pages.title: A28 Dataset shift monitoring
text: **A28 · Proposed distribution monitoring**

Dataset shift monitoring tracks changes in the observations or populations encountered by a deployed or research system. AI may summarize complex image or feature distributions, while explicit metadata can reveal changes in instruments, sites or workflows. A detected shift does not automatically mean performance has degraded.
## Connect an alert to a review process

The proposed response should identify who investigates, what additional evidence is needed and whether any workflow restriction is justified. Automatic retraining should not be the default reaction, because it can introduce new unvalidated behaviour.

Monitoring should preserve privacy and site context. Aggregated statistics may support an investigation without transferring patient-linked records. Changes in data availability or review practice can also alter monitored distributions and should be recorded. The objective is early recognition of a meaningful change and a controlled response, not an uninterrupted stream of novelty alerts.

pages.title: A29 Sequence quality triage
text: **A29 · Proposed sequence-data triage**

Sequence quality triage helps determine whether molecular data are suitable for a proposed downstream analysis. AI may identify complex quality patterns, but established pipeline checks and explicit metadata should remain central. The task concerns the quality of measured sequence data, not inference of a sequence from a plate image.
## Preserve the molecular provenance

The record should retain accession or file identity, tool versions, reference data and the quality decisions made. A later database or pipeline update should produce a new analysis version. NCBI documentation provides a basis for understanding the context and limitations of its sequence-based resources. [R25]

This proposed capability belongs to the bioinformatics product track. It should not silently reject or alter measured molecular data. Where quality is insufficient, the output should identify the limitation and the analysis it affects, allowing a qualified user to decide whether additional evidence or a different workflow is required.

pages.title: A30 Resistance gene evidence retrieval
text: **A30 · Proposed resistance-evidence analysis**

Resistance-gene evidence retrieval connects qualified molecular observations with curated knowledge about resistance determinants. The function may combine sequence-analysis outputs with structured evidence retrieval. It should preserve the distinction between a detected sequence feature, a database annotation and a clinically expressed phenotype.
## Keep the evidence chain visible

CARD and NCBI resources offer different forms of resistance-related information. The proposed system should identify the resource and version used, the analysis method and the exact molecular input. It should not describe a database hit as a new laboratory measurement. [R24] [R25]

The initial role is research and qualified molecular-result support. An absent match does not prove susceptibility, and a present determinant does not by itself establish every clinical consequence. The interface should preserve these limits and direct discrepancies to review rather than resolving them through an unsupported single confidence score.

topics.title: AI for review, operations and assistance
text: **A31 · Proposed phenotype and genotype reconciliation**

pages.title: A31 Phenotype genotype discrepancy review
text: **A31 · Proposed phenotype and genotype reconciliation**

A measured susceptibility phenotype and a molecular finding answer different questions. A discrepancy may reflect expression, an unrepresented mechanism, assay conditions, mixed populations, sample identity or an error in either workflow. The proposed capability organizes these explanations for expert review; it does not decide that one evidence class always overrides the other.
## Preserve the direction of inference

A sequence-derived mechanism prediction should identify the detection method and reference knowledge used. A phenotype-derived hypothesis about a gene remains an inference even when it resembles a known association. Database evidence can support interpretation, but it cannot supply a molecular measurement that was never performed. [R24] [R25]

The review interface should display both original records, not a merged value that conceals disagreement. Proposed actions may include checking sample identity, reviewing assay quality or obtaining an appropriate confirmatory investigation. Clinical reporting rules remain separately controlled. Performance assessment should include discrepancies that the system cannot explain, because honest unresolved cases are preferable to convincing invented mechanisms.

pages.title: A32 Genomic similarity research
text: **A32 · Proposed genomic similarity research**

Genomic similarity analysis can support research into related isolates and population structure. Similarity depends on the chosen representation, sequence coverage, organism and comparison method. It is not by itself proof of transmission, common exposure or identical susceptibility.
## Similarity requires context

An embedding distance is a model output, not a universal genetic distance. Its interpretation must be established for the organism group and use case. The platform should retain the sequence-analysis pipeline, reference collection snapshot and thresholds used to generate a relationship. Public repository access must follow the repository's terms and data-use conditions. [R25]

An authorized research workspace could place phenotypic observations beside genomic relationships to explore hypotheses. Patient-level epidemiological conclusions require additional information, appropriate governance and expert assessment. The proposed software should therefore distinguish a computational cluster from an investigated outbreak, and it should avoid presenting either as a demonstrated AMReye.AI clinical capability.

pages.title: A33 Literature evidence retrieval
text: **A33 · Proposed literature evidence retrieval**

Evidence retrieval helps a reviewer find relevant studies, methods and limitations. AI may expand terminology, rank passages and organize contradictory findings. It should operate over identifiable sources and show what was actually retrieved, rather than generating citations from linguistic plausibility.
## Separate retrieval from authority

A search result is a candidate source. Study design, specimen context, comparator, sample size and limitations determine what the source can support. A vendor performance statement, an original clinical study and a laboratory proof of concept should not receive the same evidentiary weight merely because they share keywords.

The interface should record the search date and query, distinguish full-text review from abstract access and expose unresolved contradictions. Generated summaries require source checking before external use. Standards questions should point to the controlled standards service, because a language model's recollection is unsuitable for selecting clinical interpretation rules. The retrieval system is a research aid with its own measurable failure rate.

pages.title: A34 Standards rule consistency checking
text: **A34 · Proposed standards consistency assistance**

Standards interpretation should be implemented through a versioned, testable rules service. AI can assist with finding inconsistent mappings, missing metadata or unexpected changes during expert review. It should not improvise breakpoints or silently reinterpret a result when a new document appears. [R01] [R02]
## The rules service remains authoritative

An assistance output should be a review item, not an executable change. Promotion of a correction requires an authorized reviewer, a controlled source and regression tests. Historical reports retain their original interpretation and rule version; a later reinterpretation becomes a linked event with a reason.

Rapid methods deserve separate namespaces and eligibility checks. A routine endpoint threshold must not be substituted into an early reading because the organism and antimicrobial names match. The evaluation should deliberately include missing organism information, unsupported combinations, unit errors and superseded corrections. An explicit unavailable interpretation is the appropriate result when required scope information cannot be established. [R04] [R05]

pages.title: A35 Reviewer workload prioritization
text: **A35 · Proposed reviewer workload prioritization**

Review prioritization organizes work according to defined laboratory policies, technical uncertainty and operational urgency. Its purpose is to help qualified staff attend to cases efficiently while preserving every case's required review. It should not create an invisible queue in which difficult or unfamiliar samples are indefinitely deferred.
## Operational advice needs boundaries

A predicted review duration is an operational estimate. It is not a measure of clinical severity. Any use of clinical urgency must follow the laboratory's authorized policy and data permissions. The queue should make aging visible and provide a deterministic maximum-delay escalation independent of the model.

Evaluation should compare the proposed ordering with a simple baseline under realistic arrival patterns and staff availability. Average turnaround alone can conceal poor service for a smaller case group. Report tail delays and unresolved counts as well. If the model becomes unavailable, staff should retain a complete, intelligible queue and a predictable manual ordering method.

pages.title: A36 Inventory and consumable forecasting
text: **A36 · Proposed inventory and consumable forecasting**

Consumable forecasting estimates future demand to support laboratory planning. The useful unit may be a disk, plate, calibration material, replacement component or service kit. The forecast must account for expiry and compatible use, because an apparently adequate stock count can still be unusable for the scheduled work.
## Recommendations are not purchases

The software should expose the assumptions behind a planning quantity, including the service period and uncertainty. Approval, supplier qualification and purchasing remain controlled business processes. No automatic order should arise merely because an AI forecast crosses a threshold.

Laboratories with limited history need a simple, inspectable baseline and conservative uncertainty. Data from another site may help only when workload and procurement conditions are comparable. A forecast should be revised when a method changes its consumable mix. The original forecast and subsequent actual consumption should remain available so that apparent improvements can be assessed without retrospectively rewriting the prediction.

pages.title: A37 Predictive maintenance
text: **A37 · Proposed predictive maintenance**

Predictive maintenance estimates whether instrument condition is deteriorating before a functional failure occurs. Candidate inputs include illumination stability, focus actuator behavior, temperature excursions, fan performance and repeated acquisition faults. The model should support service decisions without overriding mandatory calibration or safety checks.
## A service label must be trustworthy

Replacing a component does not prove that the component caused the original fault. Service records should distinguish suspected causes from findings confirmed by inspection or testing. Models trained on ambiguous repair labels can learn misleading associations.

The proposed system should retain deterministic limits for conditions that require immediate action. A low predicted risk cannot waive an overdue calibration or an electrical fault. For Reader V1, basic fault logging and stable maintenance procedures are more credible initial functions than precise remaining-life estimates. Advanced forecasts become useful only after sufficient field evidence establishes their reliability across instrument revisions and operating environments.

pages.title: A38 Energy and acquisition scheduling
text: **A38 · Proposed energy and acquisition scheduling**

Acquisition scheduling chooses when and how to collect observations within a qualified workflow. AI may allocate computation or suggest research sampling times that capture informative changes. The optimization must respect biological timing, thermal stability, illumination exposure and required quality checks.
## Optimize within the method

For endpoint Reader V1, an optimization may concern processing and queue management after a valid acquisition. It should not modify the biological method to save energy. Adaptive temporal sampling belongs to a separately evaluated research workflow, especially when the timing of growth observations affects the conclusion.

The scheduler must record the observations it intentionally omitted and why. A forecast cannot retroactively replace those measurements. On loss of cloud connectivity, the device needs a defined local schedule that preserves required operations. Evaluation should include workload bursts and degraded power conditions, because a policy optimized only for average conditions may fail at the moment reliability matters most.

pages.title: A39 Fleet quality surveillance
text: **A39 · Proposed fleet quality surveillance**

Fleet surveillance compares instrument quality indicators across deployments to identify emerging problems. A coordinated view may reveal a drifting illumination batch, a software regression or an unusual calibration pattern. Cross-site comparison is meaningful only after accounting for configuration, workload and environmental differences.
## Aggregation does not remove governance

The smallest useful data set should be selected for the surveillance question. A service engineer may need a reference-image metric and instrument version without needing patient identifiers or biological images. Access rights and retention should follow the purpose of each data flow.

A fleet alert should trigger investigation through the quality system. It should not silently change local measurement algorithms. Corrective actions require assessment of affected records, release controls and deployment verification. Independent sites should retain essential local functions during a central outage, while the central record later reconciles event timing and versions without overwriting the original local history.

pages.title: A40 Natural language workflow assistance
text: **A40 · Proposed natural language workflow assistance**

A language interface can help authorized users locate records, understand software messages and navigate documented procedures. Its practical value is reduced interaction burden. It should distinguish information retrieval from actions that alter records, interpretations or access permissions.
## Keep consequential actions explicit

The assistant should identify the intended record and show the exact proposed change before a consequential action. Retrieved text is data, not permission to execute instructions. Approval should come from the authenticated user with the appropriate role, through the same controls as the conventional interface.

Clinical interpretation should remain in the qualified measurement and standards workflow. The assistant may explain why a record is awaiting review, but it should not invent a susceptibility category or approve its own explanation. Voice, mobile and touchless access can use this interaction layer only after usability, environmental noise, authentication and error-recovery behavior are evaluated for the intended setting. [R22] [R23]

topics.title: Digital plate records and computational models
text: **The durable representation of an observed plate**

pages.title: The digital plate record
text: **The durable representation of an observed plate**

The digital plate record is the foundation of the proposed simulation system. It stores observations, identity, timing, calibration, handling events and reviewer decisions. A record can be valuable without a predictive model: it allows a laboratory to revisit what was observed and to understand how a reported measurement was produced.
## What belongs in the record

Each acquisition should retain its original file, a content integrity value, device configuration and the time interval over which the signal was acquired. Measurements derived from an image should link to that image and to the calibration and algorithm versions used. A corrected boundary becomes a new measurement event associated with the reviewer and reason.

The record should distinguish physical identity, direct observations, derived measurements, qualified interpretations and simulations. These layers answer different questions: which object was observed, what was recorded, what analysis calculated, what the reviewed workflow concluded and what a model estimates beyond observation.
## Preservation is a product capability

The stored record should remain intelligible if the original instrument is replaced or a model is retired. This requires documented formats, units, reference identifiers and an export path. Retaining only a screenshot of a final result would lose information needed for investigation and reanalysis.

The record does not become a predictive twin merely because it contains many sensors or a three-dimensional visualization. Prediction requires an explicit model, a defined question and evidence that the model can answer that question within a stated domain. Those additional requirements are developed throughout this part.
!FIG work/assets/figures/record-model-twin.png | Three linked representations with distinct evidentiary roles. Original conceptual diagram.

pages.title: From record to computational model
text: **A model turns a question into a calculation**

A computational model represents selected features of a physical system using mathematical rules or learned relationships. It may describe an optical measurement, the expansion of a colony or the distribution of an antimicrobial in a medium. Its scope should follow the question; a detailed rendering of an enclosure does not necessarily improve a biological forecast.
## Define the quantity of interest

For AMReye.AI research, candidate quantities include visible colony area, a spatial growth probability, a time to a defined observation threshold or a forecast distribution of an image-derived measurement. These quantities differ from susceptibility categories and require separate validation before any clinical interpretation is considered.

The same image may support several models, but each needs a separate output identity. An estimated biomass should not be relabelled as a measured viable count. A model can fit the observed past while being unsuitable for extrapolation, particularly when multiple parameter combinations explain the same early trajectory.
## Start with a baseline

A constant-value forecast or a simple growth curve establishes whether a more complex model adds information. Complexity should be justified by improved predictive performance, useful uncertainty and practical interpretability. The proposed platform should preserve baseline results alongside experimental models during development, making improvement testable rather than assumed.

pages.title: Requirements for a predictive twin
text: **A predictive twin must remain connected to evidence**

The proposed predictive twin is a computational representation linked to a particular physical plate, updated when qualified observations arrive and used to answer a bounded forecasting question. A general probabilistic twin framework has been demonstrated in engineering research; transferring that idea to microbiological plates requires new biological evidence. [R59]
## Minimum functional contract

The twin should identify its physical counterpart, current model version, last accepted observation, estimated state and permitted prediction horizon. It should also describe the conditions under which updating is suspended. An image rejected for identity or calibration failure should not automatically adjust the biological state.
## Bidirectional use needs an additional gate

A twin might eventually recommend a further observation or a virtual experiment. Any action that changes the physical assay, such as adjusting incubation or exposure, needs its own validation and control path. A simulation service should not gain authority over an instrument simply because the two exchange data.

Reader V1 can establish the record and measurement foundations before a predictive twin is available. This sequence supports future research while keeping the initial product proposition credible. The twin's maturity should be assessed by its validated forecasting domain, not the number of simulated images it can generate or the visual realism of its interface.

pages.title: A state space view of plate development
text: **State evolution and observation are different processes**

A state-space formulation separates biological development from the process used to observe it. Let xₖ represent the latent state at time tₖ, uₖ the recorded inputs and θ the model parameters. A proposed discrete representation is:
**xₖ₊₁ = f(xₖ, uₖ, Δtₖ; θ) + wₖ**
**yₖ = h(xₖ, cₖ) + vₖ**

Here yₖ is an observation, cₖ describes calibration or capture conditions, wₖ represents unresolved process variation and vₖ represents observation error. The equations are a modelling scaffold, not an implemented AMReye.AI algorithm. Vector components may have different units and therefore need explicit scaling and covariance definitions.
## Choose interpretable states where possible

A simple research state might contain visible occupied area and a growth-rate parameter. A richer state could represent local population density, nutrient availability or antimicrobial concentration. Including an unobservable state adds assumptions; it does not make that quantity measured.

State variables must remain within their defined ranges. Missing temperature intervals cannot be assumed constant without an explicit assumption. Segmented area in mm² retains image and segmentation uncertainty. Process variation should describe unresolved biological changes rather than absorb every instrument defect.

The model should use actual elapsed time, especially when acquisition intervals vary. Numerical propagation over a long gap may require smaller internal steps than the observation interval. Testing should challenge irregular timing, abrupt input changes and boundary conditions before the representation is used to support forecasts.
!FIG work/assets/figures/state-observation.png | State propagation and observation mapping. Arrows represent model dependencies, not fixed hardware connections.

pages.title: Observation models and sensor likelihoods
text: **The observation model connects biology to a sensor**

An observation likelihood describes the probability of obtaining a signal for a given model state and capture condition. This connection is essential because cameras, gas sensors and electrical probes measure different physical effects. Their outputs should not be treated as interchangeable estimates of bacterial abundance.
## Examples of observation relationships

For an image, a forward model may include illumination, object geometry, optical blur, sampling and sensor noise. A simplified model might instead relate segmented area to a latent occupancy state. For a gas channel, the relationship may additionally depend on chamber mixing, background atmosphere and transport delay.
## Avoid double counting

Two features extracted from the same image often share errors. Treating them as independent can produce an unjustifiably narrow posterior distribution. A model should account for shared image quality, calibration and preprocessing where these materially affect the output.

Observation models need calibration data that distinguish sensor behavior from biological variation. A stable optical target can help assess image formation, while it cannot establish the relation between image appearance and viability. The proposed system should retain both types of evidence and identify which relationship each experiment actually tests.
tables: A bounded or censored likelihood may be more suitable than an unrestricted error model.

pages.title: Time origins and biological age
text: **Clock time is not automatically biological age**

A forecast needs an explicit time origin. Specimen collection, inoculation, antimicrobial exposure, incubation entry and first image are different events. A trajectory indexed only by file creation time can conceal a long and variable period of biological development before the first observation.
## Proposed temporal record

Each event should carry a timestamp, time zone or UTC representation, precision and provenance. Device clocks also need a synchronization status. If an operator enters an approximate time, the record should preserve that approximation rather than displaying false second-level precision.
## Timing uncertainty propagates

In a rapidly changing phase, uncertainty about when growth began may dominate uncertainty about an image-derived area. A model fitted to a single early image cannot always distinguish a larger initial population from a longer unobserved growth period. The resulting ambiguity should widen the forecast or limit the permitted question.

For a sub-two-hour research target, the clock origin must be stated before evaluation. Reporting time from first image when the intended claim concerns specimen-to-result time would omit preparation and prior incubation. The platform should preserve multiple workflow intervals so that speed can be assessed honestly for each intended use, including unsuccessful and delayed cases.

pages.title: Spatial representations of plate growth
text: **Represent the spatial feature that matters**

Plate growth can be represented as a continuous field, a grid of local measurements, a set of segmented objects or a graph of tracked colonies. These representations trade spatial detail against data requirements and computational cost. A whole-plate average can conceal a small localized event that matters to heteroresistance research.
## Candidate representations

An occupancy map describes where visible growth is present. An object representation records individual boundaries, locations and tracking identities. A radial profile can summarize an approximately circular inhibition pattern, but its validity decreases when the boundary is irregular or neighboring zones interact.
## Coordinate systems are part of the evidence

Spatial observations should refer to a plate coordinate system with units and a transform from image coordinates. Registration uncertainty should accompany comparisons across time. If the plate rotates or shifts, a stationary pixel does not represent a stationary biological location.

The proposed model should retain access to original images even when a reduced representation is used for computation. A reviewer may need to inspect a location excluded by the segmentation. Spatial compression should therefore be evaluated against the intended research question, including rare local features, rather than judged only by average reconstruction quality.

pages.title: Population growth model families
text: **Growth curves are hypotheses with domains**

Population models provide compact descriptions of change. An exponential model, dN/dt = μN, represents growth at a constant specific rate μ. A logistic form, dN/dt = μN(1 − N/K), adds a limiting level K. These equations are illustrative mathematical baselines; neither automatically describes the visible area, viability or antimicrobial response of a real plate.
## Map the variable before fitting

If N denotes cell number, its units and measurement basis differ from a normalized image intensity. An image-derived proxy may have a nonlinear relationship to population size, especially after objects overlap or the detector saturates. Fitting the same equation to different proxies does not give the fitted parameters the same biological meaning.
## Early agreement can hide later divergence

Several curves may fit the first observations almost equally well but imply very different later behavior. A one-day record therefore does not establish that the remaining days can be reconstructed reliably. The useful forecast horizon depends on the organism, assay, conditions and output.

The research programme should compare model families prospectively on withheld future observations. Reporting only goodness of fit to the observed past would not test forecasting. Parameters should retain uncertainty and correlation, particularly when the observed period covers only a small part of the proposed growth trajectory.

pages.title: Diffusion and spatial transport models
text: **Transport models connect location, time and exposure**
Spatial antimicrobial exposure can be explored with transport equations. An illustrative reaction–diffusion form is:

Here c is concentration, D is an effective diffusion coefficient and r represents a specified loss or reaction term. If distance is expressed in mm and time in hours, D has units mm²/h. The equation is a research starting point, not a calibrated disk-diffusion model for AMReye.AI.
## Boundary and initial conditions matter

A simulation requires a description of the initial distribution and the behavior at the domain boundaries. Disk release, agar properties, geometry and environmental history may influence the modeled exposure. A visually plausible gradient is insufficient evidence that the concentration field is correct.
## Do not reverse a clinical method casually

An observed zone diameter does not uniquely identify the underlying concentration history or a minimum inhibitory concentration. Different parameter combinations can produce similar visible boundaries. Inferring an MIC from a simulated field is therefore a separate research claim requiring a suitable reference method and validation.

A useful first application may be sensitivity analysis: determining which uncertain transport assumptions most affect a proposed observation schedule. Such a study can inform experiment design without claiming that the simulation replaces an established susceptibility method.

pages.title: Mechanistic and learned hybrid models
text: **Hybrid models combine constraints and learned relationships**

A hybrid model uses mechanistic structure for some processes and learned components for others. For example, a transport calculation might describe a spatial input while a learned observation model relates local state to image features. Another design could use a simple growth equation with a bounded, data-driven residual term.
## Define responsibility at each boundary

The mechanistic component should declare its assumptions and parameter units. The learned component should declare its training domain and output constraints. Their combined uncertainty is not necessarily the sum of two independent errors, because the components may have been fitted to the same data.
## Preserve meaningful constraints

Nonnegative quantities, bounded occupancy and causal timing can be enforced where the underlying definition requires them. Constraints reduce some implausible behavior but do not prove that the model is biologically correct. A perfectly smooth, nonnegative trajectory can still make an inaccurate forecast.

Evaluation should compare the hybrid with both its mechanistic baseline and a suitable purely empirical model. The comparison needs held-out conditions and an explicit computational cost measure. A more elaborate model is justified when it offers a demonstrated advantage for the intended question, such as better calibrated forecasts or useful transfer with limited data, while preserving an intelligible route for investigating failure.

topics.title: Prediction, uncertainty and observation continuity
text: **A fitted parameter is not always identifiable**

pages.title: Parameter identifiability
text: **A fitted parameter is not always identifiable**

Identifiability concerns whether the available observations can determine a model's parameters. Structural identifiability asks what could be determined with ideal data under the model. Practical identifiability concerns the actual sampling, noise and observed time span. Both matter before a fitted parameter is given a biological interpretation.
## An illustrative ambiguity

In N(t) = N₀ exp(μt), a single value of N at a known time cannot determine both the initial level N₀ and growth rate μ. Multiple pairs can produce the same observation. Additional time points may help, but an uncertain time origin introduces another source of ambiguity.
## Design observations to distinguish explanations

A new sensor is valuable when it helps resolve a relevant ambiguity. Measuring an independent environmental input may be more informative than adding another feature from the same image. Experimental design should therefore consider parameter sensitivity and expected information, not just the number of channels.

For the proposed twin, parameter estimates should retain uncertainty and the data interval used to estimate them. A precise-looking best fit should not conceal a broad set of plausible alternatives. If different parameter sets lead to incompatible future decisions, the appropriate outcome is a shorter horizon, an additional observation or an unresolved research result.

pages.title: State estimation from sparse observations
text: **Sparse data require disciplined updating**

State estimation combines prior information, a process model and new observations. Candidate methods include deterministic optimization, filtering and sequential sampling. The choice depends on nonlinearity, the form of uncertainty and computational constraints. No estimation method can recover information that the data and assumptions do not contain.
## Proposed update sequence

The platform should first validate identity, timing and observation quality. It then predicts the state to the observation time, evaluates the new signal under the observation model and updates the state distribution. Finally, it records diagnostics and determines whether forecasting remains eligible.
## A large residual needs investigation

An unexpected observation may reveal new biological behavior, a changed environment, an incorrect identity or an instrument fault. Automatically forcing the model through every observation can hide these problems. Conversely, rejecting every surprising point can prevent the model from recognizing a real change.

The proposed update policy should make these alternatives explicit. A quarantine state can preserve a disputed observation while stopping its use in downstream predictions. Research comparisons should include sparse and irregular schedules that resemble actual operation. Randomly deleting isolated images from an otherwise complete series is only one missing-data scenario and does not represent every real interruption.

pages.title: Forecasting beyond the last image
text: **A future trajectory is a conditional prediction**

Forecasting propagates a model beyond the last accepted observation. The output is conditional on the estimated state, parameters and assumed future inputs. If temperature, atmosphere or handling changes after observation stops, a forecast based on unchanged conditions may no longer apply.
## Preserve the forecast origin

Each prediction should identify the last real observation and the exact time at which the forecast was issued. Later observations can evaluate that prediction, but they must not be used to revise its historical score. A revised forecast is a new record.
## One day observed does not guarantee later days

The proposed capability may investigate whether a limited observation period supports useful forecasts over a longer period. It should test each horizon against genuinely withheld future measurements. Performance can deteriorate after a growth transition, a previously unseen morphology or a change in the relevant environment.

Generated images may illustrate a predicted state, but visual realism is not a forecast metric. Evaluation should use the defined biological or image-derived quantity and its uncertainty. The interface should show measured observations with a different visual encoding from simulated continuation, and exports should retain the distinction in machine-readable fields as well as captions.

pages.title: The prediction horizon
text: **A horizon is a validated limit, not a display preference**

The prediction horizon is the future interval over which a forecast is permitted for a particular use. Its useful length depends on the output, acceptable error, input uncertainty and model domain. Different quantities from the same twin may have different horizons.
## Define a horizon policy

A research programme should prespecify performance requirements at several future intervals. These may include a maximum error, interval calibration, a minimum useful coverage and an eligibility domain. The permitted horizon should be the longest interval supported by those requirements, not the furthest point that the solver can calculate.
## Horizon evaluation must include failures

It is misleading to report long-horizon accuracy only for cases where the model happened to remain confident. The evaluation should show the proportion of all eligible cases receiving a forecast at each horizon and the error among those accepted. Rejected and unavailable cases remain in the accounting.

A forecast should expire when its intended use or input assumptions cease to apply. Expiry does not delete the simulation; it changes what the result is allowed to support. For continuity after a lost plate, an exploratory trajectory may remain available beyond the qualified horizon, but it must be visibly outside validated predictive use and excluded from laboratory result release.

pages.title: Uncertainty propagation
text: **Uncertainty passes through the entire calculation**

Measurement noise, calibration, time origin, model parameters and future inputs all contribute to forecast uncertainty. Propagating only the final model's statistical variance can omit dominant sources. Shared errors also matter: two measurements using the same spatial calibration are not independent simply because they came from different images. [R16]
## An illustrative measurement calculation
If a diameter is calculated as d = sp, where s is scale in mm/pixel and p is a pixel diameter, a first-order variance approximation is:
**Var(d) ≈ p²Var(s) + s²Var(p) + 2sp Cov(s, p)**
The covariance term vanishes only when independence is justified. This equation illustrates propagation for one measurement; it does not quantify an AMReye.AI instrument's uncertainty.
## Use intervals that answer the question

A confidence interval for an estimated mean differs from a prediction interval for a future observation. The latter must account for future variation relevant to the defined outcome. Interval labels should state their meaning and nominal probability.

Monte Carlo propagation can handle nonlinear relationships when the input distributions are defensible. More simulation draws reduce numerical sampling error; they do not correct missing uncertainty sources or invalid assumptions. The report should identify which uncertainties were included, which were bounded and which remain unquantified.

pages.title: Aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty
text: **Different uncertainties call for different remedies**

Aleatoric uncertainty describes variation represented as inherent randomness in the chosen model, such as variability among otherwise comparable observations. Epistemic uncertainty concerns limited knowledge, including poorly estimated parameters or an inadequate model. The distinction depends on the model and available information; it is not a permanent label attached to a phenomenon.
## Decide what additional information could help

Repeated measurements can characterize some observation variation. A better calibration may reduce uncertainty about scale. Additional laboratories can reveal a domain limitation that repeated measurements at one site would miss. An extra sensor helps only if it addresses an uncertainty relevant to the prediction.
## Do not interpret confidence as certainty

A model can produce a narrow interval when its assumptions are wrong. Agreement among several models can also be misleading if they share training data, features or structural omissions. Confidence should therefore be assessed against independent outcomes and challenged under plausible shifts.

For the proposed twin, the user interface should explain the dominant reason for uncertainty where that reason is known. “Insufficient recent observation” suggests a different response from “unsupported organism–assay combination.” A generic confidence percentage without those distinctions would provide less useful guidance and could encourage overinterpretation.

pages.title: Forecast calibration and scoring
text: **Score the forecast that existed before the outcome**

Forecast evaluation compares predictions issued at a defined origin with later independent observations. A rolling-origin design repeats this process at several prespecified points in a trajectory. The training process must not see the future observations used for scoring, including through normalization, parameter tuning or selection of an apparently successful horizon.
## Evaluate accuracy and uncertainty together

Point metrics such as absolute error describe a central prediction. Interval coverage checks how often an interval contains the defined future outcome. Interval width describes precision. A very broad interval can achieve high coverage while being operationally unhelpful, so both should be reported.
## Avoid a favorable average concealing failure

Repeated predictions from the same plate are correlated. Treating them as independent samples can overstate precision. Statistical analysis should preserve the plate or isolate grouping and the study's sampling structure. Results should also include cases with interrupted observation, because continuity is an explicit product research objective.

Model selection and final evaluation need separate data. A model that was repeatedly adjusted after viewing the test trajectories has effectively trained on them. The proposed programme should preserve a frozen evaluation set or a prospective evaluation period, with the analysis plan and model version recorded before outcomes are examined.

pages.title: Missing observation intervals
text: **A gap remains a gap in the measured series**

Missing observations can arise from scheduled omission, failed acquisition, network delay, physical handling or loss of the sample. These causes carry different information. The proposed record should preserve the expected observation, its status and the reason it is absent wherever that reason is known.
## Distinguish delayed data from absent data

A locally acquired image may arrive at the server late. That is different from an image never captured. The server should use the acquisition time for biological analysis and the receipt time for operational auditing. Backdated ingestion must not make a historical forecast appear to have used information that arrived later.
## Evaluate the return of observation

When a real observation resumes, compare it with the earlier forecast before updating the model. A large discrepancy may require investigation rather than immediate assimilation. The historical prediction remains available for scoring even if the new observation produces a better state estimate.

Missingness tests should include long contiguous outages, failures associated with poor image quality and unrecorded environmental changes. An algorithm that performs well when random frames are removed may still fail when all missing observations occur during condensation or rapid biological change. The proposed validation should reflect those mechanisms explicitly.
