pages.title: Dataset representativeness
text: **Representativeness is a property of the intended domain**

A validation collection should reflect the conditions under which the product is expected to work. Relevant dimensions include organisms, antimicrobial combinations, media, plate geometry, image quality, sites, users and clinically important result ranges. A large dataset can still be narrow if most observations come from similar cases.
## Build a coverage matrix

The proposed study should map intended-use dimensions to available cases and identify gaps before model training and final evaluation. Rare but consequential conditions may need deliberate enrichment. Their prevalence in the evaluation collection should be reported so that overall metrics are interpreted correctly.
## More images are not always more independent evidence

Many images of one plate can help study temporal behavior or acquisition repeatability. They do not provide the same population evidence as the same number of independent isolates. The analysis should identify the biological unit and account for dependence among observations.

Data collection should preserve failed captures and unavailable results, because these influence real-world coverage. A model evaluated only on images that passed an expert selection process may appear more capable than it is in routine operation. The proposed product evaluation should therefore distinguish performance on accepted images from the complete workflow's ability to obtain an acceptable result.

pages.title: Site and temporal separation
text: **Separate development from evaluation at meaningful boundaries**

Training and test separation should prevent information about the evaluation outcome from influencing model development. Random image splitting is often insufficient when several images share a plate, isolate, patient, batch or acquisition session. The relevant grouping depends on the claim being evaluated.
## Proposed separation strategy

The development collection supports model fitting and exploratory decisions. A validation collection supports tuning and threshold selection. A final independent collection or prospective period assesses the frozen system. Site and temporal separation can challenge transfer beyond the conditions that shaped development.
## Document what the split actually tests

A held-out site can test some operational transfer, but it does not guarantee coverage of every new organism or instrument revision. A temporal split can reveal drift while still sharing many site-specific features. The report should state which forms of generalization the design supports.

The proposed software should retain dataset release identifiers and partition assignments. If a reference label changes, affected analyses should be traceable. Evaluation data should not quietly migrate into training while the same historical metrics continue to describe the revised model. New training releases require an appropriate new assessment of performance.

pages.title: Repeatability and reproducibility
text: **Repeatability and reproducibility test different sources of variation**

Repeatability examines variation under closely controlled conditions. Reproducibility examines variation when specified conditions change, such as instrument, operator, day or laboratory. Both are relevant to a measurement product, and neither alone establishes agreement with the correct value.
## Proposed variance study

A nested or crossed design can separate contributions from repeated capture, repositioning, operator and instrument. The design should reflect the permitted workflow and avoid attributing biological change to instrument variation when the same plate is observed over a period in which its appearance evolves.
## Use stable targets for instrument questions

Reference artifacts can help isolate optical and geometric variation. Biological material is needed to assess the complete measurement of real appearances. These studies answer complementary questions and should be reported separately.

The analysis should estimate relevant variance components and uncertainty, not merely report that repeated values look similar. A highly repeatable systematic bias is still an accuracy problem. Proposed acceptance should therefore combine repeatability and reproducibility evidence with independent reference agreement and clear operating limits. The resulting calibration and service requirements should follow the observed sources of variation rather than an arbitrary maintenance interval.

pages.title: Bias agreement and uncertainty
text: **Agreement needs more than correlation**

Two methods can be strongly correlated while differing by a clinically relevant offset or scale error. Measurement validation should examine differences in the reported units, their dependence on magnitude and the uncertainty of the reference comparison. A scatter plot alone can conceal systematic disagreement.
## Proposed analysis views

For paired diameters, calculate the difference between the investigational and reference measurements in mm. Examine its average, spread and relationship to diameter, organism, image quality and other relevant factors. Agreement limits require assumptions about the difference distribution and appropriate handling of repeated observations.
## Preserve reporting resolution

Rounding can change comparisons near a decision boundary. The system should retain the original measured value and the rule governing its reported form. Analysis should distinguish raw measurement behavior from the effect of rounding and categorical interpretation.

A suitable study should report confidence intervals and case counts for important subgroups. Pooled agreement may conceal a systematic problem in a smaller domain. The proposed product should restrict its qualified scope when evidence identifies such a limitation, rather than allowing a favorable overall average to override the unresolved subgroup result.

topics.title: Interpretation, usability and software validation
text: **Categorical agreement depends on the applicable interpretation rules**

pages.title: Categorical interpretation evaluation
text: **Categorical agreement depends on the applicable interpretation rules**

Categorical evaluation compares the investigational and reference interpretations within a defined organism–antimicrobial–method domain. It should use the applicable rule version and retain the underlying measurements. The same diameter can lead to different interpretations when the method or standards context changes. [R01] [R02]
## Use correct denominators

Categorical agreement is the proportion of evaluable paired results assigned the same category under the specified framework. For conventional error analyses, a very major error concerns an investigational susceptible result when the reference is resistant; its denominator is the relevant reference-resistant set. A major error concerns an investigational resistant result when the reference is susceptible, with the corresponding reference-susceptible denominator. Exact handling must follow the chosen evaluation framework.
## Do not merge unlike category meanings

EUCAST's I category denotes susceptibility with increased exposure; it should not be casually equated with another framework's intermediate category. The system should preserve the source vocabulary and any approved mapping rather than translating categories through a generic three-letter lookup.

The proposed evaluation should report measurement and interpretation errors separately where possible. A correct numerical measurement can still receive an incorrect category through a rule-mapping defect. Conversely, a measurement error may remain within the same category while exposing a weakness that matters near another threshold. Both patterns require investigation.

pages.title: Evaluating rare and consequential errors
text: **Zero observed errors do not establish a zero error rate**

Rare consequential errors require deliberate statistical planning. If n independent eligible cases produce zero errors, an exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound for the underlying error probability is 1 − 0.05^(1/n). This is a mathematical illustration under independent, identically distributed Bernoulli assumptions, not a product performance result.
## Plan the relevant denominator

For a particular error class, the relevant sample may be only the reference-resistant or reference-susceptible subset, not every test in the study. Multiple drug results from one isolate may also be dependent. The analysis should reflect that structure rather than treating every output as an independent opportunity to demonstrate safety.

The zero-error ambition is translated into engineering requirements: prevent known failure sequences, detect disagreement, abstain when evidence is inadequate and recover without inventing data. Each control needs measurable performance, including false alarms and missed failures. Multiple sensors cannot guarantee zero error because common causes can make them agree incorrectly.
## Interpret the evidence conservatively

An enriched challenge collection can help investigate rare failure modes, while a representative workflow study helps estimate operational coverage. These designs answer different questions. A credible claim should state the assessed error class, domain, denominator and confidence interval. The absence of an observed error is encouraging evidence within that study, not proof that an error is impossible.

pages.title: Abstention and coverage evaluation
text: **Abstention is useful only when its cost and coverage are visible**

An abstaining system declines to produce an eligible result when evidence is insufficient. This can reduce unsafe outputs, but a model can achieve a low accepted-case error rate by rejecting most difficult cases. Evaluation must therefore report both accuracy among accepted cases and the proportion of the intended workload that receives a result.
## Proposed selective-performance report

The study should define eligibility independently of model confidence, then account for every eligible case. Reasons for abstention should be meaningful, such as unreadable image, identity uncertainty, unsupported domain or sensor disagreement. A generic failure category can conceal distinct problems requiring different remedies.
## Test thresholds on independent data

Confidence thresholds should be selected using permitted development data and evaluated after being fixed. Reporting the most favorable threshold from the final test set would bias the result. Performance should also be stratified by site, organism and relevant difficult conditions.

The proposed interface should offer a useful next step without disguising abstention as a negative result. “Unavailable because the boundary is unreadable” has different meaning from a measured diameter. A receiving system must preserve this distinction so that an abstained case is not accidentally converted into zero, susceptible or normal during export.

pages.title: Robustness to imaging disturbances
text: **Robustness testing should reproduce meaningful disturbances**

The imaging system should be challenged with disturbances expected within or near its operating limits. Relevant factors include glare, condensation, exposure variation, blur, plate pose, label occlusion, background changes and vessel variation. Tests should assess both measurement degradation and the ability to recognize an unsupported image.
## Separate tolerance from detection

Some disturbances may be small enough for qualified measurement to continue. Others should trigger abstention. The study should establish the boundary between these states and verify that the quality check recognizes it. A system that remains numerically stable on a visually corrupted image may be confidently wrong.
## Use physical and synthetic challenges appropriately

Synthetic perturbations can isolate a software property, while physical tests reveal interactions among optics, material and environment. A simulated blur filter may not reproduce all effects of an actual focus change. Both forms of evidence should state their scope.

The proposed report should identify the disturbance level, affected area and reference behavior. Combined disturbances deserve attention because several mild effects can jointly invalidate a measurement. Recovery tests should verify that a successful recapture produces a new linked observation and that the original failed image remains available for investigation.

pages.title: Sensor failure and common causes
text: **Multiple sensors can share the same failure**

Multimodal sensing can improve error detection when channels provide complementary information. It can also create false agreement when several channels share a calibration error, clock fault, power disturbance or confounding environment. The proposed validation should test the independence assumed by the fusion method.
## Build a common-cause map

The engineering team should identify shared power, timing, mounting, calibration, preprocessing and environmental dependencies. A fault in one shared element may affect many apparently separate measurements. Voting across those measurements does not create independent confirmation.
## Evaluate the recovery decision

Detection alone is insufficient. The system must choose an appropriate qualified fallback, request review or abstain. Excluding a faulty auxiliary sensor may be acceptable for one task and invalidate another. Reduced-input modes need separate evidence and explicit eligibility rules.

The study should report fault-specific detection, false alarms, detection delay and the correctness of the resulting workflow state. It should also include faults not represented during model training. AMReye.AI's error-reduction strategy is therefore a combination of diverse evidence, explicit dependency analysis and safe handling of uncertainty, with no guarantee that sensor multiplicity eliminates every error.

pages.title: Early result validation
text: **An early result must be evaluated at the claimed time**

Rapid-AST research should specify the clock origin, specimen context, organism–drug scope and reference method before evaluation. An early output is eligible only if the method and interpretation have been established for that time. Routine endpoint breakpoints are not automatically applicable to a shorter observation interval. [R04] [R05]
## Proposed sub-two-hour study definition

The study should state which preparations and observations occur within the two-hour interval and which occur beforehand. It should preserve timestamps for unsuccessful cases and include the time needed for mandatory review when the claim concerns a reviewed result.
## Preserve the time-to-result distribution

A median below two hours can coexist with many much later cases. Report the fraction meeting the target and the distribution of delays. A model should not be scored at its eventual successful time when the claim concerns an earlier fixed deadline.

The initial programme may focus on selected workflows where sufficient signal is plausible. Expansion to other organisms, drugs or specimens requires new evidence. External studies motivate these investigations, but their analytical speed and performance cannot be imported as an AMReye.AI result.

pages.title: Human review and usability validation
text: **Human review needs validation as part of the system**

The complete product includes the interaction between software and intended users. A correct algorithm can still lead to an incorrect result through confusing presentation, wrong-record selection or ineffective correction controls. Usability evaluation should focus on tasks whose failure could affect safety, data integrity or the laboratory decision.
## Proposed critical tasks

Users should be able to verify identity, recognize unreadable observations, inspect measurement context, resolve flags, correct a result and understand the consequences of approval. Simulation views add the task of distinguishing measured evidence from predicted continuation.
## Assess realistic conditions

Participants should represent intended users, and tasks should reflect workload, interruptions and available training. Assistance from the development team during a study can conceal interface weaknesses. Observed difficulties should be analyzed for their causes and addressed through design where feasible.

The evaluation should measure errors, recoveries and understanding as well as task duration. A faster interface that encourages automatic acceptance of uncertain outputs would not satisfy the review objective. The proposed release evidence should show that users can carry out critical tasks reliably within the product's intended context, with remaining limitations reflected in design, training and use restrictions.

pages.title: Software verification and release control
text: **Software verification should follow the consequences of failure**

Verification checks that software requirements are implemented correctly and that components interact as specified. The proposed development process should link requirements, risk controls, design and test evidence. Lifecycle standards such as IEC 62304 provide a relevant planning framework; applicability and classification require product-specific assessment. [R52]
## Test the complete result path

Unit checks can validate numerical functions and state transitions. Integration tests should verify identity, calibration, interpretation, review and export together. System tests should include interrupted operations and realistic failure states. Passing isolated algorithm tests does not establish a correct end-to-end record.
!FIG work/assets/figures/verification-layers.png | Proposed verification layers and the need to reassess evidence when the configuration changes.
## Control what changes after testing

A release should identify software, models, standards rules and relevant dependencies independently. If one changes, the affected evidence should be reassessed. A signed or integrity-checked package supports distribution control, but it does not establish that the contents are clinically correct.

The proposed release process should retain test failures and their resolution, known limitations and rollback instructions. Unresolved issues need a documented impact assessment. A development build, public demonstration and qualified product release should have distinct identities so that evidence or records from one cannot be mistaken for another.

pages.title: Standards content verification
text: **Standards content is a separately controlled product dependency**

The interpretation service should identify the standards body, document version, correction state and applicable method. Measurement algorithms and standards rules need independent version identities. Updating a model should not silently change clinical thresholds, and updating thresholds should not obscure the measurement originally produced. [R01] [R02]
## Proposed content verification

Authorized source material should be mapped into structured rules by a controlled process with expert review. Tests should cover organism and antimicrobial mappings, units, method restrictions, footnotes, unavailable combinations and correction notices. Licensed content should be handled under its applicable terms.
## Check boundary behavior deliberately

Test values at, immediately below and immediately above relevant thresholds, following the method's rounding and reporting conventions. Character encoding, decimal separators and unit conversion can produce defects even when the source table was read correctly.

The proposed release package should include a standards-content manifest and regression evidence. A language model may assist expert review but should not generate executable breakpoints from memory. Before deployment, the team must verify the current source version and corrections again, because a dated compendium cannot guarantee that its reference snapshot remains the applicable rule set indefinitely.

pages.title: Interoperability verification
text: **Interoperability is preservation of meaning across a boundary**

An interface can transmit data successfully while changing its meaning. A missing value converted to zero, a simulated result treated as measured or a corrected report handled as a duplicate can create serious downstream errors. Verification should test semantics, identity and workflow states as well as network delivery.
## Proposed interface contract

Each receiving system should have an approved mapping for identifiers, units, terminology, result states, timestamps and amendments. The mapping should state which information is mandatory and what happens when it is absent. A transport acknowledgment should not be mistaken for clinical acceptance or review.
## Test both sides of the exchange

A local export file that looks correct does not establish that the receiving system interpreted it correctly. End-to-end testing should include readback or equivalent confirmation of the stored meaning. The assessment should also cover retries, timeouts and partial failures.

The proposed platform should preserve the original export payload and mapping version where appropriate for audit and privacy requirements. Changes to a laboratory system or interface profile need impact assessment. Interoperability is a maintained service responsibility, not a one-time claim based on the presence of an API endpoint.

pages.title: Traceable audit and correction records
text: **An audit trail should explain a result's history**

The audit record should capture who performed a relevant action, what changed, when it occurred and which record versions were affected. It should distinguish user actions, automated processing and administrative operations. The purpose is to reconstruct the result pathway and investigate discrepancies without relying on recollection.
## Proposed event model

Events should use stable identifiers and reference the exact input and output versions. Original observations remain preserved. Corrections append a new state and reason, while dependent analyses and approvals are assessed for invalidation. Audit access itself should be controlled and monitored.
## Integrity and completeness are different

A cryptographic integrity check can reveal changed bytes, but it cannot prove that an event was recorded truthfully or that all relevant events exist. The system needs reliable event generation, durable storage, clock context and reconciliation of interrupted operations.

Verification should include attempts to bypass normal editing paths, interrupted writes and corrections after export. The resulting history should remain understandable to an authorized reviewer. Retention and deletion policies must also account for applicable legal and institutional requirements; “immutable” should describe controlled alteration behavior, not an unqualified promise to retain personal data forever.

topics.title: Privacy, security and AI assurance
text: **Collect data for a defined purpose**

pages.title: Data minimization and purpose
text: **Collect data for a defined purpose**

Data minimization begins by identifying what each product function needs. A service engineer may require a calibration trend and hardware version without needing patient identifiers. A measurement algorithm may require a plate image whose label region contains information irrelevant to analysis. The design should reduce unnecessary exposure at the point of collection and use.
## Proposed purpose map

Each data class should have a documented purpose, authorized roles, retention basis and permitted onward use. Clinical operation, service diagnostics, product improvement and research are distinct purposes that may require different permissions and agreements.
## Preserve useful lineage without excessive disclosure

Pseudonymous identifiers can support linkage within an authorized workflow while limiting routine access to direct identifiers. The reidentification mapping should have its own access controls. Pseudonymization is not the same as anonymization, because the relationship may still be recoverable.

The proposed platform should make purpose restrictions enforceable through permissions and data flows. A broad statement that all available repositories will train an AI would be inconsistent with this approach. Curated, licensed and purpose-specific access can support useful research while preserving the rights and responsibilities attached to each source.
tables: Can irrelevant label information be excluded from a research derivative?
Can service proceed without biological content?

pages.title: Consent and lawful data use
text: **Lawful use must be assessed for the actual data flow**

The legal and ethical basis for collecting, storing and reusing data depends on jurisdiction, institutional roles, purpose and the nature of the information. A laboratory's permission to process a specimen does not automatically authorize every form of commercial model training or onward sharing. The proposed programme should document these distinctions before data collection.
## Current Indian planning context

India's final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 provide phased commencement. The Gazette distinguishes provisions commencing at publication, after one year and after eighteen months. Applicable obligations, corrections and other relevant law must therefore be checked for the deployment date and processing arrangement. This compendium describes design intentions, not a legal compliance determination. [R54]
## Build controls that support the decision

The system should retain evidence of the applicable permission or agreement without exposing unnecessary personal information. Research datasets need approval and access records appropriate to the study. A change in purpose should trigger reassessment rather than being treated as covered by a historical generic permission.

The deployment team should obtain qualified legal and institutional review for the specific arrangement. Technical safeguards support lawful processing, but encryption or pseudonymization alone does not establish that a proposed use is authorized.
tables: Separate clinical, service, research and model-development purposes.

pages.title: Identity access and authorization
text: **Authorization should be enforced where the data are accessed**

Authentication establishes an identity; authorization determines what that identity may do. The proposed platform should enforce permissions on the server or equivalent trusted boundary, including direct requests for records, images, exports and administrative actions. Hiding a button in the interface is not an access control.
## Proposed role separation

Laboratory reviewers, operators, service staff, researchers and administrators may need different privileges. Access should follow the minimum scope required for the task and be reviewed when responsibilities change. Shared accounts weaken accountability and should not be the default for consequential actions.
## Test the denied paths

Verification should attempt access through direct object identifiers, stale links, alternate routes and lower-privilege sessions. A successful authorized request does not demonstrate that unauthorized requests are rejected. Signed links and cached files need expiry and scope consistent with the intended access policy.

Session revocation, account recovery and emergency access should have defined behavior. The system should preserve essential audit evidence while avoiding disclosure of credentials or secrets in logs. Controlled external review of a product document or research dataset should use an explicit audience and should not accidentally expose the same material through a public route or search index.
tables: Restricted technical data and time-bounded support access.
Strong authentication and auditable privilege changes.

pages.title: Encryption and key management
text: **Encryption depends on key management and endpoint controls**

The proposed system should protect sensitive data in transit and at rest using established, appropriately configured cryptographic mechanisms. Encryption is one layer of protection. An authorized application with excessive access, a compromised endpoint or an exposed key can still disclose encrypted information after decryption.
## Proposed key lifecycle

Keys and credentials should be provisioned through controlled mechanisms, stored outside source code and ordinary logs, rotated where appropriate and revoked when no longer authorized. Recovery arrangements must avoid making a single lost key the cause of permanent loss of required records.
## Include devices and removable media

An instrument may retain images or queued records during offline operation. Its local storage and service access need protection appropriate to the data. Exported files can also leave the application's controls, so the export workflow should identify the recipient, purpose and permitted handling.

The engineering specification should use current supported security mechanisms and independent review rather than inventing a custom encryption scheme. Verification should include configuration and operational procedures, not only the presence of an encryption library. The product claim should describe the implemented protection accurately without suggesting that encryption makes the system immune to compromise.

pages.title: Secure software development
text: **Security engineering should be part of ordinary development**

The proposed software lifecycle should include threat modelling, secure design, dependency management, code review, verification and vulnerability response. Security requirements should follow the product's assets and trust boundaries. Medical-device cybersecurity guidance and health-software security standards provide relevant planning references, with applicability assessed for the intended product. [R49] [R53]
## Track the software supply chain

A software bill of materials identifies relevant components and versions. It supports vulnerability assessment and change management but does not itself prove security. The team should determine whether a reported vulnerability is reachable in the product and what mitigation or update is needed.
## Test the AI-specific boundaries

Retrieved documents and user-supplied text should not gain authority to change permissions or execute actions. A language assistant needs constrained tools, source-aware responses and explicit authorization for consequential operations. Training and evaluation should include misleading instructions embedded in otherwise relevant material.

Security findings should enter the same controlled change process as other product defects, with priority based on impact and exposure. The proposed programme should retain unresolved risks and support periods transparently. A clean automated scan is useful evidence for the checks performed, not a guarantee that no exploitable weakness exists.
tables: Assets, actors, trust boundaries and misuse scenarios.

pages.title: Instrument and network security
text: **Instrument security includes physical and network boundaries**

An instrument connects software to a physical laboratory workflow. Security assessment should consider local storage, service ports, removable media, update mechanisms and network access. A protected cloud service does not compensate for an instrument that exposes records or accepts unauthorized control locally.
## Proposed deployment boundary

The device should expose only the services needed for its qualified functions. Network segmentation, authenticated communication and controlled administration can limit unnecessary reachability. Remote support should be explicitly authorized, scoped and auditable, with a defined end to the session.
## Safe operation during isolation

If a security incident requires network isolation, the instrument should enter a defined operating mode. It may retain eligible local capture and review or suspend functions that depend on trusted external services. The choice must follow the qualified workflow and risk assessment, not an improvised response during an incident.

Verification should include unauthorized control attempts, invalid updates and loss of network trust. The product should preserve record integrity and avoid unsafe physical actions when communication fails. Security and biological reliability interact: an incident that changes timing, calibration or environmental control may require assessment of affected laboratory records as well as restoration of the software.

pages.title: Incident response and recovery
text: **Incident response should restore trustworthy service**

The proposed incident process should identify, contain, investigate and recover from events affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability. Recovery is complete only when the system and relevant records are trustworthy for their intended use. Restarting a service without assessing altered data or configuration can leave the underlying problem unresolved.
## Proposed response record

The team should preserve the incident timeline, affected systems, observed indicators and actions taken. Access to evidence should be controlled, and sensitive information should not be copied into broad support channels. Notification obligations depend on the applicable law, agreement and incident context.
## Test restoration before it is needed

Backups should be tested for completeness, integrity and usability, including required keys and configuration. Recovery objectives should reflect the laboratory workflow and retention requirements. A backup that exists but cannot be restored within the needed context is not an effective continuity measure.

Exercises should include corrupted records, lost credentials, unavailable cloud services and instrument replacement. After restoration, the system should reconcile queued events and identify uncertain intervals. Affected approvals or interpretations may require review if their inputs or integrity cannot be established. Incident closure should retain the evidence and residual limitations rather than merely marking the service online.

pages.title: Privacy in shared research datasets
text: **Research sharing should preserve utility while limiting disclosure**

A research dataset may contain direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, labels embedded in images and sensitive institutional information. Removing a name field is not sufficient to establish anonymity. The proposed sharing process should assess what can be inferred from the combination of fields and the recipient's access to other information.
## Proposed dataset release process

The release should have a defined purpose, authorized recipients, permitted analyses and retention conditions. Data minimization should be applied to images, metadata and free text. The team should verify that transformation has preserved the scientific variables required for the study.
## Treat transformed data as a new release

The dataset should retain a version, transformation description and relationship to the authorized source. Researchers need to know whether values were removed, generalized, imputed or simulated. Privacy transformations can affect analytical validity and should be considered in interpretation.

The proposed programme should use institutional and legal review appropriate to the data and jurisdiction. A public repository's availability does not automatically authorize every reuse or combination. Shared research should return useful scientific value while respecting the original permissions and avoiding claims that a technical de-identification step guarantees zero reidentification risk.

pages.title: AI assurance and change management
text: **AI assurance continues after the first evaluation**

An AI capability needs a defined intended use, data lineage, performance assessment and change process. Assurance also includes behavior under uncertainty, shift and misuse. General AI risk-management and good machine-learning-practice resources provide useful principles, but they do not certify a particular model or replace product-specific evidence. [R21] [R23]
## Proposed model release record

The record should identify the model, training data release, preprocessing, decision thresholds and evaluated domain. It should retain conventional baselines and known limitations. The interface and downstream rules that use the model are part of the evaluated system configuration.
## Monitor without uncontrolled learning

Field monitoring can identify drift, unexpected failures and review patterns. It should not automatically convert every user correction into a training label or update the deployed model continuously. Candidate changes need curation, evaluation and controlled release.

The proposed system should support rollback to a qualified version while preserving which version produced each historical output. Monitoring should include accepted-case errors, abstention, data quality and important subgroups. A stable average score can conceal changing case mix or a local failure. Assurance therefore requires interpretable evidence and accountable decisions throughout the model's service life.

topics.title: Clinical study preparation and release gates
text: **Clinical study preparation starts before data collection**

pages.title: Clinical study preparation
text: **Clinical study preparation starts before data collection**

A clinical performance investigation should be designed around the intended product claim and conducted through the applicable ethical, institutional and regulatory processes. The protocol should define responsibilities, material handling, reference methods, data governance and analysis. A retrospective convenience collection may answer an exploratory question while remaining insufficient for a broader product claim. [R35]
## Proposed preparation package

The study team should specify eligibility, recruitment or specimen-selection methods, endpoints, sample-size rationale and handling of missing or indeterminate results. Training and instrument configuration should be controlled. The investigational output's role in clinical care must be explicitly determined and authorized.
## Preserve deviations and unsuccessful cases

Protocol deviations should be recorded with their effect on interpretation. Exclusions should follow prespecified rules and be reported transparently. A study should not remove difficult cases merely because they reduce apparent performance.

The proposed programme should involve appropriate microbiology, clinical, statistical, engineering and governance expertise. No clinical study completion, recruitment, approval or patient benefit is claimed here. The product's next evidence step should be selected from the actual maturity of its measurement and software functions, with exploratory work separated from evidence intended to support release or clinical claims.
tables: Clear question, population, method and prespecified analysis.

pages.title: India regulatory assessment
text: **India regulatory assessment follows intended use and product function**

The proposed reader, interpretation software, integrated instrument and predictive research functions may raise different regulatory questions. Assessment should begin with what each function does, the material it processes and the medical decision it supports. Calling software an assistant or labelling a device research-only does not by itself resolve its regulatory status.
## Current reference and its limits

CDSCO's 2026 medical-device software guidance discusses intended use, risk classification, quality systems and regulatory pathways under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017. The document states that it is an awareness resource and directs professional use to the statutory provisions and applicable clarifications. It is a planning reference here, not a product-specific legal determination. [R26]
## Keep endpoint and predictive functions separate

A qualified endpoint measurement function should not be used as evidence that a rapid classification or simulated biological result is authorized. Each extension needs an assessment of its intended use and evidence consequences. Public copy, demonstrations and instructions should remain consistent with that scope.

Before regulated evaluation or commercialization, the programme should obtain appropriate specialist review and verify current statutory requirements. No device classification, licence, clearance or certification is asserted by this compendium. The immediate deliverable is a coherent technical and evidence plan from which that assessment can proceed.
tables: Identify hardware, software, accessories and connected functions.

pages.title: Quality management and standards planning
text: **Quality management connects design, evidence and delivered units**

The proposed quality system should ensure that requirements, risk controls, design decisions, suppliers, production and service remain traceable. ISO 13485 is a relevant medical-device quality-management reference; ISO 14971 addresses risk management. Their applicability and implementation should be assessed for the product and organization, with no certification implied. [R50] [R51]
## Select standards by function

Software lifecycle, health-software security, laboratory competence and instrument safety address different aspects of the programme. The standards plan should identify the exact edition, applicable scope and required evidence. A list of standards is not evidence that the product complies with them.
## Laboratory competence is a separate consideration

Testing and calibration services may require competence arrangements appropriate to their work. ISO/IEC 17025 provides a relevant framework for testing and calibration laboratories, but it does not replace medical-device product requirements or establish an accreditation for AMReye.AI. [R64]

The quality system should scale with development maturity while preserving the evidence needed for later decisions. Early prototypes can be flexible, but their configurations and test conditions must still be recorded if the findings are to inform subsequent engineering or external claims.

pages.title: Release gates and residual risk review
text: **Release requires a defined decision on the remaining risk**

A release gate should assess the complete configuration intended for use: instrument, software, model, calibration, standards content, interfaces, instructions and service arrangements. Each component may pass its own tests while their combination remains inadequately evaluated. The release decision should therefore review the integrated evidence and unresolved limitations.
## Make unresolved matters explicit

Known issues should identify affected conditions, consequences and controls. A limitation should not be hidden in a technical file while marketing implies unrestricted capability. Where evidence is insufficient, the release may be restricted, deferred or retained for a defined research purpose.

The zero-error aspiration informs this process through prevention, detection, abstention and recovery. It is not a release criterion that can be proven universally. The responsible decision is whether the evidence and residual risks support the exact intended use under the applicable requirements.

AMReye.AI remains at research and prototype stage in this compendium. The proposed gates provide a route toward a dependable product and a basis for partner review. Future claims should be revised only when the corresponding engineering, analytical, clinical or operational evidence has actually been obtained and assessed.

topics.title: Scientific evidence for measurement and biological research
text: **Evidence supports a particular proposition under particular conditions**

pages.title: How to read the evidence synthesis
text: **Evidence supports a particular proposition under particular conditions**

This synthesis evaluates the scientific basis and unresolved questions behind the proposed platform. It is a focused critical review, not a systematic review with exhaustive database coverage or a meta-analysis. Original studies, standards, agency guidance and manufacturer documentation serve different purposes and should not be treated as interchangeable levels of proof.
## Four questions for each source

The relevant questions are what was measured, in which population, against which comparator and under which operating conditions. A result can be credible within its study while remaining insufficient for a different specimen, organism, instrument or clinical decision. Publication establishes an accessible account of work; it does not independently certify every claim in that account.
## Reading quantitative results

Agreement, precision, accuracy, sensitivity and time to result answer different questions. A high correlation can coexist with systematic measurement bias. A small average error can conceal clinically important outliers. A rapid answer among selected successful runs can coexist with a substantial unresolved fraction.

Where the available evidence does not establish a denominator, independent validation or local applicability, the conclusion remains bounded. The practical outcome of this review is a set of testable design decisions and research questions. No external study is represented as an AMReye.AI experiment, and no aggregate performance score is assigned to the proposed platform.
tables: Assess a measured finding and its design limitations.
Establish applicable procedural and interpretive requirements.
Understand scope, responsibilities and evidence expectations.

pages.title: Disk diffusion standards and reader evidence
text: **A calibrated image does not replace the biological method**

CLSI M100 Edition 36 and EUCAST clinical breakpoint tables version 16.1 were the current editions verified for this publication date. Their applicability depends on the relevant method, organism, antimicrobial and conditions. A breakpoint value detached from those conditions is not a complete interpretation rule. [R01] [R02]

The CLSI correction of 9 July 2026 restores the sulfamethoxazole concentrations in combination MIC notation in Table 2H-1. It illustrates why an edition number alone is insufficient version control. The correction does not create a disk-diffusion indication where the table's method restrictions do not permit one. [R74]
## Reader precision is one component

Hombach and colleagues' variance analysis distinguished biological variation from technical contributions, including preparation, streaking, materials and reading. Their estimated contributions varied substantially across the tested organism–drug combinations. The findings support evaluating the entire preparation-to-reading process rather than assuming that image precision determines total assay precision. [R67]
## Consequence for development

Reader V1 should preserve the distinction between measurement uncertainty and method variability. Its interface should expose missing method context before category assignment. Validation should include plates near relevant decision boundaries and difficult reading conditions, with a predefined route for unresolved cases. Greater numerical precision should never be presented as proof that an unsuitable biological preparation has become valid.
tables: Is the plate eligible for interpretation?
Independent readings and controlled repeat captures.
Eligible, corrected standards content and reviewer decision.

pages.title: External evidence on automated zone measurement
text: **Automated measurement evidence must disclose human intervention**

Hombach et al. compared on-screen adjusted Sirscan readings with manual measurements and separately assessed repeated automated readings. The study reported improved repeatability in the automated condition. The distinction between adjusted clinical readings and the precision experiment matters: their results do not establish that every autonomous reading was correct without review. [R66]
## A recent AI study requires additional clarification

The 2026 study by Ciftci and colleagues reports categorical agreement of 94.2% and mean absolute diameter error of 0.42 mm. Its methods describe 207 original photographs in one passage and 1,024 baseline images elsewhere, expanded to 5,120. The detection metric also differs between a table and the ablation narrative. These counts and the independence of plate/isolate partitions require clarification before the headline metrics can serve as a robust benchmark. [R12]
## Proposed evaluation response

AMReye.AI should report the unedited model output and the final reviewed result separately. Every evaluated plate should retain its split assignment, source image lineage and correction history. An augmented image must remain in the same partition as its source and associated biological unit.

Evidence should make these distinctions auditable. A model explanation or attention map can support investigation, but it cannot substitute for independent performance evaluation or establish that a model has learned a biologically valid mechanism.
tables: Describes views and transformations, not new isolates.

pages.title: External evidence on rapid single cell AST
text: **Rapid single-cell AST demonstrates a route, not a universal timescale**

Baltekin et al. demonstrated direct single-cell imaging in a microfluidic setting and reported susceptibility classification for 49 clinical uropathogenic E. coli isolates against ciprofloxacin within ten minutes of the measurement sequence. The overall method was described as requiring less than thirty minutes from sample loading. The narrow organism–drug evaluation and the timing origin are essential parts of that result. [R11]
## Translation questions for AMReye.AI

The study motivates investigation of early phenotypic responses where sufficient cells can be observed under a controlled antimicrobial exposure. It does not demonstrate that an ordinary endpoint plate photograph can deliver the same answer. Differences in specimen preparation, cell capture, exposure, optical sampling and decision criteria must be evaluated explicitly.
## Sub-two-hour research target

The proposed target should begin with a defined specimen and clock origin, not a platform-wide promise. A feasibility study should prespecify the proportion of eligible samples expected to receive a reportable answer, the comparator method and acceptable uncertainty. Time distributions should include failed runs and repeats.

A useful early answer is one whose correctness and limits are understood. If a sample requires longer observation, abstention preserves the distinction between a target and an established capability. Faster inference cannot compensate for insufficient biological information.

pages.title: External evidence on heteroresistance in infection
text: **Heteroresistance has mechanistic and context-dependent clinical evidence**

Band et al. linked an initially susceptible classification of Enterobacter cloacae with a resistant subpopulation and treatment failure in a murine infection model. This establishes a biologically consequential example under the tested conditions, rather than a universal human outcome or an imaging diagnostic rule. [R08]

Doijad and colleagues examined mechanistic determinants of colistin heteroresistance in the Enterobacter cloacae complex. Kupke and colleagues later described transient amplification events in a veterinary clinical isolate. Together these studies motivate attention to population structure and unstable resistance phenotypes without implying a single mechanism for all organisms and drugs. [R09] [R60]
## Clinical association is not uniform

Wei et al. identified heteroresistance in 40 of 164 non-resistant isolates within a 212-isolate collection. The study did not find a significant increase in the assessed hospitalization or progression outcomes. Its retrospective context and denominators should accompany interpretation. This finding does not negate the murine mechanism; it limits a universal clinical-outcome inference. [R61]
## Proposed contribution of imaging

AMReye.AI can investigate whether longitudinal spatial observations improve recognition of candidate minority growth. The first validation question is detection of a reproducible visual event. Confirmation of heteroresistance is a separate biological question requiring appropriate reference characterization.
The product should preserve the chain between these stages. It should not label every satellite colony as resistant or infer clinical treatment failure from an image alone.
tables: Temporal evidence of a biological event, subject to confounders.
A method-supported heteroresistance finding within defined scope.

pages.title: External evidence on heteroresistance and combinations
text: **Combination findings generate hypotheses that require their own evaluation**

Band et al.'s 2019 work investigated the exploitation of heteroresistance to identify effective antibiotic combinations. The study provides a mechanistic reason to examine how differently susceptible subpopulations respond to combined exposures. It does not authorize a general combination recommendation or establish a treatment-selection function for AMReye.AI. [R07]
## A proposed research use

The platform could support controlled experiments by recording spatial growth, exposure context and time-dependent responses under a prespecified design. Its contribution would be measurement and traceability. Interpretation of interaction, mechanism and therapeutic significance would require the appropriate experimental and clinical expertise.
## Avoid a false shortcut from image to therapy

An apparent reduction in visible growth can result from different biological processes. A single image cannot establish killing, durable suppression, mechanism or patient benefit. Even a reproducible laboratory interaction remains conditional on the tested system.

The proposed software should therefore present research measurements and uncertainty without generating autonomous treatment instructions. A useful capability would be the ability to compare hypotheses and retrieve the complete experimental record. The development objective is to make combination research more inspectable, while keeping therapeutic claims behind their own evidence and authorization requirements.
tables: Establish the relevant heterogeneity before the comparison.
Preserve concentrations, timing and the experimental context.
Define growth, survival or another measured outcome in advance.
Use a suitable comparator and prespecified analysis.
Evaluate separately from laboratory interaction evidence.

pages.title: Definitions of persistence and tolerance
text: **Resistance, tolerance and persistence describe different response patterns**

The consensus statement by Balaban and colleagues distinguishes resistance, which concerns growth under antimicrobial exposure, from tolerance and persistence, which concern survival during killing. Persistence refers to a surviving subpopulation rather than uniformly slower killing across the population. These distinctions require suitable experimental endpoints and cannot be established by vocabulary alone. [R10]
## Implication for a measurement platform

An endpoint zone image primarily records spatial growth inhibition under its method conditions. A time series may reveal additional dynamics, but the observable signal still has to match the biological question. An unchanged object might be alive, dead or an imaging artifact. Absence of visible expansion does not establish eradication.
## Design the record around the actual endpoint

The proposed data model should store whether an experiment measures growth, viable survival, metabolic response or another signal. Analysis should preserve the observation period and exposure definition. A generic field called “resistance score” would obscure distinctions that matter scientifically.

For research comparisons, the programme should agree on terminology before data collection. Reviewers should be able to identify whether a claim follows from the measured endpoint or remains a hypothesis. This is especially relevant when multimodal measurements disagree: a metabolic signal and an optical growth signal may answer different questions rather than indicate that one sensor has failed. Biological interpretation should precede automatic reconciliation.
tables: Requires the applicable assay and interpretive context.

pages.title: Evidence for spatial and temporal growth models
text: **Growth models explain variation without guaranteeing an individual future**

Thomas et al. developed a stochastic cellular model linking gene expression, metabolism and replication. The work connects fluctuations in cellular processes with heterogeneous growth and evaluates model behavior against reported physiological observations. It provides a basis for investigating variable responses, not a validated forecasting model for a particular AMReye.AI plate. [R13]

Kapteyn, Pretorius and Willcox describe probabilistic graphical modelling for digital twins in an engineering setting. Its relevance here is methodological: distinguish latent state, observation, uncertainty and decision. Biological calibration and validation remain separate work. [R59]
## Evidence needed at plate scale

The proposed twin must connect its latent variables to actual measurable quantities. A plausible growth equation is insufficient if several parameter combinations fit the same short observation period but predict incompatible futures. That situation is an identifiability limitation, not a reason to select the most visually convincing trajectory.
## Scientific consequence

Simulation continuity preserves computation after physical observation ends. It cannot preserve knowledge of unobserved contamination, environmental changes or new biological events. The proposed publication and interface should retain the final measured state and show how uncertainty evolves beyond it. Model-based exploration remains valuable precisely when its assumptions and limits can be inspected.
tables: Sensitivity and identifiability analysis using the intended observations.
Does forecasting beat a simple baseline?
Prospective time-split comparison against persistence and simple growth fits.
Withheld-observation experiments with known later measurements.

pages.title: Optical metrology evidence
text: **Sensor specifications and system metrology answer different questions**

EMVA 1288 provides a framework for characterizing camera behavior. Optical documentation explains how geometry, perspective and lens choice affect imaging. The JCGM uncertainty framework supports an explicit account of contributions to a measurement result. None supplies an automatic accuracy specification for an assembled plate reader. [R14] [R15] [R16]
## The measurement chain is the object of validation

A camera can have a small pixel pitch while the final system has substantial error from distortion, defocus, plate height, reflections or boundary interpretation. Similarly, a lens chosen for reduced perspective sensitivity still requires alignment and verification across the actual object field.
## Proposed metrology experiment

The optical bench should compare known geometric targets at multiple positions and relevant heights. Repeat captures should vary remounting, illumination and qualified environmental conditions. The analysis should separate scale error, spatial distortion and repeatability, then examine biological boundaries using independent reference readings.

The resulting evidence should state where measurements are eligible and when recalibration or rejection is necessary. Object sampling in micrometres per pixel is a useful design calculation, but it should be reported separately from diameter uncertainty in millimetres. Keeping those quantities distinct prevents a component specification from becoming an unsupported biological measurement claim.
tables: Image quality under the selected exposure and illumination.
Usable field, focus, distortion and mounting stability.
Traceability and fitness for the spatial scale of interest.
A defensible budget for the assembled measurement procedure.

pages.title: Gas and environmental sensor evidence
text: **Environmental sensing supports context before it supports biological inference**

Manufacturer documentation for gas and environmental sensors establishes their physical signals, operating ranges and integration requirements. A broad gas response or a temperature channel does not identify a bacterial species, resistance mechanism or metabolite without additional evidence. The platform's candidate catalogue therefore separates environmental monitoring from exploratory biological sensing. [R17] [R18]
## A controlled question for each signal

Temperature, humidity and gas measurements can help explain whether acquisition occurred under qualified conditions. Using the same channels as biological predictors is a separate research programme. It requires demonstrating that the signal reflects the intended biology rather than media, cleaning agents, room conditions or sensor history.
## Evidence threshold for inclusion

A channel should earn its place through incremental information, reliability or control value. A modality that improves apparent training accuracy but fails across sites should not be described as robust biological sensing. Candidate selection should compare its benefit with the added calibration, maintenance and contamination-control burden.

The strongest near-term use may be detecting a condition that makes the optical result unreliable. That is a meaningful contribution even when the channel cannot support a standalone diagnostic inference. The product should express this role directly, rather than convert every installed sensor into a separate clinical claim.

topics.title: AI evidence, comparators and unresolved propositions
text: **Sequence evidence does not remove phenotype uncertainty**

pages.title: Sequence based resistance evidence
text: **Sequence evidence does not remove phenotype uncertainty**

CARD and NCBI Pathogen Detection provide curated resistance-related resources and documented analytical contexts. Their content supports structured investigation of genetic determinants and isolate relationships. A database match is not equivalent to a measured susceptibility result, and an absent match does not prove susceptibility. Version, coverage and the underlying sequence quality remain material. [R24] [R25]
## Separate three evidence paths

The proposed platform should distinguish externally measured molecular results, computational interpretation of sequence data and predictions from images or other phenotypes. These paths can be compared, but they should not be merged into a field that hides how a conclusion was obtained.
## A useful disagreement study

The programme can examine cases where a measured phenotype and a molecular result diverge. The investigation should consider assay coverage, expression, regulatory context, mixed populations, measurement quality and record linkage before assigning an explanation. The aim is to identify resolvable causes and persistent uncertainty.

Model training should avoid learning site, lineage or specimen shortcuts that merely correlate with resistance in the available collection. Evaluation should separate related isolates and examine performance when the distribution changes. A useful genomic integration service preserves evidence provenance and explains discordance. It does not promise to process every repository or infer every resistance mechanism from a plate image.
tables: Limited to the assay's target and intended use.
Conditional on sequence quality, pipeline and database coverage.
A research inference requiring independent molecular confirmation.

pages.title: AI assurance evidence
text: **AI assurance is a lifecycle argument supported by measurements**

Good machine learning practice, transparency principles and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework emphasize structured development and evaluation of AI systems. These resources help organize evidence and responsibilities; they do not supply an automatic approval or a universal performance threshold. [R21] [R22] [R23]
## Test the proposed decision behavior

For AMReye.AI, an assurance case should connect intended use to data, models, interfaces and human decisions. The evidence should show how the system behaves when an input is outside its training experience, a sensor disagrees or a reviewer changes a result. Performance on a convenient retrospective test set is only one component.
## Meaningful baselines

Each proposed AI capability should be compared with an appropriate conventional method. Fixed image-quality rules, geometric fitting, simple trend models and explicit workflow logic may outperform a learned approach when data are limited or the task is well constrained. The choice should follow measured benefit.

The assurance programme should report both capability and burden: correction frequency, unresolved cases, reviewer workload and operational failures. A system that reaches high agreement by deferring nearly every difficult case has a different value proposition from one that handles those cases reliably. Both accuracy and coverage belong in the product evidence.
tables: Documented population, workflow and data coverage.
Patient, isolate, plate and site lineage controls as applicable.
Versioned models, change assessment and rollback evidence.
Preserved inputs, outputs and decision lineage.

pages.title: Manual and digital reader comparators
text: **Manual and digital readers occupy a defined part of the workflow**

Manual disk-diffusion reading combines method-specific visual judgment with measurement and transcription. A digital reader can support imaging, zone measurement and result handling while retaining operator responsibility for ambiguous growth. BIOMIC V3 is an example of a commercial digital reading system; the Sirscan study provides historical experimental evidence relevant to this category. [R29] [R66]
## Compare equivalent tasks

Reader V1's appropriate comparison begins with the endpoint reading workflow. The evaluation should use the same eligible plates and distinguish preparation, incubation, capture, analysis, review and export. Incubation time should not disappear from a total-turnaround claim merely because it occurs before loading the reader.
## Potential differentiation to investigate

AMReye.AI proposes a tightly linked record of capture quality, measurement uncertainty and reviewer actions. The question is whether that linkage improves reproducibility and reduces avoidable work in the intended laboratory. This requires a measured comparison; it is not established by including more software functions.

Competitive assessment should account for local service, consumables, training, maintenance and existing laboratory systems. An institution may value interoperability and dependable support more than an expanded feature list. The development programme should therefore compare the complete endpoint service offered to a user, with current regional specifications checked before any procurement decision.
tables: Bias, spread and outliers against independent reference readings.
Detection of invalid or ambiguous inputs, including false acceptance.

Traceability of source image, scale, interpretation and correction.
Export accuracy and resilience to interrupted transfer.

pages.title: Integrated disk diffusion comparators
text: **Integrated disk-diffusion automation extends beyond image analysis**

COPAN describes RADIAN within an automated microbiology workflow that includes disk application, incubation-related handling, digital reading and supporting software functions. Its scope is broader than a standalone endpoint reader. The existence of this category rules out a general claim that automated plate-based AST or AI-assisted disk reading is unique to AMReye.AI. [R27] [R28]

Cherkaoui et al. evaluated a Colibri–RADIAN workflow against VITEK 2 in routine laboratory conditions. The study is relevant because it assesses an integrated process and categorical agreement, rather than only segmentation on stored photographs. Its findings remain specific to the evaluated configuration and comparison. [R68]
## Proposed comparison design

The integrated AMReye.AI track should be evaluated independently from Reader V1. It introduces additional responsibilities for sample identity, movement, preparation, timing and recovery. These functions change the risk profile and the amount of verification required.
## Distinguishing ambition from demonstrated advantage

The proposed platform's modular sensing and longitudinal data could create research value, but adding these functions does not establish superior clinical results or lower total cost. A credible comparison should examine defined workflows, throughput distributions, quality outcomes and service requirements. The integrated track should progress only when each added automation function improves a verified process without obscuring its failure modes.

pages.title: Automated ID and AST comparators
text: **Identification and susceptibility systems should be compared by output**

VITEK 2, BD Phoenix M50 and DxM MicroScan WalkAway represent established automated ID/AST system families. Their cards or panels, supported organisms and reporting functions differ. Current manufacturer documentation is useful for identifying those functions, while the applicable regional labeling and panel-specific evidence determine actual use. [R30] [R31] [R69]

MALDI-TOF systems such as VITEK MS PRIME primarily support organism identification through mass-spectral analysis. Identification can inform an AST workflow, but it is not the same measurement as phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility. [R72]
## Implication for the portfolio

Reader V1 should support reliable integration of independently established identity where required. It should not imply that a disk image performs the same identification function as a validated biochemical, molecular or mass-spectral method. Phenotype-to-genotype and morphology-based identification remain separately evaluated research capabilities.

Competitive differentiation should be assessed at the level of the user's decision. A laboratory may use an integrated ID/AST system for routine panels and retain disk diffusion for selected requirements. The proposed product should explain where it fits, how records connect and what evidence supports that use. A list of instrument names cannot substitute for a comparison of specimen requirements, reportable scope, exception handling and operational fit.
tables: How is organism identity established and linked to the specimen?
What susceptibility output is supported for the relevant panel?

pages.title: Rapid AST and microfluidic comparators
text: **Rapid AST is a family of methods with different clocks and specimens**

Manufacturer documentation describes dRAST as a positive-blood-culture phenotypic AST workflow with results in as little as four hours. VITEK REVEAL describes rapid phenotypic AST for Gram-negative positive blood cultures, with average timings around 5.5–6 hours. Q-linea describes ASTar reports in approximately six hours from its relevant workflow. These are manufacturer-described timings, not a direct independent comparison or time from patient sampling. [R70] [R71] [R75]

EUCAST RAST has its own eligibility, timing and interpretation documents. A research single-cell method, a commercial positive-blood-culture system and an early disk-diffusion method should therefore remain distinct comparator classes. [R04] [R05]
## AMReye.AI research position

Sub-two-hour performance remains a target for selected, explicitly defined workflows. The proposed studies should compare reportable-answer distributions, not the fastest successful example. Organism–drug coverage, invalid runs, repeat testing and reviewer time belong beside the timing result.

Microfluidics may shorten diffusion distances or permit observation of individual cells, but it also introduces loading, material, exposure and sampling constraints. Its value must be tested in the chosen biological workflow. The platform should pursue the mechanism that best supports reliable early information, while maintaining endpoint Reader V1 as a distinct development priority.
tables: Question to resolve before comparing speed

pages.title: Research imaging and software comparators
text: **Research imaging platforms compete on experimental information**

Reshape Biotech describes automated endpoint and time-lapse capture, structured analysis and data-sharing workflows for microbiology research and quality-control applications. This is a relevant comparator for longitudinal imaging and research data services. Manufacturer workflow descriptions do not establish clinical AST performance or equivalence with a diagnostic system. [R73]

Research modalities such as speckle imaging, Raman-based analysis, electrical microfluidics and calorimetry provide additional examples of measurable microbial responses. Their existence supports a broad technology search, while each has its own sampling and validation boundaries. [R38] [R40] [R42] [R44] [R45]
## Proposed research-platform comparison

For the AMReye.AI research family, useful outcomes include experimental reproducibility, observation completeness, analysis transparency and the ability to compare conditions without losing provenance. Clinical categories may not be the appropriate primary endpoint for these applications.
## A disciplined breadth of scope

The proposed portfolio should offer distinct research functions rather than imply that one device performs every method. Microscopy, spectroscopy and automated plate handling may belong to different configurations or collaborations. The decision to integrate a modality should follow a demonstrated user question and measurable benefit.

An effective research service can help laboratories preserve and analyze experiments even before a predictive twin becomes useful. That near-term value should be evaluated on its own terms, while predictive and diagnostic extensions remain subject to additional evidence.

pages.title: Regulatory evidence and label specificity
text: **Regulatory evidence belongs to a specific device and intended use**

The CDSCO medical-device software guidance provides context for assessing software under India's Medical Devices Rules. It does not, by itself, assign AMReye.AI a classification or establish permission to market. Intended use, software function, hardware relationship and applicable statutory requirements require a product-specific assessment. [R26]

The FDA decision identified in reference R32 illustrates another boundary: a regulatory record supports the device and indications covered by that record. Similarity in imaging or AI terminology cannot transfer another device's authorization to the proposed platform. [R32]
## Evidence that should accompany a regulatory comparison

The programme should retain the exact device, version, jurisdiction, indication and limitations when discussing an authorization. A manufacturer's broad product-family page may not identify the particular configuration relevant to an institution's intended workflow.
## AMReye.AI publication boundary

This compendium describes proposed engineering and research requirements. It is not a regulatory submission, clinical-use instruction or declaration of conformity. The validation and quality sections identify work that the development programme must complete.

Current FDA cybersecurity guidance and software lifecycle standards can inform planning, but a citation to them does not demonstrate implementation. [R49] [R52] [R53] The product's eventual regulatory case should connect its actual design and evidence to the applicable requirements, with qualified review of the intended market and use.

pages.title: Contradictions and unverified propositions
text: **Contradictions should change the strength of a claim**

The literature and product landscape support meaningful opportunities, but several attractive propositions remain unverified. The proposed platform should retain these as explicit research questions. A stronger vocabulary cannot resolve an evidence gap, and a larger sensor catalogue does not supply validation by itself.
## Contradiction does not always mean one source is wrong

The murine heteroresistance study and the retrospective clinical collection answer different questions. An effect under a controlled infection model can coexist with an absence of a significant association in a particular clinical analysis. Both should inform the research design without being collapsed into a universal conclusion. [R08] [R61]
## Proposed response to unresolved evidence

AMReye.AI should identify the decision affected by each uncertainty. Some gaps prevent a claim; others determine an experiment or a configuration choice. The response should be proportionate: preserve an unresolved status, obtain independent characterization or revise the intended use.

The same discipline applies to negative findings. A failed exploratory modality can be valuable if it reveals a confounder or an integration cost. Development should reward informative evidence, including evidence that narrows the portfolio, rather than treating every proposed capability as an inevitable product feature.

pages.title: Priority questions for original AMReye.AI evidence
text: **The next decisive evidence should come from AMReye.AI's own defined tasks**

External work establishes scientific plausibility, known alternatives and important limitations. The development programme now needs original evidence that connects the proposed system to its intended users. The highest-value studies are those that resolve a specific release or research decision.
## Priority evidence sequence

Reader V1 should first demonstrate a dependable measurement chain and review workflow. Advanced sensing and forecasting can then be investigated against that foundation, using independently defined outcomes rather than a single broad “platform accuracy” measure.
## What a publishable result should include

The proposed reports should describe configuration, biological population, sampling, reference method, exclusions, missing data, uncertainty and failures. Data splits should respect biological and capture lineage. Where sharing is permitted, analysis definitions and appropriately protected data should support independent scrutiny.

The programme should also measure practical consequences: review effort, instrument downtime, calibration burden and integration errors. A technically impressive measurement can have limited value if it creates an unreliable workflow. Original AMReye.AI evidence should therefore show both what the system measures and how that measurement supports a dependable laboratory process.
