topics.title: Reader V1 engineering and dataset development
text: **Development should produce evidence-bearing increments**

pages.title: From requirements to verified increments
text: **Development should produce evidence-bearing increments**

The proposed programme should convert the platform vision into bounded engineering questions. Each increment should deliver a function and the evidence needed to assess it. This approach allows configuration ideas to remain flexible while preventing an untested concept from becoming a fixed product promise.
## Begin with observable requirements

A requirement should describe a behavior, condition and acceptance method. “Reliable imaging” is too broad to test directly. A more useful requirement identifies the permitted plate range, capture conditions, quality decision and retained record. Numerical thresholds should follow justified design targets and evidence, not arbitrary precision.
!FIG work/assets/figures/development-evidence.png | Proposed sequence for one bounded development increment; an adverse finding can justify restriction or stopping.
## Preserve learning across changes

An unsuccessful prototype can establish a useful limit, such as insufficient optical contrast or an impractical service requirement. The relevant conditions and measurements should be retained so that the same assumption is not repeatedly rediscovered. Historical evidence must still identify the configuration that produced it.

For AMReye.AI, the first increments should establish the endpoint reader's capture, calibration, measurement, review and export chain. Advanced sensing, automation and predictive twins can develop through separate research questions that use those foundations. Their progress should be assessed individually, without making the initial product depend on every element of the long-term vision.

pages.title: Reader V1 engineering sequence
text: **Reader V1 should establish a complete, narrow workflow**

The near-term engineering sequence should prioritize controlled endpoint imaging and a traceable reviewed measurement. A small complete workflow is more informative than a collection of disconnected demonstrations because it exposes identity, calibration and state-management failures at their interfaces.
## Proposed sequence

First establish a repeatable optical arrangement and qualified capture records. Then develop spatial calibration and image-quality assessment. Add measurement with independent comparison, followed by controlled interpretation, review and export. Integrate service and recovery behavior before evaluating the workflow in a broader setting.
## Keep the biological method controlled

The reader should not change incubation or preparation conditions merely to simplify imaging. Any proposed method change requires a separate assessment. The exact reference components in the concluding BOM are a dated procurement configuration, not a commitment to a permanent chip generation or enclosure shape.

The programme should use explicit go/no-go decisions after each major uncertainty is tested. If the optical arrangement cannot meet the required field and measurement performance, software complexity should not be used to conceal the limitation. The appropriate response is to revise the arrangement or narrow the intended scope before proceeding.

pages.title: Optical bench development
text: **The optical bench should measure its own limitations**

Optical development should establish field coverage, sampling, distortion, focus behavior, illumination uniformity and stability. The bench should allow controlled comparison of alternatives without implying that the final product must use one fixed enclosure or station arrangement.
## Proposed bench programme

Use appropriate reference artifacts to characterize geometry and image formation, then evaluate representative biological appearances within authorized laboratory work. Record lens settings, distances, illumination, exposure and processing. A photograph of a clear plate is insufficient evidence of calibrated measurement performance.
## Compare alternatives on the same task

Conventional and telecentric optics, different illumination geometries and alternate acquisition settings should be compared using the intended measurement and service constraints. Telecentricity may reduce some magnification variation, but field size, cost and integration burden remain relevant. [R15]

The development report should separate object-plane sampling from achieved accuracy. A small nominal pixel pitch does not account for blur, distortion, calibration or boundary ambiguity. The selected arrangement should be justified by a measured uncertainty budget and practical reproducibility, with unresolved limitations carried into the next prototype rather than hidden by a high-resolution specification.
tables: Focus and distortion behavior across the intended region.

pages.title: Mechanical design and service access
text: **Mechanical design should support measurement and maintenance**

The mechanical system should hold relevant optical and sample relationships within their permitted ranges while allowing cleaning, service and safe operation. Plate loading, access and thermal behavior are part of the measurement design. A rigid-looking enclosure does not establish stability under actual use.
## Proposed design considerations

Candidate configurations should be assessed for vessel compatibility, repeatable placement, access to components, cable routing and contamination-sensitive surfaces. The design should avoid unnecessary crevices and provide materials and finishes appropriate to the cleaning process being qualified.
## Design for recovery from ordinary mistakes

Misloading should be detectable before measurement. Access panels and moving parts need appropriate safeguards. The instrument should make it clear when a service action requires recalibration or readiness checks before returning to use.

Early prototypes may use adjustable fixtures to explore geometry. A later production design should reduce unnecessary adjustment while retaining the controls needed for calibration and service. The transition should be supported by tolerance analysis and measured assembly variation. No particular multi-zone layout or final industrial form is fixed by this compendium; alternative configurations remain open to evidence-led selection.

pages.title: Electronics and power development
text: **Electronics should provide stable, observable power and signal paths**

Electronics development should define power domains, interfaces, protection, grounding and timing requirements before selecting components. Compute capability is only one requirement. Stable acquisition, manageable heat, serviceability and predictable failure behavior are equally relevant to a measurement instrument.
## Proposed electrical design record

The design should document expected and peak loads, supply tolerances, connection ratings and behavior during startup, shutdown and interruption. Sensor signals should retain appropriate conditioning and calibration. Loads such as illumination or motors should not be driven directly from interfaces that are not rated for them.
## Evaluate substitutions as system changes

A newer processor may offer more performance but introduce thermal, software or availability disadvantages. Selection should compare the actual workload, power envelope, support and validation burden. The concluding BOM records current candidates for one reference configuration; the main design remains generation-independent.

Custom electronics can later reduce wiring complexity or improve efficiency when the required interfaces and performance are stable. Before that transition, modular procurement can support rapid learning. Both stages require configuration records and verification of the complete signal and power path, especially where an electrical fault could produce a plausible but incorrect observation.

pages.title: Embedded software and control development
text: **Embedded control should make instrument state explicit**

The embedded layer coordinates acquisition, readiness checks, local storage and hardware status. Its design should distinguish commanded actions from confirmed outcomes. An image request, for example, is not a completed observation until the acquired data and associated record have been verified and stored.
## Proposed state model

Useful states include initialization, ready, acquiring, processing, awaiting review, degraded and faulted, with transitions defined by the relevant workflow. A physical-control subsystem may require additional states. The exact implementation can vary, but unsupported transitions should be rejected consistently.
## Keep timing and identity close to acquisition

The capture record should be created from the actual instrument event rather than reconstructed from a later filename or upload time. Clock status, sequence identifiers and configuration should remain available during offline operation.

Verification should challenge rapid repeated commands, power loss, full storage, unavailable sensors and invalid configuration. A responsive interface is not enough if background acquisition silently fails. The embedded layer should provide reliable evidence of what the instrument did, allowing higher-level AI and workflow software to reason from trustworthy observations rather than optimistic command status.

pages.title: Measurement software development
text: **Measurement software should preserve the numerical chain**

The measurement pipeline should connect the original image to calibrated geometry, quality assessment and a reviewable output. Each transformation needs a defined purpose and version. Preprocessing that improves visual appearance can change edge location or suppress small features, so its effect on the measurand must be evaluated.
## Proposed pipeline development

Begin with explicit geometric baselines and independently assessed boundaries. Compare candidate segmentation approaches on representative data, including ambiguous cases. Preserve calibration and image-coordinate transforms so that a reviewer can understand how a numerical diameter was obtained.
## Compare custom models with conventional methods

Custom models should be selected because they improve the defined task, not because a particular architecture is fashionable. A simpler algorithm may offer adequate performance, easier verification or lower compute demand. The comparison should include error, coverage, uncertainty and operational cost.

The pipeline should return explicit unavailable states when required evidence is missing. It should not manufacture a diameter from a low-confidence boundary or treat a failed calculation as zero. Later AI improvements can be introduced through controlled releases while historical records retain the exact measurement pipeline that produced them.

pages.title: PIMS and interface development
text: **PIMS development should begin with identity and record integrity**

PIMS is the proposed Plate Information Management System linking physical objects, observations, analyses and reviewer decisions. Its initial implementation should make those relationships reliable before adding advanced analytics or conversational features. A complete record path supports both product use and later research.
## Proposed implementation sequence

Define stable identifiers and the core event schema. Implement capture ingestion, calibration references and measurement records. Add review, correction and export with explicit version relationships. Then test recovery, retention and access behavior across the complete workflow.
## Interfaces should remain explicit

The field dictionaries in the appendices are proposed contracts. They identify the information that must survive between components, not a claim that every interface has been implemented. Implementation should validate required fields, units and allowed value states at the boundary.

Data migrations need their own verification. A new schema should preserve historical meaning and identify transformations rather than silently replacing old records. PIMS should make it possible to retrieve an original observation and reproduce or explain its result even after models, rules and interfaces have changed. That capability is central to the platform's long-term scientific and service value.

pages.title: Dataset operations and model development
text: **Dataset operations are an ongoing product capability**

Useful model development depends on consistent collection, annotation, quality assessment and release of authorized data. These activities should be treated as a managed operation rather than an occasional export from routine records. The process must preserve biological identity and the distinction between observation, reviewer judgment and confirmed reference evidence.
## Proposed dataset workflow

Collection plans should identify the evidence gaps they address. Incoming data are checked for completeness, permission, duplication and technical quality. Annotation uses defined instructions and expert review appropriate to the task. A release records its composition, lineage, known limitations and permitted use.
## Prioritize information, not volume alone

Active data selection may help identify uncertain or underrepresented cases for expert review. It should not distort the final evaluation population or turn model confidence into a biological reference. Collection priorities should consider rare failure modes and the practical cost of confirmation.

The proposed operation should support corrections to labels and permissions with clear downstream impact tracking. A revised annotation may affect a training release, while a withdrawn authorization may affect future use. Model development should remain connected to those governance events. This makes the data service useful for sustained research without assuming that every stored observation is automatically available for every future AI purpose.

pages.title: Design reviews and configuration control
text: **Design reviews should resolve specific technical decisions**

A design review should assess whether evidence supports the next development step. It should bring together the people responsible for measurement, software, biological interpretation, safety, manufacturing and service as appropriate. Its value lies in resolving assumptions and interfaces before they become expensive or difficult to change.
## Proposed review inputs

The review should include requirements, alternative designs, test results, unresolved issues and the configuration being assessed. A rendered concept or demonstration can communicate an idea, but it should not be mistaken for verified engineering evidence.
## Configuration control preserves comparability

Each prototype and test should identify the hardware, software, calibration and method context. A result from one configuration should not automatically support another. Changes to optics, mounting or preprocessing may alter measurement behavior even when the product name remains the same.

The proposed process should retain the decision and its evidence, with follow-up actions tied to a clear owner. This is product development discipline, not a requirement to freeze the platform's form prematurely. Flexible exploration remains possible when the conditions and consequences of each alternative are recorded well enough to compare them fairly.

topics.title: Manufacture, installation and service delivery
text: **Supplier qualification should address quality and continuity**

pages.title: Supplier qualification and substitution
text: **Supplier qualification should address quality and continuity**

Component selection should consider specification, authenticity, availability, support and the consequences of substitution. A low public price is useful procurement information, but it does not establish domestic stock, delivery to the intended location or suitability for a measurement product. The dated BOM therefore separates observed listings from quotations and unresolved procurement checks.
## Proposed supplier assessment

For critical components, the programme should identify authorized supply routes, revision control, documentation and incoming acceptance criteria. Supplier changes should trigger an assessment of whether the component's relevant behavior remains equivalent.
## Define critical characteristics

For a lens, focal length alone may be insufficient; mount, image circle, focus range and distortion can matter. For a power supply, connector fit does not establish electrical compatibility. Incoming checks should target the properties that affect the system rather than merely confirming that the item powers on.

The proposed programme should maintain alternatives where practical, but avoid claiming interchangeability before assessment. A substitution may require recalibration, software changes or additional validation. Procurement resilience comes from understanding these dependencies and planning qualification, not from listing many nominally similar products in a catalogue.

pages.title: Prototyping and design for manufacture
text: **Prototyping should answer questions about production as well as function**

An adjustable laboratory prototype can establish a measurement principle. A manufacturable design must also tolerate component variation, repeatable assembly, inspection, cleaning and service. The transition should preserve the function demonstrated on the bench while reducing dependence on individual craftsmanship or undocumented adjustment.
## Proposed design-for-manufacture review

The team should examine part count, tolerances, assembly sequence, fasteners, cable routing and access for inspection. Critical optical relationships should have a defined assembly and verification method. A design that requires repeated subjective alignment may be difficult to reproduce consistently.
## Pilot builds reveal different problems

A small series of controlled builds can expose variation that one prototype does not show. Record assembly time, rework, failed checks and measurement performance across units. These findings should inform design changes before claims about scalable manufacture are made.

The proposed vertical-integration strategy should retain this evidence-led approach. Custom parts can improve consistency when requirements are stable, while premature tooling can lock in unresolved assumptions. Manufacturing readiness should be demonstrated through repeatable builds and acceptance evidence, not inferred from a detailed rendering or a completed bill of materials.
tables: Analyze and measure its effect on calibration and field coverage.

pages.title: Assembly and production verification
text: **Production verification should establish the identity and readiness of each unit**

Each delivered instrument should have a traceable configuration and evidence that it meets the applicable production acceptance requirements. Assembly completion is not equivalent to measurement readiness. The acceptance process should verify the functions and critical characteristics that can vary between units.
## Proposed unit record

The record should identify the instrument, critical components, software and model versions, calibration, inspection results and disposition. Rework should remain visible, with the affected checks repeated as appropriate. A failed unit should not disappear from production quality statistics after repair.
## Acceptance criteria need a validated basis

Production checks should relate to design verification and validation. A convenient test is insufficient if it does not detect variation that can affect the result. The programme should establish whether a reference-artifact check predicts the relevant instrument behavior and what additional checks remain necessary.

Trend analysis across production can identify drift, supplier variation or an assembly problem. Such findings should enter corrective action and configuration review. The proposed process supports consistent delivery while preserving the distinction between unit acceptance and the broader clinical or analytical evidence supporting the product's intended use.

pages.title: Calibration transfer to production
text: **Calibration must transfer from development to routine production**

The calibration method should be reproducible across instruments and service locations. It needs appropriate reference artifacts, environmental conditions, calculation methods and acceptance criteria. A calibration performed successfully by the development team does not establish that the same result can be obtained reliably during production or field service.
## Proposed transfer package

The package should define the reference target, placement, acquisition settings, computation and independent verification. It should specify what invalidates calibration and how out-of-tolerance findings affect prior measurements. Traceability should be appropriate to the measurand and intended uncertainty. [R16]
## Assess the calibration operator and fixture

Placement variation, target wear and interpretation of instructions can affect results. A transfer study should include the people and equipment expected to perform calibration. It should measure repeatability and identify where fixtures or clearer instructions reduce variability.

The instrument should store calibration identity and validity with each measurement. Replacing a lens, altering focus or changing a relevant image pipeline can require requalification. Service should therefore include both the physical replacement and the evidence needed to restore measurement readiness. Calibration is a continuing product responsibility rather than a one-time factory certificate detached from subsequent changes.
tables: Identity, uncertainty or verification basis and condition.

pages.title: Installation and site acceptance
text: **Installation should verify the actual operating environment**

Site acceptance establishes that the delivered instrument and workflow are ready for the intended local use. It should assess the environment, configuration, interfaces and trained users. A successful factory test does not establish that power, networking, space and laboratory procedures at the destination are suitable.
## Proposed installation assessment

The site should confirm placement, relevant environmental limits, electrical arrangements and authorized network access. The instrument configuration and calibration should be checked after transport. Interfaces should be verified with the receiving laboratory system using appropriate test records.
## Agree on responsibility before routine use

The laboratory and service team should understand who performs readiness checks, calibration review, software updates and incident escalation. The installation record should identify limitations or local restrictions. Unresolved issues should lead to a defined disposition rather than an assumption that ordinary use will reveal whether they matter.

The proposed acceptance process should preserve evidence of unsuccessful checks and their resolution. Where the product remains investigational, site activities must follow the authorized study and regulatory conditions. Installation of a prototype does not itself establish clinical approval or qualification for routine diagnostic reporting.

pages.title: Training and operational handover
text: **Training should prepare users for normal work and exceptions**

Operational handover should ensure that intended users understand the product's scope, critical tasks and limits. Training should cover ordinary capture and review as well as identity conflicts, unreadable images, corrections and recovery. Users should know when to stop and seek support rather than improvise around a failed control.
## Proposed training structure

Role-specific instruction can separate operator, reviewer, administrator and service responsibilities. Practical exercises should use appropriate examples with known teaching objectives. Synthetic examples are useful for rare software states, while real authorized images are needed for relevant visual interpretation skills.
## Evaluate understanding after instruction

Attendance does not establish competency. Assessment should use independent examples and critical scenarios appropriate to the role. Refresher training may be needed after significant interface or workflow changes. Records should identify what was assessed and any limitations in authorization.

The proposed handover should include usable instructions, service contacts and a clear support process. Language and accessibility should be evaluated with intended users. The objective is dependable operation within a qualified scope, not reliance on the development team's continued presence to explain ambiguous behavior or resolve every routine exception.
tables: Correct association and recognition of incomplete acquisition.

pages.title: Maintenance and support delivery
text: **Service delivery should restore a qualified function**

Maintenance and support are part of the proposed product portfolio. Their purpose is to keep instruments and records dependable over the service life. A repair is complete when the affected function has been verified, not merely when a replacement part has been installed or an error message has disappeared.
## Proposed service workflow

Support begins with a clear description of the fault, instrument identity and affected workflow. Remote diagnostics should use only authorized data. On-site or depot work should preserve configuration, record replaced components and identify any need for recalibration or software requalification.
## Service terms should match evidence and capacity

Response times, availability commitments and maintenance intervals should be established from the actual delivery model and field evidence. They are not fixed promises in this compendium. The programme should measure time to diagnosis, restoration and recurrence alongside user burden.

The service portfolio can include calibration, preventive maintenance, training, interface support and research assistance. Each requires a defined scope and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance may later improve planning, but it should complement mandatory checks and confirmed service findings. A model's low failure-risk estimate cannot override evidence that an instrument is outside its qualified operating condition.

pages.title: Fleet updates and rollback
text: **Fleet updates should be reversible and traceable**

Software, models and standards content may change during the product's life. The proposed update process should establish what is changing, which units are eligible and what evidence supports deployment. Historical records must retain the versions that produced their results, even after the instrument is updated.
## Proposed staged deployment

An update should be verified in a controlled environment, then introduced through a defined deployment sequence with monitoring and rollback criteria. Compatibility checks should include hardware, calibration, data schema and interfaces. The update should not interrupt a critical operation without a qualified transition plan.
## A rollback is more than replacing an executable

Database migrations, changed calibration and new result semantics can make reversal difficult. The design should specify which changes are reversible and how records created under a newer version remain interpretable. A rollback must not erase the audit trail of the attempted update.

Fleet monitoring should identify affected configurations and sites without collecting unnecessary patient information. If a defect can affect prior results, the quality process should assess the scope and appropriate communication. The proposed system should support that investigation through version lineage, rather than relying on users to remember when their instrument changed.

topics.title: Custom electronics, silicon and technology transfer
text: **Custom electronics should follow stable measurement requirements**

pages.title: Custom electronics strategy
text: **Custom electronics should follow stable measurement requirements**

Vertical integration can improve power efficiency, signal quality, assembly consistency or serviceability when the product's requirements are sufficiently understood. The proposed strategy begins with modular, available components for learning and moves toward custom boards where measured benefits justify the engineering and qualification burden.
## Candidate integration stages

An early custom board might organize power, illumination control and sensor interfaces while retaining a replaceable compute module. Later revisions could integrate acquisition or specialized processing. The sequence should follow bottlenecks demonstrated in the actual workload.
## Custom does not automatically mean better

Integration can create shared failure modes and make replacement more difficult. It can also increase dependence on a specific supplier or fabrication process. The comparison should include lifecycle support, test access and recovery from component obsolescence.

Each custom revision should retain verification points for critical signals and power domains. Production testing and calibration must be planned alongside circuit design. The long-term objective is an efficient and dependable platform whose custom elements serve demonstrated needs. No custom electronic assembly or manufacturing readiness is claimed as completed merely because this strategy is described.
tables: Reduced wiring or improved reliability without unacceptable coupling.

pages.title: Custom model and silicon strategy
text: **Custom models and eventual silicon require different maturity gates**

AMReye.AI intends to develop task-specific models and may eventually investigate specialized silicon for efficient inference or acquisition. Custom model development can begin while hardware remains modular. Custom silicon requires a much more stable workload, interface and support strategy because its physical implementation is harder to revise.
## Establish the workload before specializing it

The programme should measure inference latency, memory use, energy, accuracy and uncertainty on representative tasks. Model compression or acceleration must preserve the behavior required by the validated workflow. A smaller model that changes abstention or rare-error behavior needs appropriate reassessment.
## Preserve an update and service path

Clinical knowledge, standards and model requirements evolve. A specialized design should keep appropriate functions updateable and avoid hard-coding assumptions that are likely to change. Standards interpretation, in particular, should remain independently versioned rather than embedded as an immutable hardware truth.

The ambition for deep customization is a staged strategy, not a claim that every chip is currently designed in-house. Selection should follow measured performance, power, quality, availability and lifecycle needs. The newest commercial component is not automatically the best choice, and a custom component is not automatically the most efficient solution for a still-changing research workload.
tables: Independent task performance and reproducible training.

pages.title: Partnerships and technology transfer
text: **Partnerships should define contributions and evidence ownership**

The proposed platform can benefit from laboratory, engineering, manufacturing and research partnerships. Each partnership should identify the problem being addressed, the work each party performs and the outputs each receives. A broad expression of interest should not be represented as a secured collaboration or completed validation.
## Proposed collaboration structure

A laboratory partner may contribute workflow expertise and authorized evaluation material. An engineering partner may support optics, electronics or manufacturing. A research partner may develop methods or independent analysis. These contributions need compatible quality, data and intellectual-property arrangements.
## Technology transfer needs reproducibility

A design or model is transferable when another qualified team can reproduce the relevant function using the supplied specifications, procedures and evidence. Source code or a drawing alone may be insufficient. Calibration, test fixtures, training and quality controls can be equally important.

The programme should assess whether a partner can maintain the intended quality and service responsibilities. Transfer should preserve configuration and evidence lineage so that local changes do not inherit unsupported claims. The product compendium describes the proposed collaboration model; it does not announce any institution, supplier or regulator as an appointed or committed partner.

pages.title: Development decisions and exit criteria
text: **Exit criteria should decide what the evidence permits next**

Development decisions should connect the current evidence to a bounded next step. A successful prototype may justify a more representative evaluation, while a failed assumption may justify redesign or restriction. The decision should state what has been demonstrated and which uncertainties remain material.
## Decide on evidence rather than accumulated features

A larger sensor catalogue, more AI functions or a more elaborate enclosure does not establish a better product. The relevant question is whether each addition improves the defined measurement, workflow or research capability enough to justify its complexity and risk.

The programme should maintain alternative paths where major uncertainties remain. For example, an imaging-only reader can progress while a gas-sensing hypothesis is tested separately. Failure of an exploratory modality should not invalidate a qualified function that does not depend on it.

The long-term AMReye.AI vision combines instruments, software, data and services around traceable observation. Its execution should produce evidence that partners can inspect and users can rely on. Each released capability should carry a clear scope, support model and maturity statement, while future research remains visible as an opportunity requiring its own proof.

topics.title: Record interfaces and field dictionaries
text: **Proposed interfaces preserve evidence across transformations**

pages.title: Interface catalogue and record relationships
text: **Proposed interfaces preserve evidence across transformations**

The following dictionaries document proposed record contracts. They are design specifications for review, not a claim that an API, database or device interface has been implemented. Field names are illustrative and can be revised through schema governance without changing the underlying provenance requirements.
## Record relationships

A specimen or research sample can produce multiple preparations and plates. Each plate can have multiple capture attempts. Observations and measurements reference the exact capture or biological context that produced them. Interpretations and reviewer decisions reference immutable versions of those results.
## Shared semantics

Every record should have a unique identifier, schema version, creation time and originating system. A revision should identify the prior version without overwriting it. Missing data require a reason rather than a plausible default.

The value state should distinguish **measured, derived, imputed, simulated and unavailable**. These states describe origin, not quality. A measured value can be unreliable; a simulated value can be useful within its research scope. Quality, eligibility and review disposition therefore require separate fields. The export contract should preserve these distinctions so that another system cannot silently convert an estimate into an observation.

pages.title: Capture record field dictionary
text: **A capture record identifies an acquisition attempt, including failure**

The proposed capture contract separates the planned observation from the image actually obtained. An unsuccessful attempt still produces an auditable event. A later successful capture has its own identifier and timestamp; it does not replace the missing earlier observation.
## Validation rules

An image hash cannot be supplied when no image exists. A failed capture must not receive a fabricated zero-size image or a copied prior frame. If the clock is unreliable, the system should retain that uncertainty and avoid unsupported temporal analysis.

Image orientation and coordinate conventions should be explicit so that a measurement region remains reproducible after export. Storage references should not expose unrestricted access to confidential images. The proposed consumer should verify integrity and eligibility before analysis, then retain the original bytes alongside any normalized derivative. A recapture can resolve an image-quality problem while leaving a gap in a time series that still requires disclosure.

pages.title: Sensor observation field dictionary
text: **A sensor observation retains its raw signal and interpretation state**

The proposed contract accommodates biological signals, environmental measurements and instrument-control channels. A common format should not imply that these channels have the same biological meaning. Each observation needs a defined quantity and context.
## Preserve different kinds of absence

A disconnected channel, a value below a detection limit and a channel not installed are different states. The record should not encode all three as zero. A below-range observation should retain the bound and method context where known.

Compensation should produce a derived value linked to the raw signal and conversion version. If several channels share a compensation input, that dependency should remain inspectable. Downstream fusion should receive both the value and its quality state, including any timing mismatch. This allows a model or reviewer to distinguish biological disagreement from a sensor that was never eligible to contribute.

pages.title: Calibration record field dictionary
text: **Calibration records define where a conversion is valid**

A calibration is a relationship between a known reference and an instrument response under stated conditions. The proposed record should preserve the artifact, procedure and results needed to understand that relationship. A calibration identifier alone is insufficient if its scope is inaccessible.
## Consumer responsibilities

The proposed measurement service should verify that a calibration matches the actual configuration and operating domain. An expired, superseded or incompatible record should not be selected merely because it is the most recent entry.

Changes to lens position, camera orientation, mechanical alignment or relevant firmware can require reassessment. The record should support those decisions without automatically assuming every change has the same impact. Historical measurements retain their original calibration reference. If a later investigation changes their interpretation, the correction should identify the affected records and preserve the original result rather than silently rewriting its metrological history.

pages.title: Measurement record field dictionary
text: **A measurement record links a quantity to the evidence used to estimate it**

The proposed measurement contract supports zone diameters and other defined image-derived quantities. It separates an algorithm's geometric output from standards interpretation and final review. A numeric diameter should not implicitly carry a susceptibility category.
## Corrections and unavailable values

A reviewer-adjusted boundary should create a new measurement version linked to the original and the associated decision. A missing or unreadable zone should use an unavailable state with a reason. It should not use a conventional numeric value that another system might interpret as a real diameter.

The record should retain sufficient precision for analysis while applying any required reporting convention only at the appropriate stage. If rounding affects interpretation, the selected rule should be explicit and reproducible. Geometry should remain tied to the source coordinate system so that a reviewer can inspect the exact boundary behind the number.

pages.title: AI output field dictionary
text: **An AI output is a versioned inference with a defined task**

The proposed interface should make an inference reproducible and distinguish it from a reviewed conclusion. Different capabilities may return geometry, a quality flag, a forecast or a ranked research hypothesis. Their outputs should declare their semantics instead of sharing an ambiguous confidence field.
## Confidence is not automatically probability

A raw score, calibrated probability and prediction interval are different objects. The contract should identify which is being returned and under which validation conditions it has meaning. A percentage should not be displayed simply because it looks intuitive.

The system should preserve outputs from failed or abstaining runs for investigation where appropriate, while preventing them from becoming reportable conclusions. A later model version may produce a different answer to the same image. That new inference should be linked as a separate analysis, retaining the earlier output and the reviewer decisions that relied on it. Retrospective reanalysis does not silently revise a previously authorized report.

pages.title: Standards interpretation field dictionary
text: **Standards interpretation is a traceable transformation of eligible evidence**

The proposed interpretation record should bind a measurement to the exact standards package and biological context used. Standards content requires independent version control, including corrections. It should not be embedded invisibly in a model artifact or inferred from the current date.
## No cross-method fallback

The absence of an eligible rule should result in an unresolved interpretation. An endpoint rule should not be substituted for an early reading, and a rule for one organism should not be applied to another because their measurements appear similar. [R01] [R02] [R04]

The proposed interface should preserve a readable explanation of the rule selection. When standards change, historical reports retain their original interpretation basis. Any authorized re-interpretation should create a new version with a reason and a clear relationship to the earlier record. This supports clinical governance without erasing the conditions under which an earlier decision was made.

pages.title: Reviewer decision field dictionary
text: **Reviewer decisions identify exactly what was accepted or changed**

Mandatory review in Reader V1 requires more than a generic approval flag. The proposed decision record should identify the evidence shown, the versions reviewed and the action taken. Changes to material inputs should invalidate approval of the affected result until the revised evidence is reviewed.
## A review must be informed

The interface should expose the original image, relevant quality flags, calibration context and proposed boundary. It should identify simulated or unavailable data clearly. A reviewer should not have to infer which version is being approved from a mutable screen.

Bulk review may be useful for eligible routine cases, but the workflow must preserve the ability to inspect exceptions and define what the bulk action covers. A correction should retain both the initial and revised measurements. The service should prevent export of an obsolete approval after an upstream change, and should show the specific reason that another review is required.

pages.title: Export and provenance field dictionary
text: **An export is an authorized snapshot with a verifiable delivery outcome**

The proposed export contract should preserve the meaning of the reviewed result across system boundaries. A successful network connection does not prove that the receiving system accepted the correct record or interpreted its units and states properly.
## Transfer and correction behavior

Retries should use an idempotency mechanism so that an uncertain acknowledgement does not create duplicate reports. A receiver rejection should remain visible, with a reason and an authorized recovery path. The instrument should retain the source record even if a destination is temporarily unavailable.

If an approved result changes after export, the workflow should issue a traceable correction or replacement according to the receiving system's conventions. It should not silently resend altered content under the same immutable identity. Research exports must preserve prediction labels and access restrictions. Public publication of a summary is a separate decision from authorized transfer of detailed laboratory records.

topics.title: Worked record and recovery examples
text: **Synthetic example: a reviewed endpoint measurement**

pages.title: Worked example of a reviewed endpoint record
text: **Synthetic example: a reviewed endpoint measurement**

This example illustrates proposed record relationships using invented identifiers and values. It is not a patient result, validation observation or clinical interpretation. No susceptibility breakpoint is applied.
## Example event sequence

A qualified capture of synthetic plate EX-PLATE-001 produces image EX-IMG-01. Calibration EX-CAL-04 is eligible for the illustrated configuration. The initial derived diameter is 18.6 mm. A reviewer identifies an incorrectly placed boundary and creates a revised measurement of 18.2 mm, retaining both versions.
## What the example demonstrates

The corrected number is not substituted into the original record. The reviewer action explains why a new measurement exists, and the absent interpretation remains absent. A measurement review can be complete while a clinical result remains unavailable.

An export for a permitted research purpose could include the reviewed diameter, its derivation and the unresolved interpretation state. It should not insert a susceptible or resistant category merely to satisfy a required field in another system. If the receiving schema cannot represent this state, the export should fail with a meaningful mapping error rather than invent a clinical conclusion.

pages.title: Worked example of interrupted observation
text: **Synthetic example: observation stops while simulation continues**

This invented sequence illustrates the proposed digital-twin contract. Times are relative to an explicitly defined research observation start. Values are illustrative and do not describe measured AMReye.AI performance or biological growth.
## Evidence and forecast branches

The final successful observation occurs at 24 hours. A planned 26-hour capture fails, and the physical plate is subsequently unavailable. A previously qualified research model can be run conditionally from the last observed state. Its outputs remain simulations and cannot be relabeled as recovered measurements.
## When continuation should stop

If the model has no validated horizon for the new conditions, the result should remain exploratory or be withheld. A user request for a longer animation should not extend the qualified prediction domain. The record should distinguish computation completed from prediction eligible for use.

If later observations become available from the same verified physical plate, they form new evidence. They can update the model state and support a comparison with earlier forecasts, but should not overwrite the historical predictions. If the replacement is a different plate, it needs a different physical identity even when prepared from related material.

pages.title: Worked example of disagreement and recovery
text: **Synthetic example: disagreement triggers investigation and recapture**

This invented case illustrates a proposed recovery workflow. A plate image passes a simple brightness check, but the focus assessment fails. An environmental channel also reports an out-of-range condition. Neither a majority vote among checks nor a plausible-looking diameter is sufficient to authorize the result.
## Proposed sequence

The system retains the initial capture, the failed checks and the attempted measurement as ineligible. A reviewer investigates the setup and identifies a positioning problem. The environmental condition is assessed separately; it is not assumed to share the same cause merely because it occurred at the same time.
## Recovery has a biological boundary

A successful recapture can resolve an optical defect. It cannot automatically undo an inappropriate incubation condition or recreate a missed observation time. The reviewer must decide whether the underlying plate remains eligible for the intended method.

The proposed audit should retain both resolved and unresolved causes. This allows later analysis of common faults and prevents the system from learning that any recapture is an acceptable remedy. Recovery is complete when the relevant measurement and workflow are qualified again, with a documented reason for using or rejecting the resulting evidence.

topics.title: Glossary and cross-reference index
text: **Biological terms should identify the phenomenon being discussed**

pages.title: Glossary of biological terms
text: **Biological terms should identify the phenomenon being discussed**

These concise definitions support reading the compendium. Operational definitions for a study must additionally specify the assay, conditions and endpoint. The glossary does not replace current laboratory methods or clinical standards.
## Language and inference

“Candidate minority growth” describes an observation for investigation. “Confirmed heteroresistance” describes a biological conclusion supported by the relevant method. “Predicted resistance determinant” describes a computational inference, while a measured molecular result has a different evidence path.

Using these distinctions consistently helps the reader see where the platform measures a signal and where further characterization is required. Tolerance and persistence terminology follows the cited consensus; the applications chapters explain its limits for imaging. [R10] [R65]

pages.title: Glossary of measurement terms
text: **Measurement terms separate resolution, uncertainty and reliability**

The quantity being measured should always be stated. A specification in pixels, micrometres or milliseconds does not automatically express the quality of the final biological result. The same term can otherwise be misread across optics, software and clinical evaluation.
## Units and reporting

Zone diameters are expressed in millimetres. Optical object sampling may be expressed in micrometres per pixel. Relative humidity is expressed as % RH, while temperatures require an explicit scale. Time-to-result claims require both a unit and a starting event.

A confidence interval for a study estimate is not the same as uncertainty assigned to a single instrument measurement. The validation protocol should state which quantity an interval describes, how it was obtained and which conditions it covers. The sensing and calibration chapters apply these distinctions to candidate technologies. [R16]

pages.title: Glossary of software and twin terms
text: **Software and twin terms retain the origin of information**
These definitions distinguish stored evidence, transformations and predictions. They are intended to support a shared vocabulary across scientific, engineering and laboratory review.
## Terms for platform scope

“Lab-in-a-box” denotes an integrated workflow concept; it does not imply that every laboratory function fits within one enclosure. “Lab-on-a-chip” denotes miniaturized functions implemented on an appropriate chip or microfluidic substrate. Neither term establishes clinical completeness.

The proposed “hive mind” is a coordinated, governed learning and analysis concept across authorized data sources. It does not imply unrestricted access to laboratory records or automatic trust in outputs from other instruments.

pages.title: Reader V1 BOM configuration and price basis
text: **Reader V1 reference configuration, priced 13–14 September 2026**

This eight-page BOM describes one coherent endpoint imaging reference configuration. It uses a manually loaded plate, controlled visible illumination, a fixed camera, local computation and mandatory human review. It is a prototype procurement basis, not a released manufacturing drawing or a clinically qualified instrument.
## Configuration boundary

The reference uses a Raspberry Pi 5 with 8 GB RAM, an HQ C/CS-mount camera and a 16 mm C-mount lens. A separate 12 V adapter supplies the proposed illumination assembly. The computer uses its official USB-C supply. The reference assumes an existing monitor, keyboard and mouse for local review; these are not included in the hardware total.
## Procurement status

Forty line items are specified. Named candidate parts and merchant SKUs are retained where verified. Custom assemblies and unresolved commodity selections have explicit quotation gaps. No order, stock reservation or destination-specific checkout was completed. Formal quotation dates are therefore unavailable; the stated dates are public-listing observation dates.

The lens and camera cable listings were sold out at observation. Several other items were listed in stock, but neither an Indian storefront nor a dispatch claim establishes confirmed delivery to the project. Before purchase, verify exact variants, invoice treatment, regional plugs, lead times and the complete assembled compatibility.

text: **Local capture and review without a separate accelerator**

The selected board is a current candidate for a modest endpoint workload. Its inclusion is not a measured throughput claim. Thermal, storage and power behavior require verification under the actual capture and analysis software. [R47] [R48]
## Compatibility and sourcing

Lines 01–03 use Thingbits listings observed on 14 September 2026. Line 04 uses the Robocraze listing observed on 13 September. The remaining amounts are engineering allowances; exact commodity SKUs and the RTC assembly quotation remain open.

The active cooler should use the board's intended connector and mounting arrangement. The microSD selection is 64 GB with no preinstalled operating system; the manufacturer's full card suffix, authenticity and write endurance require confirmation. A sustained-write and abrupt-power-loss test should precede use with important records.

The micro-HDMI cable supports an existing review display. The RTC battery supports timekeeping and is not a power backup. Network access should use an authorized local connection. No cloud subscription, GPU accelerator, display, keyboard or mouse is included in this configuration.

pages.title: Reader V1 BOM camera and optics
text: **A C/CS optical path with an explicitly qualified field of view**
The selected camera is the C/CS-mount, camera-only variant. The M12 variant is not interchangeable with this lens plan. The included adapter is counted once. [R46] [B12]
## Geometric feasibility calculation

Using a 4.712 mm sensor height and a 110 mm illustrative object field gives magnification about 0.0428. A 16 mm thin-lens approximation then places the object about 390 mm from the principal plane. This is an optical design estimate, not a final enclosure dimension. Nominal object sampling is about 36.2 micrometres per pixel, not measurement accuracy.

The lens listing's minimum object distance is 0.2 m; actual focus, field coverage, distortion and edge quality still require a bench check. The frame should allow adjustment and stable locking. The camera cable must be the 15-pin standard to 22-pin mini camera type for the selected board, not a display cable. Place the compute board near the camera so a 300 mm cable is sufficient.
The lens and cable were listed sold out on 13 September. Obtain equivalent exact-part quotations before procurement; do not silently replace the focal length or cable pinout.

pages.title: Reader V1 BOM illumination and calibration
text: **An engineered light path and a traceable geometric reference**

All eight amounts below are engineering allowances, not commercial quotations. The proposed visible-light assembly uses 12 V DC with a design ceiling of 12 W. Spectral selection and geometry remain open until the optical bench establishes adequate contrast and uniformity.
## Selection and validation requirements

The LED assembly should operate at a stable acquisition condition. The enable board is proposed to switch the low-voltage load using a qualified 3.3 V control interface; it must not draw LED current from a GPIO pin. Continuous DC illumination is the reference mode. Any later dimming or pulsed operation requires exposure-synchronization evaluation.

The calibration artifact allowance is a quotation gap, not a guarantee that INR 12,000 buys the required certificate or uncertainty. Select the artifact after defining the measurand, field and uncertainty budget. The neutral target is for relative intensity checks unless independently characterized. A printed ruler or uncalibrated gray card cannot substitute for traceable geometric calibration.

Diffuser, reflector, baffle and heat-spreader materials require cleanability, stability and optical verification. Their costs must be replaced by supplier quotations after dimensions and material grades are fixed.

## Fit and serviceability

The frame must accommodate the optical working distance established on the bench, the selected plate field and stable camera mounting. The holder should locate the intended plate family reproducibly without obscuring relevant growth or labels. A different plate size requires a separate fit and field-of-view check.

The removable tray and enclosure should support the laboratory's qualified cleaning procedure. Hinges, latches and feet should preserve stability during normal loading. Fasteners and standoffs are a single kit allowance; final quantities belong in controlled assembly drawings.

The initial identification path uses image-readable labels or manually verified identifiers within the proposed review workflow. A separate barcode scanner and printer are not included. Supplier selection, material grades, tolerances and fabrication lead times remain quotation and engineering gaps for every item on this page.

topics.title: Executive summary
text: AMReye.AI APEX XR is the top-of-the-line clinical + research + bio-automation configuration of the AMReye.AI platform. It is conceived as a modular benchtop workstation, not a compact first product. Its purpose is to unite standardized plate imaging, direct broth microdilution, controlled incubation, research phenomics, multimodal sensing, plate and liquid handling, traceable data management and laboratory orchestration in one system.

The product thesis is practical: preserve accepted microbiology methods, instrument them, make their execution observable, and convert every sample into a reviewable digital record. The clinical pathway begins with measurement and workflow support; the research pathway uses the same chamber, optics and automation to produce time-resolved phenotypic datasets.

ONE-SENTENCE POSITIONING
AMR-Eye APEX XR is an AI-native microbiology workstation designed to digitize, standardize and automate plate-based AST, direct MIC and research phenotyping while keeping a qualified human in control of every reportable result.

topics.title: What the flagship is - and is not
text: It is the eventual maximum configuration that demonstrates the full AMReye.AI platform architecture.
It is not the ₹7.5 lakh milestone-linked PoC and initial-validation funding scope.
It is not evidence that every subsystem has already been built or integrated.
It is not a replacement for a biosafety cabinet, laboratory quality system or qualified microbiologist.
It does not claim six-hour clinical turnaround except in separately validated, method-specific rapid AST workflows such as applicable EUCAST RAST conditions [S13].
It does not infer an exact MIC from a disk-diffusion zone. Direct MIC is produced through a broth microdilution workflow [S15].

topics.title: Positioning
text: AMReye.AI should be positioned as an AMR/AST-first modular microbiology platform that can expand into research and laboratory automation. It should not be positioned as the only AI plate-imaging system: established products already validate smart incubation, digital imaging, AI plate analysis, automated ID/AST and full laboratory automation [S16-S19].

topics.title: Why a flagship is necessary
text: Architecture proof: demonstrates how optics, biology, safety, AI, robotics and records fit into one coherent system.
Technical ceiling: creates a high-performance reference platform for algorithm development and assay validation.
Partner platform: gives hospitals, universities, pharma labs and OEMs a common integration target.
Product-family anchor: allows Lite, Core and Clinical products to inherit validated components without carrying every research module.
Commercial signaling: supports premium enterprise and research use cases while the lower tiers address affordability.

EVIDENCE RULE
A feature appearing in a proposal is a design input, not proof of implementation. The development team should maintain a capability-evidence matrix linking each claim to a test report, dataset, risk control and approval state.

Vision, sensor fusion, robotics planning, local model inference
Industrial HMI/control computer, PIMS database, integration gateway
Operator workflow, local records, report review, LIS/LIMS interfaces
STM32-class safety controller, watchdogs, sensor acquisition, deterministic control
Thermal loops, motion limits, lighting triggers and safety interlocks
Plate queue, metrology station, research imaging, MIC deck, gas and environment control
Biological process space with cleanable, controlled, observable conditions
Medical-grade PSU class, UPS, LiFePO4 backup, protective devices, HEPA path
Safe energy delivery, controlled shutdown and fault containment

topics.title: Data and control flow
text: Every transition is logged in the Plate Information Management System (PIMS). Raw data are retained with hashes, timestamps, calibration identifiers, software/model versions and user actions so a result can be reconstructed.
tables: Calibrated images + temperature + humidity + gas + weight + position
Measurement models -> structured standards rules -> QC -> confidence
Technician review -> signed result -> LIS/LIMS/report -> optional de-identified analytics

topics.title: Dual imaging architecture
tables: 31 MP monochrome global-shutter camera + large-field telecentric lens + calibrated transmitted illumination
Kinematic plate nest, fiducials, barcode, environmental history and repeatable focus/height
High-sensitivity color/RGB-NIR camera + epi/oblique/dark-field/NIR + optional fluorescence
Purpose: disc localization, zone-boundary measurement, dimensional repeatability and microdilution well reading
Purpose: one plate identity and one digital twin across both paths
Purpose: pigment, morphology, time-lapse, reporter signals, texture and exploratory phenomics

METROLOGY CORRECTION
Telecentric optics reduce perspective error but do not create sub-micron whole-plate accuracy. System-level accuracy, repeatability, uncertainty and edge performance must be established using traceable artifacts and the final camera-lens-lighting-mechanics stack.

topics.title: Updated flagship hardware stack
text: Named components are reference classes for an engineering build. Production selection must also consider lifecycle, regional availability, environmental ratings, serviceability, EMC, calibration, supplier qualification and regulatory evidence.
tables: Jetson AGX Thor developer kit for development; T5000 module + qualified carrier for production [S6-S7]
Essential to APEX; right-size for lower tiers
STM32H7-class MCU, isolated I/O, independent watchdogs and hardware cut-outs
Industrial touch display and separate control computer with encrypted local storage
Teledyne FLIR Oryx ORX-10G-310S9M class: 31 MP, global shutter, 10GigE [S9]
0.238x large-field TitanTL class, ~122.7 mm horizontal FOV on APS-H; final sensor pairing and plate coverage require optical validation [S8]
High-sensitivity color camera with visible and 940 nm NIR response; filterable optical path
Transmitted, epi, oblique, dark-field, polarized, 940 nm NIR and switchable fluorescence channels
