Eight-channel BME690-class gas-sensor array with controlled sampling and reference channel [S10]
VL53L8CX 8x8 ToF sensor for position, proximity and gross depth [S11]
Laser triangulation, structured light or chromatic/confocal profilometry
Insulated chamber, PT100-class sensing, bidirectional thermal control, active humidity management
O2/CO2 sensing, regulated ports, valves/flow controllers, pressure and exhaust management
Calibrated optical scattering with reference channel and tube identification
96-well broth microdilution deck with transmitted optical reading, kinetic imaging and plate map
24-48 plate queue, barcode/RFID, guarded robotic transport and recovery positions
Essential to flagship automation; not PoC
Purpose-built 8/12-channel pipetting and dispensing module with disposable tips
Medical-grade PSU class, UPS, LiFePO4 backup, emergency stop, fuses, leakage/temperature monitoring

topics.title: Jetson AGX Thor / T5000 rationale
text: The Jetson AGX Thor developer kit combines a T5000 system-on-module, Blackwell GPU, 128 GB memory and up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS within a 40-130 W operating envelope. NVIDIA positions the developer kit for development and testing; production devices should use a production module and a qualified or custom carrier [S6-S7].
tables: Run metrology, RGB/NIR/fluorescence analysis, sensor fusion and robotics services without serializing every workload.
Support high-resolution image pipelines, temporal models and local multimodal tools with margin for development.
Potentially reserve compute resources for critical vision services while lower-priority analytics run in parallel; this is not a safety certification.
Connect 10GigE imaging, NVMe data storage and robotics/control gateways.
Use CUDA, TensorRT, containers and model tooling for repeatable deployment.
High cost, heat and power. Thor is justified for the flagship reference platform, not automatically for Lite/Core production.

topics.title: Three-zone Bio-Vault chassis
tables: A separated Logic Deck, biological chamber and Power/Safety Bay in a cleanable benchtop enclosure.
Isolates compute heat and electrical risk from controlled biological conditions; provides a stable geometry for optics and robotics.
The flagship combines high-power compute, sensitive measurement and cultures; physical segregation simplifies thermal design, cleaning and service.
Anodized aluminium structural members, stainless or chemical-resistant internal surfaces, replaceable liners and service-access panels balance stiffness, hygiene and manufacturability.

topics.title: STM32-class Reflex controller
tables: A deterministic microcontroller and safety I/O layer independent of the AI operating system.
Runs temperature/humidity control, light triggers, motor limits, door/UV interlocks, watchdogs and fault shutdown.
A Linux crash, AI overload or update must not disable basic safety or sample protection.
Industrial MCU class offers deterministic timing, mature peripherals, hardware watchdogs and long-term embedded support.

topics.title: Industrial HMI / Interface computer
tables: A separate operator-facing computer with touchscreen, local database and gateway services.
Guides workflows, stores local records, shows images and boundaries, manages users, and interfaces with LIS/LIMS.
Separating UX and records from high-load AI improves resilience and permits controlled updates.
Industrial PC or serviceable SBC class with encrypted NVMe and supported OS; exact platform should follow lifecycle and cybersecurity review.

topics.title: Jetson Thor / T5000 Cortex
tables: A high-performance edge AI node based on the Thor platform [S6-S7].
Executes high-resolution vision, model inference, sensor fusion and automation planning locally.
APEX is a development/reference ceiling and must support multiple simultaneous pipelines without cloud dependence.
Thor/T5000 provides exceptional memory and AI headroom; the developer kit is for engineering, while a production module and carrier are the deployment path.
Essential for flagship; optional/right-sized in lower tiers

topics.title: Clinical metrology camera
tables: A 31 MP monochrome global-shutter, 10GigE industrial camera class [S9].
Captures stable, high-resolution whole-plate and well images for dimensional and optical measurement.
Clinical measurement requires repeatability, trigger control, low geometric ambiguity and traceable acquisition settings.
Monochrome global-shutter machine vision avoids Bayer interpolation for edge measurement and supports synchronized illumination; final performance is system-dependent.

topics.title: Whole-plate telecentric lens
tables: A large-field telecentric lens class capable of covering a plate-scale field on a large sensor [S8].
Reduces magnification change with object distance and perspective distortion across the field.
Disk-diffusion zone measurement is sensitive to parallax and plate placement, especially near edges.
A TitanTL-class optic offers an unusually large field and specified telecentricity/distortion; the exact camera-lens pairing, FOV, working distance and uncertainty must be validated.
Essential to flagship metrology; not necessarily to Lite

topics.title: Research RGB/NIR camera
tables: A separate high-sensitivity color camera with visible and near-infrared acquisition.
Records pigmentation, morphology, swarming, time-lapse behavior and NIR contrast without compromising the monochrome metrology path.
Color/phenomics and dimensional metrology have different sensor, filter and lighting priorities.
A modular color/NIR machine-vision class enables interchangeable filters and independent calibration.

topics.title: Multimode illumination
tables: Software-controlled transmitted, epi, oblique, dark-field, polarized, 940 nm NIR and fluorescence illumination.
Creates assay-specific contrast: silhouettes and ZOI edges, surface color, texture, scatter, glare suppression and reporter excitation.
No single illumination mode is robust across clear, opaque, pigmented, reflective or condensed plates.

Narrow, repeatable, strobed channels with calibration targets are preferred over uncontrolled room light. NIR may improve some condensation conditions but is not guaranteed to see through all lids or droplets.
Core visible modes essential; NIR optional; fluorescence research-only

topics.title: BME690 VOC array
tables: An array of metal-oxide gas sensors with controlled sampling, temperature profiles and a baseline channel [S10].
Produces multidimensional VOC response patterns correlated with metabolism or process state.
VOC can add orthogonal experimental information and contamination/process-change signals.
BME690 is designed for improved robustness in high-condensation environments and supports application-specific training. It is auxiliary fingerprinting, not standalone species identification.

topics.title: VL53L8CX coarse ToF
tables: Checks plate presence, approach distance, gross alignment and simple gesture/proximity events.
Low-cost position sensing can prevent motion errors and support safe handling.
It is compact and low power but spatially too coarse for colony-surface metrology.

topics.title: Research 3D profilometer
tables: A laser-triangulation, structured-light or chromatic/confocal displacement subsystem.
Measures colony height, roughness, radial topography and biofilm surface change.
Research-grade 3D claims require dense, calibrated surface measurement, not an 8x8 proximity grid.
Technique selection should follow height range, lateral resolution, reflectance and biosafety constraints; the final instrument requires traceable calibration.

topics.title: Gravimetric load cell
tables: A plate/deck mass sensor with temperature-aware calibration.
Verifies media/reagent loading, detects gross spills or dispensing errors, and trends evaporation/desiccation.
Gravimetric QC catches process failures invisible to the camera.
Load-cell class is affordable and integrable, but it must not be marketed as microgram biomass measurement in a thermally changing chamber.

topics.title: Temperature and humidity control
tables: Insulated chamber, calibrated temperature sensing, bidirectional thermal actuation and active humidity management.
Maintains validated setpoints and records excursions through the entire run.
AST and kinetic studies depend on controlled incubation; condensation and evaporation also affect imaging and media.
PT100-class sensing and independent control offer stability and auditability. Final tolerances must be verified under load and across ambient extremes.

topics.title: Gas and atmosphere control
tables: O2/CO2 sensing, regulated gas inputs, flow/pressure control and defined exhaust handling.
Creates aerobic, microaerophilic or anaerobic research atmospheres and records exposure history.
Many phenotypes are atmosphere-dependent; research reproducibility requires measured conditions.
External certified gas supply plus controlled valves/flow devices is more controllable than ad-hoc sachets, but containment and exhaust design require biosafety review.

topics.title: Integrated nephelometer
tables: A calibrated optical-scattering station with reference detector, tube ID and QC history.
Checks inoculum against the specified McFarland target before plate or MIC setup.
Excellent image analysis cannot rescue an incorrectly standardized inoculum.
A dedicated optical path and traceable reference are more defensible than estimating turbidity from a general-purpose camera.

topics.title: Direct broth microdilution module
tables: A 96-well plate deck with known concentration maps, controlled incubation and transmitted optical/kinetic reading.
Determines the lowest tested antimicrobial concentration that inhibits visible growth under the specified method.
MIC should be measured by a validated dilution workflow, not generated from zone diameter by AI [S15].
Broth microdilution is a recognized reference method class. Commercial panels/consumables, organism-drug scope and reading rules require validation.

topics.title: Robotic plate queue
tables: A 24-48 plate carousel or magazine, barcode reader, guarded transfer axis and recoverable nests.
Schedules incubation and imaging, preserves chain of custody and reduces manual handling.
The flagship must demonstrate multi-sample operation and overnight autonomy.
A constrained custom mechanism is cheaper and easier to validate than a general robot arm; capacity is a design target, not a confirmed specification.

topics.title: Purpose-built liquid handler
tables: An 8/12-channel pipetting and dispensing module optimized for serial dilution and inoculation.
Builds broth microdilution layouts, dispenses reagents and executes bounded research protocols.
Direct MIC and repeatable research require liquid-handling consistency and traceability.
A constrained module can be safer and more economical than embedding a broad third-party robot, but pipetting accuracy, carryover and contamination controls must be validated.

topics.title: Power, UPS and protective devices
tables: Medical-grade PSU class, battery backup, BMS, overcurrent/thermal protection and controlled shutdown.
Maintains safe control and data integrity through power disturbances.
Grid interruptions must not leave heaters, UV, gas valves, robotics or records in an unsafe state.
Certified components and independent cut-outs reduce integration risk; final system safety still needs testing.

topics.title: HEPA, UV-C and chamber hygiene
tables: Filtered airflow where required, cleanable surfaces, spill management and interlocked UV-C as an optional decontamination aid.
Supports contamination control and repeatable cleaning cycles.
Automated instruments need documented cleaning and cross-contamination controls.
HEPA and validated cleaning protocols address different risks. UV-C effectiveness is geometry- and dose-dependent and must be interlocked. The device is not a biosafety cabinet.

topics.title: Barcode / RFID and identity
tables: Machine-readable sample, plate, rack, reagent and consumable identification.
Binds physical items to the PIMS digital twin and prevents silent plate swaps.
Traceability is foundational to clinical, QC and multi-site workflows.
Barcode is broadly interoperable; RFID can be added for durable carriers where justified.

topics.title: Service and calibration fixtures
tables: Plate-scale dimensional artifacts, illumination references, temperature probes, turbidity references and liquid-volume checks.
Verifies drift, supports scheduled maintenance and records metrological status.
Clinical and quantitative research claims depend on known measurement performance over time.
Traceable, replaceable fixtures allow field checks without dismantling the instrument.

topics.title: Four software layers and BAHU/SaaS architecture
tables: Device drivers, deterministic control, interlocks, watchdogs, fault-state machine
BAHU HMI, PIMS, user/role controls, run orchestration, local reporting, integration gateway
Must preserve records and guided recovery if AI is unavailable
Image pipelines, measurement models, sensor fusion, research analytics, robotics planning
May degrade to manual/verified workflow; cannot bypass safety or standards rules
Multi-site fleet, remote collaboration, model registry, aggregate analytics, updates and optional advanced compute
Loss of cloud must not stop core local operation

topics.title: BAHU - Bio-Automation & Human User Interface
text: BAHU is the local operating and orchestration layer beneath the AMReye.AI brand. It gives one human-facing interface to AST, MIC, incubation, imaging, gas control, robotics, liquid handling, QC, research protocols and instrument integrations.
tables: Builds approved clinical workflows from locked steps and research workflows from permissioned modules.
Coordinates plate queues, imaging cadence, incubation windows, liquid tasks and maintenance.
Maps vendor APIs, serial devices, OPC-UA/MQTT services or file interfaces into a common command/event model.
Stops, parks or reroutes work on barcode mismatch, calibration lapse, environment excursion or robotic fault.
Shows raw evidence, boundaries, QC, rule version and uncertainty before confirm/edit/reject.
Records who did what, when, on which device/software/model/rule version.
Links protocol, samples, conditions, images, analysis and annotations to a reproducible experiment record.

topics.title: SaaS / Hive services
text: Fleet health, calibration status, software distribution and device configuration governance.
Multi-site result aggregation and role-based collaboration.
Central model registry with signed packages, staged rollout and rollback.
De-identified surveillance analytics only under appropriate governance and data-sharing agreements.
Remote support with explicit consent, session logging and least-privilege access.
tables:
SAAS IS ADDITIVE
Cloud services extend collaboration and fleet management. They are not allowed to silently change a reportable result, generate breakpoints, or make core operation dependent on a live internet connection.

topics.title: PIMS and the digital twin
text: PIMS - the Plate Information Management System - creates a physical-sample-to-digital-record chain. One record should include sample and plate identifiers, organism or assay metadata, media, antibiotic/panel map, lots, inoculum, operator, timestamps, environmental history, every image, derived measurements, QC, standards version, model version, manual edits and final disposition.
tables: Sample, plate, well, rack, device, operator
Unique IDs, barcode confirmation, duplicate detection
Raw images, exposure, light mode, sensor logs
Immutable raw objects, hashes, timestamps, calibration ID
Zone diameter, growth boundary, count, MIC endpoint
CLSI/EUCAST version, method, organism-drug mapping, footnotes
Signed structured database, effective dates, approval workflow

topics.title: CLSI/EUCAST structured standards engine
text: Breakpoints and interpretive rules must be represented as a licensed, version-controlled structured database. CLSI and EUCAST update rules and QC information; EUCAST publishes current clinical and RAST-specific tables, while CLSI emphasizes use of current standards and method-specific procedures [S12-S14].
tables: Organism/group, antimicrobial, method, specimen/workflow where relevant
Medium, inoculum, incubation, atmosphere, reading time, disk content or MIC panel
S/I/R thresholds, ATU/uncertainty areas, non-reportable combinations and exceptions
Reference strains, acceptable ranges, frequency and lot controls
Publisher, document/version, effective dates, licensed source and change record
Deterministic rule result plus human-readable explanation and exact applied rule

NON-NEGOTIABLE CORRECTION
An LLM or RAG system may retrieve and explain approved guidance, but it must not invent, infer or silently update clinical breakpoints. RAST results must use the matching RAST method, organism, antimicrobial and reading-time table - not standard overnight breakpoints [S13].

topics.title: LIMS/LIS/HIS and OEM integration
text: Order and result interfaces through laboratory-approved standards and profiles (for example HL7 v2 messaging, FHIR where appropriate, CSV/SFTP for bounded legacy workflows, and vendor APIs).
Bidirectional reconciliation: orders, sample IDs, test status, preliminary/final state, corrections and acknowledgements.
Configurable data minimization and separation of identifiable clinical records from de-identified research or surveillance data.
OEM adapter SDK with device identity, command authorization, event schema, simulation mode and conformance tests.
No unsupported claim that integration alone makes the full workflow compliant; site validation remains required.

topics.title: Human-in-the-loop clinical workflow
tables: Check identity, method, calibration and image quality
Show boundary, diameter/well endpoint and uncertainty
Apply approved rule version and QC gates
Technician confirms, edits with reason or rejects
Authorized final report, audit trail and interface acknowledgement

topics.title: Offline and edge operation
text: Core run control, image capture, measurement, locally installed standards rules, review and report generation remain available without internet. Data are queued for encrypted synchronization after connectivity returns. The system must visibly show synchronization state and prevent conflicting rule/model updates from being applied mid-run.

topics.title: Cybersecurity and software lifecycle
text: Secure boot where supported, signed software/model/rules packages, encrypted storage and TLS for external interfaces.
Role-based access, least privilege, service-mode separation and multifactor authentication for remote administration.
Software bill of materials, vulnerability monitoring, controlled patch windows and validated rollback.
Clock integrity, audit-log protection, backups, restore tests and retention policies.
Threat modeling for laboratory networks, removable media, supply chain, remote service and cross-site model distribution.

topics.title: Intended clinical capability set
text: Calibrated disk-diffusion plate imaging and zone-of-inhibition measurement.
Antibiotic-disc localization, plate-layout verification and image-quality gating.
Version-controlled CLSI/EUCAST interpretation with method and QC checks [S12-S14].
Direct quantitative MIC through validated broth microdilution workflows [S15].
Inoculum standardization via integrated nephelometry.
Incubation tracking, environmental excursion alerts and chain of custody.
Colony counting and candidate satellite/abnormal-zone flags for expert review.
Human confirmation, edit/reject pathways, audit trails and digital reporting.
LIS/LIMS/HIS connectivity and barcode-based traceability.
Method-specific rapid AST automation only where the complete workflow is validated; no blanket six-hour claim [S13].

topics.title: Research capability set
text: Time-lapse RGB phenomics and colony growth kinetics.
940 nm NIR imaging under defined plate/lid/condensation conditions.
Multi-channel fluorescence for reporter strains, dyes and experimental probes.
Morphology, pigmentation, radial growth, swarming and interaction-zone analysis.
Research-grade 3D profilometry for height, roughness and topography.
Auxiliary VOC fingerprinting using controlled BME690 sampling.
Programmable temperature, humidity, O2/CO2 and research atmospheres.
Serial dilution, liquid dispensing, multi-plate scheduling and raw-data export.
Custom models, APIs, experiment templates and reproducible digital notebooks.

topics.title: Advanced R&D features
tables: Can phenotypic time-series prioritize likely resistance mechanisms?
Research triage only; confirm with molecular/reference methods.
Can paired datasets estimate MIC distributions from zone and kinetic features?
Not a replacement for direct MIC; prospective external validation required.
Can imaging automate validated early reading windows?
Use method-specific RAST rules and permitted organism/drug/time combinations [S13].
Do VOC patterns add predictive value beyond images and conditions?
Application-specific controlled studies; no standalone species ID.
Can surface topography quantify mucoidy, biofilm or stress response?
Profilometer calibration and biological ground truth required.
Can early trajectories forecast later endpoints?
Decision support only until locked, validated and regulated for a defined use.
Can sites improve models without centralizing sensitive data?
Governance, drift control, security, consent and independent validation.
Can coordinates guide safe, traceable downstream workup?
Containment, purity, carryover and recovery validation; future robotics.

topics.title: Use Cases - What It Does, Who Uses It, and Why It Matters
text: This chapter is the operational center of the dossier. Each use case identifies the customer, problem, modules, workflow, output, value, maturity and evidence boundary. APEX XR can host all of these modules, but not every customer needs every module and not every capability is clinical.

topics.title: Concise module summary
tables: Liquid handling, BMD deck, optical reading, standards
Edge compute, local standards, sync queue

topics.title: Hospital clinical microbiology AST
tables: Hospital microbiology laboratories, diagnostic chains and qualified microbiologists.
Manual disk-diffusion reading can be variable, poorly documented and disconnected from laboratory systems.
Clinical Metrology Eye; controlled incubation; nephelometer; barcode/PIMS; structured CLSI/EUCAST engine; human review; LIS/LIMS.
Receive order and isolate -> verify inoculum -> load and image plate -> measure disk and zone boundaries -> apply current method-specific rules -> QC gate -> microbiologist review -> release.
Antimicrobial-wise measured zone, image evidence, S/I/R interpretation, rule/version, QC status, reviewer and signed report.
Standardizes acquisition and documentation, exposes the measurement boundary, and reduces repetitive manual transcription while preserving expert control.

Requires analytical performance studies across plate/media/disc/organism conditions, comparison to qualified manual/reference methods, clinical evaluation, usability, LIS validation, quality-system controls and regulatory authorization. It is not currently cleared.

topics.title: ICU and sepsis workflows
tables: ICU clinicians, microbiology laboratories, infectious-disease teams and antimicrobial-stewardship programs.
Time-critical empiric therapy needs earlier reliable susceptibility information, but conventional overnight workflows impose delay.
Priority scheduler; continuous imaging; RAST-capable protocol; PIMS; standards engine; alerting; LIS/HIS integration; human review.

Positive blood-culture workflow selected only when eligible -> execute validated direct-from-bottle RAST -> image at the permitted time -> apply RAST-specific table -> microbiologist review -> communicate preliminary/final result according to policy.
Time-stamped preliminary or final susceptibility information with method, reading time, eligible organism/drug scope and uncertainty flags.
Automation can ensure the right plate is read at the right validated window and can immediately route evidence to qualified reviewers.

No generic six-hour clinical claim. EUCAST RAST uses specific methods and time-specific breakpoints at 4, 6, 8 or 16-20 hours and is limited to validated scopes [S13]. Clinical communication policy and outcome studies are required.

topics.title: Antimicrobial stewardship
tables: Stewardship pharmacists, infectious-disease clinicians, microbiologists and hospital quality teams.
AST data may reach stewardship teams late, without clear provenance or machine-readable context.
Validated AST/MIC outputs; standards engine; resistance-pattern review flags; LIS/HIS interfaces; dashboards; audit trail.

Receive verified laboratory result -> identify policy-relevant patterns -> display organism/drug/method/rule evidence -> notify according to site-approved escalation -> document action or acknowledgement.
Traceable susceptibility result, exception flags, trend view and stewardship work queue.
Connects measurement evidence to operational review without asking an LLM to make the breakpoint or prescribe treatment.
PROPOSED SOFTWARE; clinical workflow validation required
Must not recommend patient therapy autonomously. Alert logic needs governance, local formulary context, role controls, alert-fatigue testing and clinical safety review.

topics.title: Direct MIC testing
tables: Clinical microbiology labs, research labs, pharma microbiology and reference centers.
Disk diffusion is categorical/diameter-based and does not directly determine the quantitative MIC.
Nephelometer; liquid handler; broth microdilution deck; concentration map; incubator; transmitted optical/kinetic reading; standards engine; PIMS.

Standardize inoculum -> dispense validated panel/dilutions -> inoculate -> incubate -> read growth across concentrations -> identify endpoint under the method -> apply current interpretation -> expert review.
MIC in µg/mL for the validated organism-drug-panel scope, growth image/curve, QC and method traceability.
Provides a defensible quantitative pathway based on broth microdilution rather than extrapolating MIC from zone diameter.
PROPOSED APEX - clinical and research configurations

Requires dispensing accuracy/carryover studies, panel stability, evaporation control, optical endpoint concordance, QC strains and method-specific validation against reference broth microdilution [S15].

topics.title: Teaching and academic laboratories
tables: Universities, colleges, training hospitals and laboratory-skills programs.
Students see only endpoints and receive limited objective feedback on technique, timing and measurement.
Controlled imaging; time-lapse; PIMS; instructor dashboard; plate-QC analytics; safe training protocols.
Assign exercise -> scan student/sample -> capture time zero and scheduled images -> compare streaking, growth and zone measurements -> instructor reviews -> export annotated learning record.
Time-lapse evidence, measurements, technique flags, rubric-linked report and cohort analytics.
Makes invisible incubation dynamics visible and gives instructors a reproducible record for feedback.
Training datasets and feedback rubrics must be validated for education; outputs must be labeled non-diagnostic. Biosafety supervision and institutional protocols remain mandatory.

topics.title: Research phenomics
tables: Microbiology, biotechnology, synthetic-biology and microbial-ecology researchers.
Endpoint photographs miss temporal transitions and are hard to compare across conditions.
Research RGB/NIR Eye; multimode lighting; controlled environment; plate queue; PIMS; raw export; analysis API.
Define plate map and imaging cadence -> randomize/queue plates -> acquire calibrated time series -> segment colonies/regions -> extract kinetic and morphology features -> compare conditions.
Growth curves, count/area/radial expansion, morphology/color features, images, metadata and reproducible analysis package.
Turns each plate into a structured time-series dataset and reduces manual observation burden.

Assay-specific segmentation and statistical analysis must be validated; biological replication and batch controls remain essential. Features are measurements, not automatically biological conclusions.

topics.title: Fluorescent reporter studies
tables: Synthetic-biology, gene-expression, viability and pathway researchers.
Manual fluorescence endpoints can miss transient expression and may not align with morphological change.
Research camera; excitation channels; emission filters; dark enclosure; time-lapse; plate handling; exposure calibration.

Select validated optical channel -> acquire dark/background and reference controls -> image at scheduled intervals -> correct background/bleed-through -> quantify ROI signal -> link to growth/morphology.
Fluorescence intensity/area trajectories with image evidence and acquisition metadata.
Combines reporter kinetics with visible phenotype and environment in one record.
Requires fluorophore-specific filter design, phototoxicity/bleaching studies, spectral cross-talk controls, linearity/dynamic-range validation and appropriate genetically modified organism controls.

topics.title: Heteroresistance and satellite-colony research
text: Research has shown that resistant subpopulations can be unstable and difficult to detect. An inner colony or irregular zone should prompt expert review and suitable confirmatory investigation; an image flag alone does not prove heteroresistance. Population analysis profiling was used in the cited study. [S26]
tables: AMR researchers, reference laboratories and clinical research collaborators.
Small subpopulations or colonies within inhibition zones can be missed or inconsistently recorded.
Clinical metrology; high-resolution research imaging; time-lapse; abnormal-zone detector; review interface; sample archive.

Image zone at high resolution over time -> detect candidate interior growth or changing boundaries -> track coordinates -> expert reviews -> recover/confirm with reference microbiology and molecular methods.
Candidate satellite/heterogeneous-growth map, chronology, confidence and linked confirmation status.
Preserves visual evidence and enables systematic discovery of rare spatial events.
A visual candidate is not proof of heteroresistance or a resistance mechanism. Confirmation, reproducibility, contamination exclusion and organism-specific validation are required.

topics.title: Anaerobic and microaerophilic research
tables: Anaerobe researchers, food/environmental labs and method-development teams.
Opening incubators disrupts atmosphere; growth may depend on tightly controlled O2/CO2 conditions.
Sealed Bio-Vault; gas ports; O2/CO2 sensing; flow/pressure control; internal imaging; environment logger; safety controls.
Define atmosphere profile -> purge/verify -> load compatible sealed workflow -> incubate and image without opening -> record excursions -> controlled recovery and unload.
Growth kinetics and morphology linked to measured gas, temperature and humidity history.
Enables observation without repeated atmospheric disturbance and improves experiment traceability.

Gas safety, leaks, exhaust, sensor calibration, oxygen ingress, media compatibility and biological containment require formal engineering and biosafety validation. Not a substitute for approved anaerobic systems until demonstrated.

topics.title: Biofilm and colony-morphology research
tables: Biofilm, materials, infection and microbial-ecology researchers.
Two-dimensional endpoints do not capture height, roughness, wrinkling or temporal surface development.
RGB/NIR; oblique/dark-field; optional fluorescence; research 3D profilometer; environment control; PIMS.
Set assay and surface -> acquire registered 2D/3D time points -> calibrate height and intensity -> quantify roughness/radial features -> compare treatment groups.
Topography maps, height/roughness metrics, morphology trajectories and aligned optical channels.
Unifies surface structure, color, reporter signals and environmental context.
Profilometry through lids or wet reflective surfaces may be unreliable. Technique, sterility boundary, spatial resolution and biological relevance must be established for each assay.

topics.title: Pharmaceutical QC and sterility monitoring
tables: Pharmaceutical microbiology, manufacturing QC and contract testing labs.
Manual plate reading, review and audit preparation can be labor-intensive and inconsistent across shifts/sites.
High-throughput imaging; colony counting; barcode/PIMS; role controls; audit trail; LIMS; optional fluorescence/color.
Import batch/sample plan -> track media/plates -> incubate under method -> image/read at defined points -> flag positives/outliers -> qualified analyst review -> LIMS disposition.
Count/positive-negative decision support, images, audit-ready metadata, exception log and reviewer disposition.
Standardizes documentation and can reduce manual handling while retaining method evidence.

Sterility and environmental-monitoring methods are regulated and product/site-specific. Method equivalence, detection probability, recovery, inclusivity, data integrity and electronic-record requirements must be validated. Not a universal sterility release claim.

topics.title: Environmental monitoring
tables: Cleanrooms, hospitals, manufacturing facilities and environmental microbiology teams.
Large numbers of settle/contact/air-sampling plates require traceable counts and trend review.
Plate queue; controlled imaging; colony counting; barcode/site metadata; PIMS; LIMS/dashboard.
Scan location/time/sample -> incubate by method -> image/count -> flag morphology or action-level exceedance -> reviewer confirms -> trend by zone and time.
Verified CFU count, plate image, location metadata, thresholds, deviations and trend chart.
Reduces transcription and makes every count auditable against the image.
Different media, fungi, spreading colonies and crowded plates require method-specific algorithms. Alert/action levels come from the user's approved program, not from AMR-Eye by default.

topics.title: Water and coliform workflows
tables: Municipal water labs, rural water programs, utilities and environmental testing labs.

Counts, growth kinetics, inhibition measurements where applicable, images, batch linkage and reviewer disposition.
Improves throughput, consistency and cross-shift traceability for plate-based methods.

Surveillance does not equal outbreak prediction. Requires representative sampling, harmonized methods, deduplication, privacy, data-sharing agreements, bias analysis and public-health interpretation.

topics.title: Multi-site enterprise laboratories
tables: Diagnostic chains, hospital groups, pharma/food networks and contract laboratories.

Fleet status, version compliance, QC trends, site comparisons and centralized audit evidence.
Creates a governed common operating layer while preserving local autonomy and offline continuity.
Centralization can magnify errors. Change control, site validation, data residency, access boundaries, tenant isolation and downtime procedures are mandatory.

topics.title: Custom lab automation via BAHU
tables: Research institutes, biotech startups, QC labs and technical collaborators with non-standard workflows.

Turns a bespoke hardware collection into a visible, repeatable workflow without hard-coding every experiment into the core product.
Custom workflows are not automatically validated. Adapter failures, timing, units, unsafe commands and device ownership must be addressed with conformance testing and bounded permissions.

topics.title: Remote and offline decentralized laboratories
tables: District hospitals, field/public-health labs and sites with unreliable connectivity.

Edge compute; local PIMS; cached signed standards/rules; local reports; UPS; encrypted sync queue; remote support controls.
Authenticate locally -> run full approved workflow offline -> issue local reviewed report -> queue de-identified/authorized data -> sync and reconcile when connected.
Local result and audit record, visible sync status, conflict log and later fleet update.
Preserves essential operation and traceability without treating internet access as a laboratory prerequisite.
Local rule/model currency, clock accuracy, backup, service logistics and delayed central reconciliation require explicit procedures. Offline capability does not relax clinical validation.

topics.title: OEM and instrument integration
tables: Instrument manufacturers, automation integrators, incubator vendors, LIMS providers and consumables partners.

BAHU adapter SDK; API gateway; device identity; event schema; PIMS; simulator; conformance tests.

Interoperable workflow node, traceable device events and partner-specific configuration package.
Lets AMR-Eye become an orchestration layer and modular platform instead of requiring every component to be built in-house.

Commercial agreements, cybersecurity, liability, interface stability, service ownership and joint validation are required. Integration does not transfer one device's regulatory status to the combined system.

topics.title: Competitor and benchmark context
text: APEX XR should be presented as a differentiated product strategy, not as a claim that no comparable capabilities exist. The market already demonstrates digital incubation, AI image analysis, quantitative AST and full laboratory automation.
tables: Smart incubation, continuous high-resolution imaging, colony counting, growth kinetics, fluorescence, inhibition-zone analysis and high-throughput QC [S19].
Differentiate through AMR/AST-first workflow, direct MIC, structured clinical rules, edge/offline operation and modular Indian/decentralized deployment goals. These are design goals until proven.
Integrated ID/AST, quantitative MIC-oriented workflows and maintained interpretation systems [S16].
Treat VITEK as the clinical workflow benchmark; do not imply APEX currently matches its validation, installed base or menu.
Automated ID/AST panels and susceptibility results used for clinical decisions [S17].
Use direct microdilution-style quantitative testing rather than claiming AI-derived exact MIC from disk zones.
End-to-end specimen processing, smart incubation, imaging, AI-assisted review, colony selection and AST preparation [S18].
Keep APEX robotics constrained and modular; position BAHU as an integration/orchestration architecture rather than claiming immediate full-lab automation.

DEFENSIBLE DIFFERENTIATION
AMR-Eye's credible differentiation is a combination of AST specialization, modular scope, edge/offline operation, traceable standards execution, integrated direct MIC, multimodal research options and cost-oriented deployment - not the generic use of AI to image plates.

topics.title: Competitive claim rules

topics.title: Regulatory statement
text: The intended clinical configuration is expected to fall within India's IVD regulatory framework. CDSCO states that IVD manufacture/import/clinical performance/sale are governed by the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, and classification depends on intended purpose and risk [S20]. A current CDSCO list includes an identification and antibiotic-susceptibility analyser entry, but the final classification of AMReye.AI - including software, accessories, claims and combined configurations - must be formally determined with regulatory counsel and the competent authority. The older project assertion of a fixed 'Class B' pathway should not be repeated as fact.
Freeze the intended-use statement before classification strategy.
Separate research-use-only modules from any clinical configuration and labeling.
Establish design controls, risk management, software lifecycle, usability, cybersecurity, supplier control and post-market planning under the applicable quality framework.
Treat clinical, research and OEM configurations as potentially different regulatory systems, not one universal approval.

RECOMMENDED FLAGSHIP DECISION

topics.title: RTOS and independent embedded control
text: The proposed STM32 control layer runs time-sensitive hardware tasks independently of the operator interface and AI computer. FreeRTOS is an RTOS for microcontrollers; its presence alone does not establish that an AMReye.AI controller is deterministic or safe. The project must define and test its own deadlines, priorities and fault responses. [S21][S22][S24]

Separate acquisition timing, thermal control, interlock monitoring and communications into bounded tasks. Use explicit state transitions, short interrupt handlers and traceable command acknowledgements. Slow image inference, cloud sync and interface rendering must not block essential hardware responses.

Required evidence includes measured worst-case latency, scheduling traces under load, sensor disconnect tests, power-cycle recovery and an independent review of the hazard controls. Historical claims of sub-microsecond loops or guaranteed safety are not established performance results.

topics.title: Watchdogs, interlocks and fault-state recovery
text: A proposed fault model should distinguish startup checks, ready state, active acquisition, paused operation, recoverable faults and a latched safe state. Every transition needs a cause, timestamp and recovery condition. [S21][S22]

Watchdog supervision should detect stalled critical tasks rather than merely proving that a low-priority loop still runs. Over-temperature, invalid sensor readings, door events and motion faults need defined safe responses. Critical interlocks should not depend only on the touchscreen or cloud connection.

A recovery test should show what happens to heaters, lighting, moving axes and incomplete records after communication loss or reset. Operator acknowledgement should not silently clear an unresolved hazard. These are design requirements, not completed certification.

topics.title: Multi-plate camera gantry concept
text: The September group discussion describes one camera moving above multiple plates on an interval schedule, with the incubation region centrally located and electronics below. This is a separate research configuration from the earlier single-plate enclosure drawings. [S27][S28]

A proposed XY carriage would associate each tray position with a registered plate ID and repeatable imaging pose. Design work includes homing, collision limits, cable routing, positional repeatability, exposure timing and condensation management. Acquisition should occur only after motion settles.

Validation must measure image-scale changes across the travel range, focus variation, vibration and registration errors. A multi-plate layout increases capacity only if incubation uniformity, optical calibration and scheduling remain acceptable. No throughput or cost target is confirmed.

topics.title: Decontamination concept and UV safety boundaries
text: The group discussion proposes an optional post-run internal UV cycle with interruption when the access door opens. This is an unvalidated decontamination concept. An illuminated chamber is not evidence of effective sterilisation. [S27]

Any development must evaluate enclosure leakage, material compatibility, shadowing, exposure measurement and organism-specific efficacy with qualified safety oversight. Door protection needs an independently assessed fail-safe design. Biological material handling remains governed by laboratory procedures.

The public website does not operate a UV source and provides no validated cycle or dose. A proposed software cycle should never imply that contamination, operator exposure or waste-management obligations have been eliminated.

topics.title: Open hardware, software licensing and commercial services
text: The group discussion supports an accessible, buildable hardware pathway and service-based software or AI revenue. Earlier proposals also discuss open hardware and research access. These are intended models, not proof that design files or code have already been released under a licence. [S21][S27]

Before publication, identify ownership of schematics, firmware, datasets and model weights. Choose licences deliberately, document third-party obligations and provide a versioned bill of materials and build instructions. Avoid describing every CERN-OHL variant as permissive.

Commercial value could come from integration, managed services, deployment support and validated releases. Research or nonprofit access rules, usage billing and support scope remain decisions for the team. The website has no checkout and quotes no final tariff.

topics.title: Educational and public-health access model
text: The project aims to improve access for teaching institutions, nonprofit users and resource-constrained laboratories. The group discussion proposes affordability through local construction, modular scope and potential public-health partnerships. [S27]

An access plan should separate equipment ownership, consumables, calibration, training, connectivity, repair and ongoing software support. A low purchase price is not the same as a sustainable service.

Free provision through government hospitals would require a funded programme and institutional agreement. It is an aspiration, not an existing entitlement, subsidy or government commitment. Use pilot evidence to compare total operating costs and availability.

topics.title: Web app, offline reader and instrument application
text: The public website is the discovery and documentation layer. A browser-based app can present the same content, while an installed instrument application would need controlled releases, local data handling, hardware interfaces and its own validation. [S27]

This release includes a lightweight offline reader for the consolidated library. It contains reference text, search and source links. External references still require connectivity; its material is a dated snapshot. The full instrument controls shown elsewhere remain simulations.

For a future instrument, define signed update packages, compatibility checks, rollback, backup and an audit trail. Multiple websites alone do not provide secure device updates. One canonical repository with stable topic IDs reduces conflicting copies.

topics.title: Goa diagnostic capacity and public-spending research framework
text: The team's proposed study asks whether public-health investment supports the diagnostic capacity required for AMR preparedness. It connects microbiology requirements, laboratory availability, public spending and implementation feasibility. This page states a research framework, not the findings of a completed CAG audit. [S27]

Build a source table recording the institution, financial year, audit report, page, observation, response and relevance to diagnostics. Keep sanctioned expenditure, actual spending, available equipment, functioning equipment and services delivered distinct.

Compare potential interventions against measured bottlenecks such as downtime, staffing, sample transport, quality assurance and reporting delay. Do not infer that buying AMReye.AI would resolve an audit observation without a pilot and costed implementation plan.

topics.title: Bacterial-outbreak preparedness scenarios
text: COVID demonstrates the importance of diagnostic capacity and coordinated information, but AMReye.AI's current AST direction does not diagnose or solve a viral outbreak. The defensible counterfactual concerns future bacterial or AMR events and the availability of validated microbiology infrastructure. [S27]

Model explicit assumptions: participating laboratories, staffed operating hours, eligible samples, processing capacity, failure rates and reporting delays. Compare a baseline workflow with a proposed intervention and show sensitivity ranges.

Time or resource differences in such a scenario are planning outputs, not measured savings or lives saved. The scenario explorer uses user-adjustable hypothetical inputs and makes no epidemiological forecast.

topics.title: Growth patterns, phenomics and identity limits
text: The original idea began with image-based zone measurement and expanded toward time-resolved observation of bacterial and fungal growth. Imaging can create reproducible phenotypic features, but appearance alone does not establish strain identity, genotype, protein expression or clinical susceptibility. [S21][S22][S27]

Research datasets should retain organism labels from qualified reference methods, media, incubation conditions, optics and experiment identifiers. Separate colony counting, growth-curve estimation and exploratory phenotype association as different model tasks.

A claim about proteins or metabolites needs an appropriate validated assay and reference measurement. VOC or optical signals should be described as auxiliary observations until their specificity and robustness are established.

topics.title: Model evaluation and dataset governance
text: Treat each model as a separate evidence object: intended task, input format, training provenance, test protocol, performance bounds and review workflow. A plate-segmentation model is not automatically a strain or protein model. [S21]

Split validation by laboratory, instrument, acquisition date or biological batch where appropriate to avoid related samples leaking across train and test sets. Record calibration and image-quality exclusions. Study hard cases, including overlapping zones and inner colonies.

Publish uncertainty and failure analysis alongside aggregate metrics. Human adjustments need traceability, and a revised model should be checked before release. Website demonstrations do not establish these evaluation results.

topics.title: From laboratory records to governed surveillance
text: WHO GLASS provides a framework for AMR surveillance and its data requirements. Any AMReye.AI connection to a national programme would need agreed definitions, laboratory quality processes and responsible reporting. It is not an existing GLASS integration. [S25]

A proposed pipeline should distinguish patient episodes, isolates, susceptibility records, duplicates and missing tests. Regional summaries need denominators and sampling context. Maps cannot be interpreted as representative population prevalence without an appropriate design.

Define local ownership, access, retention, de-identification and permitted aggregation before sharing. Cross-border deployment also needs country-specific agreements and validation. The website's map is an illustration.

Implemented website simulation: the #network explorer provides India and global SVG views, equivalent selectable region lists, organism/antibiotic/period filters and fixed invented counts. Percentages are calculated from resistant and tested examples; empty selections explicitly show no example data. This is not live surveillance, prevalence evidence or a programme integration. Filters stay in the browser session only.

topics.title: Project history and source reconciliation
text: The repository contains multiple generations: the early single-plate image-analysis idea, the three-zone enclosure, the expanded technical manual, the APEX XR flagship dossier and the later multi-plate gantry and public-health discussions. They should remain dated alternatives rather than being silently combined into one manufactured device. [S21][S22][S27][S28]

The supplied enclosure drawings show different component placements and title-block details. Dimensions, screen size, equipment labels, dates and engineer names embedded in the images have not been verified as fabrication specifications or authorship records.

The full original dossier remains available. New notes clarify maturity and add source provenance. Similar filenames are not sufficient evidence of duplication, and a PDF companion is not necessarily redundant with its editable source.

topics.title: Validation mode and correction provenance
text: The September master specifies a proposed Validation Mode that compares a reference result with an AMReye.AI measurement. Each record should retain method, organism, antimicrobial, disc potency where relevant, standards version, category comparison, disagreement classification and reviewer decisions. This is a software roadmap requirement, not an existing validated instrument feature. [S29][S31]

Dimensional measurement error and repeatability should be assessed separately from microbiological category agreement and clinical utility. The project calls for disagreement analysis, including major and very major errors where applicable, rather than treating computer-vision detection metrics as clinical accuracy. [S29]

A correction record should preserve the original automated value, the corrected value, reviewer identity, timestamp and override reason. The earlier website demonstration provided editable synthetic measurements and a session audit, but has no authenticated reviewer or clinical validation dataset. [S29]

Implemented website simulation: Validation comparison uses an independent, immutable synthetic fixture (CIP 24, AMC 23, MEM 28, GEN 18, SXT 26 and AMP 14 mm). It compares original and effective values with the reference and shows signed difference, mean difference, mean absolute difference and fictional category agreement. These are teaching comparisons, not clinical accuracy. Corrections require an explicit apply action and reason; successive events retain timestamps and a clearly labelled demo reviewer. Immutable report snapshots keep print, JSON and CSV consistent. No authenticated reviewer, clinical dataset or validated instrument capability is provided.

topics.title: Unreadable images, review and recapture
text: The proposed pipeline must be able to abstain when image quality, growth, condensation, plate geometry or inhibition-zone boundaries are unsuitable. The master defines NOT READABLE, REVIEW and RECAPTURE outcomes so a system is not forced to produce a measurement or susceptibility call. [S29]

A future workflow should retain the source image and the reason for abstention, direct the operator to the appropriate review or recapture step, and prevent an unsuitable image from progressing as an accepted result. Qualified method-specific review remains necessary. [S29][S31]

The earlier website offered clean, overlapping-boundary and fuzzy-margin synthetic examples. Those scenarios explain review requirements; they do not establish real image-quality detection or an implemented abstention model. [S29]

Implemented website simulation: clean, overlapping, fuzzy and unreadable examples now explain review and recapture. The unreadable scenario produces no measurements, interpretations or approvals, while allowing an incomplete report. Changing scenarios cancels processing and requires another run. Rule-profile changes preserve measurements and correction history while clearing approvals. This is an invented scenario workflow, not real image-quality detection or an instrument abstention model.

topics.title: Bio-Vault and APEX XR: separate configuration studies
text: The September master describes a proposed three-zone Bio-Vault arrangement with Jetson Orin NX, Raspberry Pi 5 and BME688. The earlier APEX XR dossier explores a larger flagship architecture including Thor/T5000 and BME690. These are alternative configuration studies, not one final bill of materials or a confirmed manufactured instrument. [S29][S21]

Keep the imaging chamber, operator interface, power and thermal requirements associated with the source configuration. Component substitutions require their own interface, thermal, cost and validation review. The original drawings remain concept references. [S28][S29]

Product names, tiers, dimensions and component choices remain provisional. The first instrument should be chosen against a defined intended use and measured requirements; advanced research modules retain separate development and evidence gates. [S29][S31]

topics.title: Reader V1: endpoint disk-diffusion reading
text: The present priority is an endpoint reader: a calibrated plate image, visible zone measurement, quality checks, uncertainty and qualified review. Broader instrument and assay capabilities remain separate proposals.

topics.title: Campus and laboratory audit collaboration
text: A proposed collaboration starts with equipment and workflow mapping, operator interviews, bottlenecks, training, data permissions and a scoped pilot. Agree the owner, deliverables, budget and acceptance criteria before work begins. No campus partnership is claimed as signed.

topics.title: Cell-culture workflow research
text: Explore record keeping, imaging review and workflow traceability for cell culture as a separate research direction. Requirements for cell lines, containment, imaging, quality controls and qualified supervision need independent definition. No automated culture capability is claimed.

topics.title: Stem-cell research workflows
text: Stem-cell work is a future research direction, not a current product capability or therapeutic service. Any collaboration needs an intended research question, appropriate approvals, qualified facilities and independent methods for identity and quality assessment.

topics.title: Organoid and tissue-model research
text: Organoids and tissue models are potential future research contexts. Define the biological model, authorized data, relevant measurements and independent validation before selecting hardware or making performance claims.

topics.title: UTI and urine-culture workflow research
text: A possible application is a bounded urine-culture laboratory workflow with validated plate reading and reviewable AST. It does not imply diagnosis directly from an unprocessed specimen or autonomous treatment advice.

topics.title: MRSA and molecular-result integration
text: Study how authorized results from qualified molecular instruments could complement phenotype records. Real-time PCR and reverse-transcription PCR are different methods; the intended method remains to be specified. No resistance gene is inferred from a plate image.

topics.title: Bioinformatics and phenotype–genotype research
text: Use traceable identifiers and versioned reference resources to study authorized phenotype and molecular data. Keep measured genotypes distinct from image-based hypotheses and computational predictions.

topics.title: Measured, derived, imputed and simulated data
text: Every plate value needs an origin label, unit, timestamp, uncertainty and quality state where applicable. A blank channel stays unavailable. Derived or imputed information must not silently become a direct measurement.

topics.title: Interoperability, APIs and audit trails
text: An interface needs a defined data contract, identity mapping, authorization, version handling and acceptance tests. Standards names and API availability do not mean a working hospital integration exists.

topics.title: System as a Service delivery model
text: Explore equipment access with maintenance, calibration, training and support as a service package. Keep it distinct from the software subscription, and validate customer demand, operating costs and contract terms before offering it commercially.

topics.title: Privacy and access governance
text: Keep public explanations separate from protected technical and partner material. Any real laboratory data would need appropriate rights, permissions, retention rules and a documented governance model before use.

topics.title: Automation vocabulary with practical meaning
text: Digital twin means a traceable record with clearly labelled data origins. Edge AI means processing close to the instrument. Human-in-the-loop means qualified review. Robotics, sensor fusion, multimodal AI, organoids and lab orchestration are research directions unless supported by specific completed evidence.
